coda-ai.value: Coda AI drafts, summarises and fills tables inside Coda's doc and table hybrid, and Grammarly acquired Coda in 2024, folding it into the Superhuman productivity suite. The product continues with AI across docs and connected data.
coda-ai.status: Active. Acquired by Grammarly, part of Superhuman.
coda-ai.tagline: AI in Coda docs for writing, summarising and table automation, with Coda now part of Grammarly's Superhuman.
coda-ai.governance_note: Enterprise terms via Grammarly; confirm after the acquisition.
coda-ai.training_optout: Coda does not train on customer data; confirm under Grammarly.

cognigy.name: Cognigy
cognigy.value: Cognigy builds voice and chat agents for customer service with a low code designer, agentic AI and deep contact centre integrations, and NICE bought it to anchor its CXone platform. European data residency and GDPR tooling are part of its appeal.
cognigy.tagline: German conversational AI platform for contact centre agents, acquired by NICE in 2025.
cognigy.governance_note: EU residency and GDPR tooling; disclose AI agents to callers where required.
cognigy.training_optout: Cognigy does not train on customer data.

copy-ai.name: Copy.ai
copy-ai.value: Copy.ai moved from short form copy to a GTM AI platform where teams build workflows that research accounts, draft outreach and produce content with any model. It competes with Jasper on the marketing side and with Clay on the sales side.
copy-ai.tagline: Copywriting tool turned go to market workflow platform, automating content, sales research and outreach.
copy-ai.governance_note: Outreach workflows send email in your name; keep human approval on anything outbound.
copy-ai.training_optout: Copy.ai states customer data is not used for training; confirm.

dataiku.name: Dataiku
dataiku.value: Dataiku lets mixed teams build data pipelines, models and LLM applications in one governed environment, with an LLM mesh that routes to any model with cost and safety controls. It is favoured by large enterprises for governed AI at scale.
dataiku.engine: Any model via the LLM mesh.
dataiku.tagline: Enterprise platform for data science, ML and generative AI applications with governance built in.
dataiku.governance_note: The LLM mesh centralises which models are allowed, with PII screening and cost tracking, which is what an AI policy needs enforced.
dataiku.training_optout: Dataiku does not train on customer data.

decagon.name: Decagon
decagon.value: Decagon deploys support agents across chat, email and voice with an agent operating procedure model that lets teams write policies in plain language, and reports high resolution rates for its enterprise customers. It is Sierra's closest rival.
decagon.engine: Multiple frontier models with Decagon's orchestration.
decagon.tagline: Customer support agents with a focus on measurable resolution and a fast growing enterprise base.
decagon.governance_note: Same action limits and audit as Sierra.
decagon.training_optout: Decagon does not train on customer data.

elai-io.name: Elai.io
elai-io.value: Elai is a smaller avatar video platform that turns blog posts, scripts or presentations into presenter videos with multilingual voices and custom avatars. It competes on price and the URL to video feature against the larger names.
elai-io.engine: Elai's avatars with partner voice models.
elai-io.tagline: Avatar video generation from text or a URL, aimed at marketing and training teams on a budget.
elai-io.governance_note: Same avatar consent and labelling rules as the category. Smaller vendor means the vendor review should check financial stability and data location.

epic-ai.api: Epic FHIR API for external integration; AI features are embedded in the EHR workflow.
cons: FDA regulatory requirements apply to clinical decision-support AI
Population-level validation required before clinical reliance
Locked into Epic's development and update timeline
epic-ai.name: Epic AI (SlicerDicer, etc.)
pros: Embedded in the EHR clinicians already use, no workflow change required
Scale of patient data behind Epic's model training
epic-ai.files: Patient records, clinical notes, and structured EHR data.
epic-ai.value: AI capabilities across Epic's electronic health record, including clinical decision support, ambient documentation (ambient listening that drafts clinical notes), and analytics via SlicerDicer and a range of prediction models. Used by over 350 million patient records' worth of institutions.
epic-ai.engine: Epic's own models and Microsoft Azure AI Services, under Epic's development and validation processes.
epic-ai.latency: Real-time for clinical decision support; batch for analytics.

pricing.model: Within Epic contract, some AI features additional
pricing.includes: Base AI features; ambient documentation is priced separately

epic-ai.quality: Quality is the sector's primary compliance question, not speed. Clinical AI models must be validated on the deployment population before clinical reliance, which is a regulatory requirement in addition to good practice.
epic-ai.tagline: AI across the EHR used by most major US health systems, with regulatory requirements that differ from any other sector.
use_cases: Ambient clinical documentation reducing physician administrative burden
Predictive risk scoring for sepsis, readmission, and care escalation
Population health analytics via SlicerDicer across the patient panel
integrations: Azure AI Services for model execution
HL7 FHIR for external data exchange
epic-ai.governance_note: Healthcare AI operates under a regulatory framework that is categorically different from general enterprise AI: FDA oversight of Software as a Medical Device applies to clinical AI tools that are decision-support for diagnosis or treatment, HIPAA governs all patient data handling, and validation on the deployment population is both a regulatory expectation and a patient safety requirement. The EU AI Act classifies AI used in clinical contexts as high-risk. Before any Epic AI feature is enabled in a clinical setting, the governance question is whether the feature constitutes a SaMD and whether the appropriate validation has been performed. See the healthcare pages in the reference library.
epic-ai.training_optout: Epic's health data terms apply and are structured around HIPAA requirements. Data stays within the health system's Epic environment.

flowise.api: Yes. Each flow exposes a prediction endpoint.
cons: Less polished than Dify for production operations
flowise.name: Flowise
pros: Apache licence with no resale conditions
Embeddable chat widget out of the box
flowise.value: Flowise is the lighter weight cousin of Dify: a node based canvas for chaining models, retrievers, memory and tools, exported as an API or embeddable chat widget. It is popular with teams that want to see the chain and change it without reading code.
flowise.engine: Any model provider; built on LangChain and LlamaIndex components.
flowise.quality: Good for prototypes; production needs monitoring you add yourself.
flowise.tagline: Drag and drop builder for LLM flows and agents, open source and self hostable.
use_cases: Website chatbots over a document set
Teaching how LLM chains fit together
flowise.governance_note: Same self hosting logic as Dify with a cleaner licence. Every node that calls an external service is a data transfer; the canvas makes those visible, which is a governance advantage of visual builders.
flowise.training_optout: Self hosted, nothing leaves except model calls under each vendor's terms.

glm-zai.name: GLM / Z.AI
glm-zai.value: Zhipu, spun out of Tsinghua, releases GLM open weights that compete at the top of open benchmarks for coding and agent tasks, and sells an API internationally as Z.AI with low prices. It was placed on the US entity list in 2025, which affects some buyers.
glm-zai.tagline: Zhipu's GLM models, among the strongest open releases for agents and coding, sold internationally under the Z.AI brand.
glm-zai.governance_note: Entity list status restricts US exports to Zhipu, not use of its open weights, but procurement teams in government and defence supply chains should check policy.

cons: Most regulated AI tool in the HR category
Jurisdictional compliance checklist is mandatory before deployment
Adverse impact questions are not resolved
hirevue.name: HireVue
pros: Structured, documented scoring reduces unstructured interview variance
Scales initial screening across high-volume hiring
Bias audit tooling is more mature than most HR AI tools
hirevue.files: Video interview recordings and game assessment responses.
hirevue.value: Automated video interview analysis and game-based assessments for high-volume hiring. Reduces recruiter time on initial screening and provides structured, documented scoring. The governance burden is proportional to the volume of hiring decisions it touches.
hirevue.engine: Computer vision, NLP, and IO psychology-grounded assessment models for interview analysis.
hirevue.latency: Analysis completes after the interview, not in real time.
hirevue.quality: Structured consistency is the proposition. The fairness and adverse impact questions are ongoing in both research and regulation, and are not resolved by any vendor.
hirevue.tagline: Video interview and assessment AI, and the focus of more AI employment regulation than any other HR tool.
use_cases: High-volume first-round screening without live recruiter time
Structured scoring across a large candidate pool with documented rationale
Reducing unstructured interview variance in hiring decisions
integrations: Major ATS platforms (Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Taleo)
Background screening and offer management systems
hirevue.governance_note: The most regulated AI tool in the HR category, by a significant margin. NYC Local Law 144 requires a bias audit before deployment in New York City and candidate notification. Illinois requires disclosure of AI use in video interviews. The EU AI Act classifies AI used in employment decisions as high-risk under Annex III. Several US states are moving on similar rules. The compliance checklist before deployment is jurisdictional-law-first, not vendor-capabilities-first: know which rules apply to your hiring locations, complete required audits, and establish candidate disclosure before turning it on. See the employment law pages in the reference library.
hirevue.training_optout: Candidate data terms require explicit legal review. This is regulated data in multiple jurisdictions.

hunyuan.name: Hunyuan
hunyuan.value: Hunyuan powers Tencent's products including WeChat features and its cloud, and its open releases in video generation and 3D asset creation drew global developer interest. The LLM line is competitive in China; the generative media models are its international calling card.
hunyuan.tagline: Tencent's model family, notable for open video and 3D generation models alongside its LLMs.
hunyuan.governance_note: Read the community licence; some releases exclude EU, UK and South Korean territories from use.

i-ready.name: i-Ready
i-ready.value: i-Ready's adaptive diagnostic places students and assigns personalised lessons, with teacher reports used for grouping and intervention, deployed in a large share of US districts. Its AI is adaptive assessment and recommendation rather than generative.
i-ready.tagline: Diagnostic assessment and personalised instruction in reading and math, one of the most used K8 platforms in the US.
i-ready.governance_note: High stakes use of adaptive scores for placement should be reviewed for fairness; the vendor publishes validity research.

cons: Stock licensing limits on some plans
invideo.name: InVideo
invideo.value: InVideo AI produces complete videos from a prompt, writing the script, choosing stock or generated footage and adding voiceover, then letting you edit by typing instructions. It is built for faceless marketing and explainer content at volume.
invideo.engine: InVideo's orchestration over licensed LLM, voice and video models.
invideo.tagline: Text to video for marketers: describe a video and get a script, stock footage, voiceover and generated clips assembled.
invideo.governance_note: Check the stock licence on your plan before commercial use; some tiers restrict it.

knowbe4.name: KnowBe4
knowbe4.value: KnowBe4 trains employees to recognise phishing and social engineering, runs simulated attacks and uses AI to tailor campaigns to each user's behaviour and to flag AI written phishing in its email security product. It appears in the education catalog because schools buy it for staff training.
knowbe4.engine: KnowBe4's own models with partner LLMs.

pricing.includes: Training, phishing, AI features by tier

knowbe4.tagline: Security awareness training and simulated phishing, with AI that personalises training and detects AI generated attacks.
knowbe4.governance_note: Simulated phishing of staff should be disclosed in policy; AI generated lures must stay within what the organisation would accept from a real attacker test.
knowbe4.training_optout: KnowBe4 does not train on customer content; confirm.

kore-ai.name: Kore.ai
kore-ai.value: Kore.ai builds enterprise agents for contact centres, HR and IT help and enterprise search on a platform with guardrails, analytics and deployment on any cloud, and ranks at the top of analyst reports for conversational AI. It competes with Cognigy, Aisera and the hyperscalers.
kore-ai.engine: Any model with Kore's orchestration and guardrails.
kore-ai.tagline: Enterprise conversational and agent platform for customer service, employee help and search, with strong governance tooling.
kore-ai.governance_note: Built for regulated contact centres: PII masking, audit logs, human escalation. Configure disclosure that the agent is AI where required.
kore-ai.training_optout: Kore.ai does not train on customer data.

krea-ai.name: Krea AI
krea-ai.value: Krea gives creators one interface over many models, Flux, Kling, Veo, Runway and others, plus its own real time canvas, upscaler and video enhancer. It is where designers compare models and finish outputs without separate subscriptions.
krea-ai.engine: Aggregated third party models plus Krea's own real time and enhancement models.
krea-ai.quality: As good as the model chosen.
krea-ai.tagline: A creative studio that aggregates the leading image and video models with real time generation and enhancement tools.
use_cases: Comparing video models for a brief
krea-ai.governance_note: An aggregator routes your inputs to whichever vendor runs the model, including Chinese vendors for some video models; know which model processed which asset before using it commercially.
krea-ai.training_optout: Varies by underlying model; confirm per model.

cons: Features overlap with Teams and Zoom clips
loom-ai.name: Loom AI
loom-ai.value: Loom records your screen and camera and its AI writes the title, summary and chapters, removes filler words and silences, and translates captions. Atlassian bought it in 2023 and ties it to Jira and Confluence.
loom-ai.engine: Loom's licensed speech and summarisation models.
loom-ai.tagline: Screen recording with AI titles, summaries, chapters and filler removal, now part of Atlassian.
loom-ai.governance_note: Recordings often contain screens with customer data; set workspace sharing defaults to private and retention rules in the admin console.
loom-ai.training_optout: Atlassian terms exclude training on customer content.

lovable.api: No. The product is the chat interface.
cons: Generated apps have shipped with exposed databases and weak auth rules
Credit pricing can run away during iteration
Debugging past a point needs a developer
lovable.name: Lovable
pros: Fastest path from idea to a working app for a non developer
Clean exit to GitHub when you outgrow it
Supabase integration gives real data and auth
lovable.files: Images and design references; the code lives in GitHub.
lovable.value: Lovable turned a prompt into a deployed full stack app, with Supabase for the backend and GitHub for the code, and grew faster than almost any software company before it. It is the reference product for the vibe coding wave: non developers shipping real software, with the security consequences that follow.
lovable.engine: Frontier models from several vendors orchestrated by Lovable's own agent.
lovable.latency: Minutes per change, which is the right expectation for a builder agent.

pricing.includes: Private projects, custom domains, more credits

lovable.quality: Impressive for a first version; security and edge cases are where generated apps have failed in public.
lovable.tagline: Describe an app in plain language and get a working web app with a database and auth.
use_cases: Prototyping a product idea in an afternoon
Internal tools for a small team
lovable.governance_note: The risk is not the tool, it is the owner who does not know what a row level security policy is. Any Lovable app that holds customer data needs a developer or a security review before launch, and the public incidents of 2025 are the case study.
lovable.training_optout: Lovable's terms cover use of prompts and projects; private projects on paid tiers are not public. Confirm current terms before putting proprietary logic in.

make-ai.api: Yes. Scenario management and webhook triggers.
cons: Operations based pricing punishes chatty flows
Complex scenarios become hard to read
make-ai.name: Make (Integromat) AI
pros: More expressive than Zapier for branching and data work
Agents add judgement to fixed scenarios
make-ai.files: Anything a module returns; binary handling supported.
make-ai.value: Make, once Integromat, is the visual automation platform between Zapier's simplicity and n8n's engineering depth, with a scenario canvas, data transformation tools and now AI agents that can decide which scenario to run. Operations teams use it for the integrations that Zapier cannot express.
make-ai.engine: Any model through its AI modules and agents; OpenAI and others as connectors.
make-ai.latency: Scenario dependent; near real time on webhook triggers.
make-ai.quality: Reliable platform; AI steps are as good as the model and prompt.
make-ai.tagline: Visual automation with thousands of app modules and AI agents that act inside the scenarios.
use_cases: Multi step integrations across SaaS tools
AI enrichment inside a data pipeline
Agents that route work between scenarios
integrations: OpenAI, Anthropic and other AI modules
make-ai.governance_note: Same rule as every automation hub: it holds credentials for many systems, so least privilege connections, an audit log and a human approval step before irreversible actions. Cloud only means the data path runs through Make's infrastructure.
make-ai.training_optout: Make does not train on customer data; AI module calls follow each provider's terms. Confirm in the current terms.

minimax.name: MiniMax
minimax.value: MiniMax covers text, speech, music and video: open MiniMax M series LLMs with very long context, the Hailuo video service, speech models and consumer apps including Talkie. It went public in Hong Kong in 2026 and is one of the most commercially broad Chinese labs.
minimax.tagline: Shanghai lab behind Hailuo video, open long context LLMs and the Talkie companion app, listed in Hong Kong in 2026.
minimax.governance_note: Same rule as other Chinese labs: open weights local, API hosted in China.

miro-ai.name: Miro AI
miro-ai.value: Miro's AI clusters and summarises workshop output, drafts diagrams and flowcharts from prompts, generates prototypes and turns a board into a document or presentation. It makes the whiteboard the start of deliverables rather than a photo of sticky notes.
miro-ai.engine: Partner models including OpenAI and Anthropic.
miro-ai.tagline: AI on the collaborative whiteboard: summarise sticky notes, generate diagrams and turn boards into documents.
miro-ai.governance_note: Enterprise admins can disable AI and choose data residency; workshop boards often hold confidential strategy, so set the controls.
miro-ai.training_optout: Miro states customer content is not used to train models; confirm.

murf-ai.name: Murf.ai
murf-ai.value: Murf produces voiceovers for training, ads and product content with hundreds of voices, pronunciation controls, a video sync editor and cloning on business tiers. It is the mid market studio between ElevenLabs and the cheaper consumer tools.
murf-ai.tagline: Text to speech studio with a large voice library, voice cloning and an API for product voices.
murf-ai.governance_note: Voice cloning needs documented consent; Murf's process requires it, and your policy should cover use after an employee leaves.
murf-ai.training_optout: Murf states customer data is not used for training; confirm.

newsela.name: Newsela
newsela.value: Newsela publishes current articles rewritten at multiple reading levels with quizzes and writing prompts, aligned to standards, and owns Formative for assessment. Its levelling has historically been done by human editors, with AI used in tooling and assessment rather than the core content.
newsela.engine: Human editorial levelling with AI tooling.
newsela.status: Active. AI claim is modest; flagged for vendor check.
newsela.tagline: Leveled news and nonfiction articles for classrooms, with each article rewritten at five reading levels and assessments attached.
newsela.governance_note: Flagged on the unverified list: the product's AI is in tooling and assessment, not in generating the articles. Describe it as a content platform with AI features.

okta-ai.name: Okta AI
okta-ai.value: Okta applies AI to detect anomalous logins and recommend access policies, and extended identity to AI agents so they get credentials, permissions and lifecycle like humans. Agent identity is the piece every governance programme now needs.
okta-ai.engine: Okta's detection models with partner LLMs.
okta-ai.tagline: AI in Okta's identity platform for threat detection, policy recommendations and identity for AI agents.
use_cases: Securing AI agents with managed identities
okta-ai.governance_note: Every agent that acts in your systems should have an identity with scoped permissions and an owner; Okta is one way to enforce that.
okta-ai.training_optout: Okta does not train on customer data.

pictory.name: Pictory
pictory.value: Pictory is the article to video and script to video tool for content marketers, choosing stock clips per sentence and adding voiceover and captions. It also summarises long videos into highlights.
pictory.tagline: Turns scripts, blog posts and long videos into short videos with stock footage and captions.
pictory.governance_note: Stock licence scope and voice usage rights belong in the asset record.

play-ht.name: Play.ht
play-ht.value: Play.ht, now PlayAI, sells realistic text to speech and a real time voice model for phone and web agents, with voice cloning and an API that developers use for IVR and companion products. It competes with ElevenLabs on latency and price.
play-ht.tagline: Text to speech and conversational voice agents, with an API built for low latency.
use_cases: Voice agents for phone and web
play-ht.governance_note: Voice agents that sound human must disclose they are AI where law requires it, and cloned voices need consent on file.

pytorch.name: PyTorch
pytorch.value: PyTorch is the framework most AI research and most modern models are written in, with an eager programming model, a compiler, distributed training and a large ecosystem. The PyTorch Foundation under the Linux Foundation governs it with Meta as the main contributor.
pytorch.tagline: The dominant deep learning framework, started at Meta and now governed by the Linux Foundation.
pytorch.governance_note: Supply chain: pin versions and watch for malicious packages impersonating PyTorch dependencies, which has happened.

cons: Name no longer used by the vendor
quizizz.name: Quizizz
quizizz.value: Quizizz rebranded to Wayground in 2025; this entry exists because the catalog carries both names. The product is profiled under Wayground: teacher created or AI generated quizzes and lessons, live games, homework and analytics.
quizizz.status: Renamed. Quizizz became Wayground in 2025; this catalog row is an alias and should point to the Wayground profile.
quizizz.tagline: Former name of Wayground, the classroom quiz and lesson platform with AI generated questions.
quizizz.governance_note: Same district data agreement as Wayground.
quizizz.training_optout: Education accounts are covered by student privacy terms; confirm.

quizlet.name: Quizlet
quizlet.value: Quizlet's Magic Notes turns uploaded notes into flashcards, outlines and practice tests, and its Q Chat tutor quizzes students conversationally, on top of the largest user made flashcard library. It is a consumer study tool with school adoption.
quizlet.tagline: Flashcard and study platform with AI that makes study sets from notes, a tutor mode and practice tests.
quizlet.governance_note: Consumer accounts for students fall outside district data agreements unless a school licence is used.

cons: Sentiment scoring of participants is contentious
read-ai.name: Read.ai
read-ai.value: Read.ai summarises meetings and measures engagement and sentiment of participants, and extends summaries to email and Slack, with a free tier that spread it widely. Its engagement scoring has drawn privacy criticism.
read-ai.tagline: Meeting notes plus engagement analytics, extended to email and messaging summaries.
use_cases: Daily digest across email and chat
read-ai.governance_note: Scoring participants' engagement and sentiment without their knowledge is a privacy and employment issue; disable it or disclose it.

recraft.name: Recraft
recraft.value: Recraft generates true vector graphics as well as raster images, lets teams train a brand style from their own assets and produces consistent icon and illustration sets, which is what design systems need. Its models rank near the top on quality benchmarks.
recraft.tagline: Image generation for designers with vector output, brand styles and consistent icon sets.
recraft.governance_note: Training a style on your brand assets uploads them to Recraft; check the terms on how style models are stored and shared.

tabnine.api: Enterprise administration APIs; no general inference API.
cons: Raw capability trails Cursor and Copilot on frontier models
tabnine.name: Tabnine
pros: Fully private deployment, including air gapped
Models trained on permissively licensed code, with indemnity
tabnine.value: Tabnine predates Copilot and chose a different lane, selling to enterprises that cannot send code to a public model: on premises and VPC deployment, models trained only on permissively licensed code, and an IP indemnity. It is the answer when the security team has already said no to the others.
tabnine.engine: Tabnine's own models, with optional routing to third party models when policy allows.
tabnine.latency: Fast completions; chat depends on the model deployed.

pricing.includes: Private deployment, custom models, admin controls

tabnine.quality: Good completions; the frontier gap is the price of the privacy posture.
tabnine.tagline: The code assistant that competes on privacy: self hosted, air gapped and trained only on permissive code.
use_cases: Code assistance in regulated or classified environments
Teams with strict IP provenance requirements
Custom models trained on a private codebase
tabnine.governance_note: This is the tool to name when a policy says code must not leave the building. Its provenance claim, models trained only on permissive licences, is the direct answer to the copyright exposure question that the other assistants handle with indemnities instead.
tabnine.training_optout: Tabnine does not train on customer code; private deployments keep code inside the customer's boundary.

trulens.api: Python. Feedback functions wrap providers and custom scoring logic; instrumentation attaches to LangChain, LlamaIndex, and custom apps.
cons: Smaller community and fewer integrations than Ragas or DeepEval
Metric naming differs from the Ragas vocabulary most teams have adopted, which costs translation effort
Judge-model variance and cost apply here as everywhere
Weaker CI-gating story than pytest-native frameworks
trulens.name: TruLens
pros: The RAG Triad is a genuinely useful diagnostic frame, not just a metric list
Built for production monitoring, not only offline experiments
OpenTelemetry tracing keeps it compatible with a wider observability stack
Feedback functions extend cleanly to domain-specific scoring
trulens.files: Feedback results persist to a local or configured store for trend analysis.
trulens.value: An open-source evaluation library built around feedback functions: programmable scorers that attach to a running application and grade its behaviour continuously. Its best-known contribution is the RAG Triad, which frames retrieval quality as three questions asked together, namely whether the context is relevant to the query, whether the answer is grounded in that context, and whether the answer addresses the question. Scoring all three localises a regression to the retriever or the generator instead of just showing that quality fell. TruLens leans toward live monitoring where Ragas leans toward offline scoring, and it emits OpenTelemetry tracing so evaluation sits alongside the rest of an observability stack.
trulens.engine: Python library with a local dashboard; OpenTelemetry tracing support.
trulens.latency: Feedback can run asynchronously beside the application, so scoring does not have to sit in the user request path.

pricing.includes: Feedback functions, RAG Triad, dashboard. Judge-model costs are yours.

trulens.quality: Strong conceptual framing and good production ergonomics. Community and integration breadth are smaller than Ragas or DeepEval, and the RAG Triad metrics rest on LLM judges with the same variance caveats as everything else in the category.
trulens.tagline: Feedback functions and the RAG Triad, aimed at watching quality in production rather than scoring a dataset once.
use_cases: Continuous quality scoring of a live application rather than a one-off dataset run
Diagnosing whether a quality drop came from retrieval or generation using the triad
Attaching custom domain scorers as feedback functions
Pairing evaluation with OpenTelemetry traces in one pipeline
trulens.governance_note: Continuous feedback scoring is what turns evaluation from a pre-launch gate into an operating control, and that distinction matters to an auditor: a quality claim evidenced only by a launch-day report says nothing about the system running today. The triad structure also produces better evidence than a single composite score, because it records which component failed rather than that something did. The standing caveats hold: judges are models with versions that must be pinned and recorded, feedback results are derived data with their own retention questions, and a grounded answer built on a stale source still scores well, so index freshness stays a separate control.
trulens.training_optout: Runs locally; judge calls reach whichever provider you configure, under that provider's terms.

unbabel.name: Unbabel
unbabel.value: Unbabel pairs machine translation with a crowd of editors and quality estimation models, originally for multilingual customer support tickets, and now sells a language operations platform. It is known for research on translation quality metrics.
unbabel.engine: Unbabel's own MT and quality models with partner LLMs.
unbabel.tagline: AI translation with human post editing for customer support and enterprise content, plus its own quality models.
unbabel.governance_note: Crowd editors handle customer content; confirm NDA and data handling.

veed-io.name: Veed.io AI
pros: One tool for most marketing video
veed-io.value: Veed is the broad browser editor for marketing teams: subtitles, translation, avatars, a text to video generator, eye contact correction, screen recording and clipping, all without installing software. It competes with Clipchamp and CapCut on ease and with Synthesia on avatars.
veed-io.tagline: Browser video editor with AI avatars, text to video, captions, dubbing and clipping in one subscription.
veed-io.governance_note: Cloud editor, so uploads live on Veed's infrastructure; enterprise tier for anything internal.

whylabs.name: WhyLabs
whylabs.value: WhyLabs profiles data statistically rather than storing raw data, which suits privacy sensitive monitoring, and added LangKit and guardrails for LLM applications. Its open source core is widely used even without the platform.
whylabs.tagline: Data and model monitoring built on the open source whylogs profiling library, with LLM security guardrails.
whylabs.governance_note: Profiling without raw data is a privacy advantage for monitoring regulated datasets.

you-com.api: Yes. Search, news and RAG APIs for developers.
cons: Smaller than the big three, with less ecosystem
Answer quality depends on which model you pick
you-com.name: You.com
you-com.files: Document upload in the app and connectors in the enterprise tier.
you-com.value: You.com started as a privacy minded search engine with an AI layer, then moved upmarket into enterprise search and agents that cite sources. Its edge is that answers come with live web retrieval and citations by default, and that it will run on a company's own content.
you-com.engine: Multiple third party frontier models plus You.com's own retrieval and ranking.
you-com.latency: Retrieval adds a second or two over a bare model call.

pricing.includes: All models, file upload, custom agents

you-com.quality: Good when the sources are good; it cites, which makes bad answers easier to catch than with most assistants.
you-com.tagline: A search first assistant that became an enterprise retrieval and agent platform.
use_cases: Research with sources you can check
integrations: Model APIs from the major vendors
Enterprise connectors for drives and wikis
you-com.governance_note: Citations are the governance feature: an answer that shows its sources can be checked. The enterprise tier's private deployment is the answer to the data path question for regulated content.
you-com.training_optout: Enterprise and API terms exclude training on customer data; confirm for the consumer tier.

01-ai-yi.name: 01.AI Yi
01-ai-yi.value: 01.AI's Yi models were strong open bilingual releases in 2023 and 2024, and the company shifted in 2025 to building enterprise applications on DeepSeek and others rather than training its own flagships. The Yi weights remain available.
01-ai-yi.status: Maintenance. 01.AI shifted to enterprise solutions on third party models in 2025.
01-ai-yi.tagline: Kai Fu Lee's lab that released the Yi open models and then pivoted from training frontier models to enterprise solutions.
01-ai-yi.governance_note: Standard open model review; company direction changed.

ai2-olmo.name: AI2 OLMo
ai2-olmo.value: OLMo is the model family that opens everything, not just weights: the Dolma training data, the training code and the checkpoints, so researchers can study how a model was made. It is the reference for what open really means and a credible model in its size classes.
ai2-olmo.tagline: Fully open language models from AI2, releasing weights, training data, code and logs for research.
ai2-olmo.governance_note: The only model family where training data provenance can be fully audited, which matters for copyright and bias reviews.

ai21-api.name: AI21 Labs API
ai21-api.value: AI21's Jamba models combine transformer and state space layers for very long context at lower cost, and the company sells them by API and through cloud marketplaces with a focus on enterprise document tasks. It also offers task specific models for summarisation and grounded answers.
ai21-api.tagline: API access to AI21's Jamba models, long context hybrid models from the Israeli lab behind Wordtune.
ai21-api.governance_note: Standard API data terms; confirm retention.
ai21-api.training_optout: AI21 does not train on API customer data by default; confirm.

cons: SaaS means prediction data leaves your infrastructure
Pricing can scale fast at high volume
Less enterprise compliance depth than IBM's offering
arize-ai.name: Arize AI
pros: Strong LLM tracing alongside traditional ML monitoring
arize-ai.files: Accepts prediction logs, embeddings, and LLM traces.
arize-ai.value: The practical choice for an ML team that needs model observability without the full enterprise governance stack. Handles traditional ML monitoring (drift, performance) and LLM tracing, evaluation, and prompt monitoring in one platform.
arize-ai.engine: Monitoring platform, not a model. Connects to model outputs and feature data.
arize-ai.quality: Strong on LLM tracing and evaluation, which is an area most governance platforms added late. Good ML monitoring depth.
arize-ai.tagline: Model observability for ML and LLM applications, used by ML teams already in production.
use_cases: Monitoring deployed ML and LLM applications for performance and data drift
Tracing LLM applications to debug prompt failures and quality issues
Running automated evaluations on LLM outputs in CI/CD
integrations: Most ML frameworks and serving platforms
LangChain, LlamaIndex, and LLM orchestration tools
CI/CD pipelines for eval in deployment
arize-ai.governance_note: LLM observability is the gap in most organizations' AI risk management: they monitor traditional ML models and then deploy LLM applications with no production visibility at all. A hallucination rate, a prompt injection, or a quality regression in an LLM feature is invisible without tracing. The audit question to ask is which deployed AI features have monitoring, and which are running dark.
arize-ai.training_optout: Monitoring platform, not a model host. Data retention and use terms govern what Arize stores from your prediction logs.

asana-ai.name: Asana AI
asana-ai.value: Asana's AI writes status reports, summarises projects, fills fields, flags risk and, through AI Studio, lets teams build agents into workflows without code. It is sold as part of Asana's higher tiers with a usage based AI Studio add on.
asana-ai.engine: Partner LLMs with Asana's work graph.
asana-ai.tagline: AI Studio and AI teammates in Asana for status updates, smart fields, summaries and workflow automation.
asana-ai.governance_note: Agents acting on tasks should be scoped to projects and logged; Asana provides admin controls for AI.
asana-ai.training_optout: Asana does not train on customer data.

baichuan.name: Baichuan
baichuan.value: Baichuan released competitive open bilingual models in 2023 and 2024 and was among China's AI tigers, then narrowed its strategy toward medical AI and hospital deployments. Its open models remain in use for Chinese language tasks.
baichuan.status: Active. Company refocused on medical AI.
baichuan.tagline: Beijing lab from a Sogou founder that released open Chinese models and then focused on healthcare AI.
baichuan.governance_note: Licence conditions on commercial use; Chinese data terms for the API.

cons: Token consumption is high on large projects
Backend and data work is weaker than the front end
Same security caveats as every app builder
bolt-new.name: Bolt.new
pros: Runs the code in the tab, so the loop is immediate
Open source core, which spawned a self hosted community
bolt-new.files: Images and design references; code exports to GitHub or downloads.
bolt-new.value: Bolt runs the whole development environment in the browser tab, Node included, so the agent can write code, install packages, run it and fix errors without a server. It was the first vibe coding product to reach a large audience and remains one of the fastest for front end heavy apps.
bolt-new.engine: Frontier models from several vendors driving StackBlitz's WebContainer runtime.
bolt-new.latency: Fast, because the runtime is local to the browser.
bolt-new.quality: Strong front end output; treat backend code as a draft.
bolt-new.tagline: StackBlitz's in browser agent that builds and runs full stack apps on WebContainers.
use_cases: Front end prototypes and marketing sites
Learning a framework by watching the agent build with it
bolt-new.governance_note: Same rule as the other builders: anything that touches customer data needs a review by someone who can read the code. The open source bolt.diy fork is the option for teams that want the workflow on their own infrastructure.
bolt-new.training_optout: StackBlitz's terms govern prompts and projects; confirm the current position before loading proprietary code.

canva-ai.api: Canva API for integration and automation.
cons: Free and enterprise tiers coexist with different data terms
canva-ai.name: Canva AI
pros: AI in a tool most teams already use without a learning curve
canva-ai.files: Images, presentation files, and design assets in Canva's format.
canva-ai.value: AI-powered image generation, background removal, text effects, and presentation assistance inside the design tool most non-designer teams already use. The value is accessibility rather than frontier quality.
canva-ai.engine: Mix of Canva's own models and third-party providers. Text to image uses Stability AI and others.
canva-ai.latency: Fast enough for interactive design work.

pricing.includes: Higher credit allowances, brand kit, admin controls

canva-ai.quality: Sufficient for internal use and social content. Below the specialist tools for fine art or production-quality commercial imagery.
canva-ai.tagline: AI design features embedded in the tool most marketing and operations teams already use.
use_cases: Generating images and backgrounds for marketing collateral without a designer
Expanding, removing, or replacing image backgrounds in existing assets
Accelerating slide and social content production for marketing teams
canva-ai.governance_note: Two practical points. First, the training-provenance question follows the sub-processor, not just Canva: if the underlying image model carries provenance uncertainty, that uncertainty applies to your published assets. Second, the free tier has different data terms than the enterprise tier, and in many organizations both are in use simultaneously, with different staff operating under different agreements without knowing it.
canva-ai.training_optout: Canva's terms and its sub-processors' terms both apply. The training-data provenance of the image generation models it uses is inherited from those providers. Enterprise agreements provide stronger data controls.

cerebras.api: Yes. OpenAI compatible chat and completions API.
cons: Hardware is a long term bet on one architecture
cerebras.name: Cerebras
pros: Fastest inference speeds publicly available for the models it hosts
Serious option for latency bound agent loops
cerebras.value: Cerebras built the largest chip ever made, the wafer scale engine, and uses it for an inference API that runs Llama, Qwen and other open models several times faster than GPU hosts. It also sells systems and cloud capacity for training. The company is known for speed, and for the IPO saga that followed.
cerebras.engine: Open models on Cerebras WSE-3 wafer scale systems.
cerebras.latency: The whole point; thousands of tokens per second on supported models.

pricing.includes: Reserved capacity or on premises systems

cerebras.quality: As good as the open model; speed is what you are buying.
cerebras.tagline: Wafer scale chips and an inference service that serves open models at record token speeds.
use_cases: Agents that make many sequential model calls
Real time voice and chat where speed matters
Training large models on owned hardware
cerebras.governance_note: Speed changes what is affordable: a reasoning loop that was too slow to use becomes usable. Keep the model licence check separate from the vendor review, and ask about data handling in the shared inference tier.
cerebras.training_optout: Cerebras states inference inputs are not used for training. Confirm in the current terms.

clipdrop.name: Clipdrop
clipdrop.value: Clipdrop packages Stability's models into practical tools, cleanup, relight, uncrop, upscale, text to image, with an API, serving designers who want Stable Diffusion without running it. Stability's financial turbulence has made its future less certain than its rivals.
clipdrop.engine: Stable Diffusion and Stability's editing models.
clipdrop.tagline: Stability AI's suite of image tools: background removal, relighting, upscaling, cleanup and generation with Stable Diffusion.
clipdrop.governance_note: Vendor review should note Stability AI's ownership changes and the training data history of Stable Diffusion, which is in litigation.

code-org.name: Code.org
code-org.value: Code.org added an AI teaching assistant that helps teachers assess student code and gives students hints, plus curriculum units on AI and machine learning, free for schools. It is the largest K12 CS curriculum provider.
code-org.tagline: Nonprofit computer science curriculum with an AI teaching assistant and courses on how AI works.
code-org.governance_note: Student privacy terms published; nonprofit governance.
code-org.training_optout: Student data is not used for training.

cons: Smaller community than W&B or MLflow
comet-ml.name: Comet ML
pros: One platform for classic ML and LLM work
Opik is open source and self hostable
comet-ml.value: Comet tracks experiments, datasets and models for ML teams, and its open source Opik project added tracing, evaluation and prompt management for LLM applications. It competes with Weights and Biases and MLflow on the classic side and with Langfuse and Braintrust on the LLM side.
comet-ml.engine: Not a model; an observability and tracking platform.
comet-ml.latency: Not applicable; logging overhead is small.
comet-ml.quality: Mature tracking; Opik is competitive and improving.
comet-ml.tagline: Experiment tracking and model management, extended into LLM evaluation and tracing with Opik.
use_cases: Tracking training runs and model versions
Tracing and evaluating LLM apps in production
comet-ml.governance_note: Traces contain prompts and model outputs, which can contain customer data. Treat the tracking platform as a data store with the same access and retention rules as the application.
comet-ml.training_optout: Comet does not train on customer data; self hosted Opik keeps traces in house.

credo-ai.api: API for integration with model pipelines.
cons: Less technical model monitoring depth than dedicated MLOps tools
Category is still maturing, product evolves frequently
credo-ai.name: Credo AI
pros: Purpose-built for AI governance programs, not adapted from GRC
Regulatory mapping for EU AI Act and NIST AI RMF
credo-ai.files: Policy documents, risk assessments, and technical model metadata.
credo-ai.value: Structured AI governance workflows: policy creation, risk assessment, AI inventory, and evidence collection for regulatory alignment. Built for organizations doing AI governance as a managed program rather than a one-time audit.
credo-ai.engine: Governance workflow platform. Integrates with model monitoring tools for technical signals.
credo-ai.latency: Async governance workflows, not interactive inference.

pricing.includes: Inventory, risk assessments, regulatory mapping, evidence storage

credo-ai.quality: Deep policy-mapping and workflow depth. Less technical depth than Arize or Fiddler for model monitoring.
credo-ai.tagline: AI governance platform built specifically for policy alignment and regulatory mapping.
use_cases: Building and maintaining an AI inventory with risk assessments per system
Mapping deployed AI against the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, or internal policy
Collecting and storing governance evidence for regulator inquiries
integrations: HRIS and identity for owner assignment
credo-ai.governance_note: This is the dedicated answer to 'we need to do AI governance as a program, not case by case.' The EU AI Act's Article 9 risk management system and Article 17 quality management system both require exactly what this tool manages: documented risk assessment, ongoing monitoring, and retained evidence. The NIST AI RMF is also mappable through it. For an organization building a formal AI governance function, this is the category to evaluate alongside OneTrust AI Governance and IBM OpenPages.
credo-ai.training_optout: Governance data platform. Not an AI model host. Data terms govern what Credo AI stores about your AI systems.

deepeval.api: Python: assert_test, metric classes, ConversationalTestCase, synthetic data generation.
cons: Requires Python fluency; not a no-code surface for domain reviewers
Heavy judge usage can trigger provider rate limits on large suites
No built-in production observability, so it pairs with a tracer rather than replacing one
The hosted platform is the path to dashboards and history; verify its terms before depending on it
deepeval.name: DeepEval
pros: Pytest-native, so it fits existing CI with almost no new concepts for the team
Broadest metric coverage of the open frameworks, including custom rubrics via G-Eval
Deterministic and model-graded checks live side by side rather than in separate systems
Red-teaming mapped to recognised frameworks makes security testing reportable
deepeval.files: Datasets and golden sets as code; results optionally sync to the hosted platform.
deepeval.value: An open-source framework that treats LLM evaluation as unit testing. Test cases are pytest functions, assertions carry thresholds, and a failing faithfulness or relevance score fails the build. That framing is the point: it puts model-graded metrics and deterministic assertions in the same suite, so a pull request can be blocked both because a required field is missing and because groundedness dropped below the line. The metric library is the broadest of the open frameworks, covering RAG metrics, G-Eval for custom rubrics, and multi-turn conversational cases that score retrieval quality across a whole dialogue rather than turn by turn. A companion library adds red-teaming aligned to the OWASP Top 10 for LLMs and the NIST AI RMF.
deepeval.engine: Python library, pytest-native. Optional hosted platform from Confident AI.
deepeval.latency: Offline. Model-graded metrics cost judge calls per case; deterministic assertions are effectively free and instant.

pricing.includes: Full metric library, red-teaming companion, pytest integration. Judge costs are yours.

pricing.limits: Verify current pricing with the vendor
pricing.includes: Hosted result tracking, dashboards, team collaboration

deepeval.quality: The most complete off-the-shelf metric coverage among open frameworks, and the cleanest CI story. Heavy judge usage on large suites can hit provider rate limits, which is a practical constraint on suite size rather than a defect.
deepeval.tagline: Evaluation written as pytest, so quality failures break the build the way any other test does.
use_cases: Blocking a deploy when a quality metric regresses, in the same pipeline as unit tests
Mixing deterministic assertions with model-graded scores in one suite
Scoring multi-turn conversations where retrieval quality shifts across turns
Red-teaming for jailbreaks, PII leakage, prompt injection, and bias before release
integrations: OWASP Top 10 for LLMs and NIST AI RMF red-team mappings
deepeval.governance_note: This is the cleanest answer to the audit question of how AI quality is controlled before release, because the evidence is the same artifact engineering already produces: a test run, versioned with the commit, that either passed or failed. Deterministic assertions deserve particular weight in that record. Model-graded scores are probabilistic and move with the judge, while an assertion that every response carries a citation, contains no PII, and refuses a prohibited prompt either held or did not. A defensible programme runs the deterministic gates first and treats the graded metrics as trend evidence on top, with the judge model pinned and recorded so scores stay comparable release to release.
deepeval.training_optout: The library runs locally; judge calls reach your configured provider. The hosted platform receives whatever results you sync, under Confident AI terms.

deepgram.name: Deepgram
deepgram.value: Deepgram's Nova models transcribe quickly and cheaply, and its Aura text to speech and voice agent API package the pieces of a conversational agent with low latency. It is a common backend for call centre and voice bot builders.
deepgram.tagline: Fast speech to text and text to speech APIs built for real time voice agents.
deepgram.governance_note: On premises deployment answers residency; voice agents must disclose they are AI where required.
deepgram.training_optout: Deepgram states customer data is not used for training without consent; confirm.

deepseek.api: REST API, largely OpenAI-compatible, which makes swapping it in unusually easy. That ease is itself a shadow-IT risk worth naming.
cons: Hosted service sits under Chinese jurisdiction
Restricted on government devices in several jurisdictions
Content behaviour reflects Chinese regulatory requirements
deepseek.name: DeepSeek
pros: Frontier-adjacent reasoning at very low cost
deepseek.files: Standard text and code handling on the hosted service.
deepseek.value: Reasoning performance close to the frontier at a fraction of the cost, with open-weight releases. The capability is real. The governance considerations are equally real and are the reason it needs its own policy decision rather than a default allow.
deepseek.engine: DeepSeek's own models, with several released as open weights.
deepseek.latency: Reasoning models trade latency for quality, as elsewhere in the category.
deepseek.quality: Genuinely strong at mathematics and code reasoning. Outputs reflect Chinese regulatory content requirements on politically sensitive subjects, which is a factual property of the model rather than a criticism.
deepseek.tagline: Frontier-class capability at very low cost, from a Chinese vendor, which is the whole governance story.
use_cases: High-volume reasoning workloads where per-token cost dominates
Self-hosting an open-weight reasoning model on controlled infrastructure
Benchmarking against incumbents to test whether premium pricing is justified
integrations: Hugging Face and standard self-hosting stacks
deepseek.governance_note: Treat the hosted API and the open weights as two different decisions. The weights can be run on your own infrastructure with no data leaving; the hosted API sends prompts to servers under Chinese jurisdiction, which triggers cross-border transfer analysis, and in some sectors and government contexts an outright prohibition. Several jurisdictions have restricted it on government devices. See the China AI regulation and global AI laws pages in the reference library before approving either.
deepseek.training_optout: The hosted service is operated from China and subject to Chinese law, including data access provisions. Self-hosting the open weights removes the data path entirely and is the only version most regulated organizations should consider.

cons: Timeline precision is weaker than Premiere
descript.name: Descript
pros: Transcript editing is faster than a timeline
descript.value: Descript turned transcription into the editing surface: delete a word and the cut happens, fix a line with a cloned voice, remove filler and silence in one click. Podcasters and video teams use it because the edit is as fast as reading.
descript.engine: Descript's own transcription and editing models plus its Overdub voice cloning.
descript.quality: Best in class for transcript editing.
descript.tagline: Edit video and audio by editing the transcript, with studio sound, filler removal and AI voices.
descript.governance_note: Voice cloning requires the speaker's consent recording, which Descript enforces; your policy should cover who may use a cloned voice and for what. Transcripts of meetings are records.
descript.training_optout: Descript states customer content is not used to train its models; confirm in the current terms.

edpuzzle.name: Edpuzzle
edpuzzle.value: Edpuzzle lets teachers add questions to videos and track answers, and its AI generates questions, summaries and voiceovers for any video, including YouTube and teacher recordings. It is standard in flipped and blended classrooms.
edpuzzle.tagline: Interactive video lessons with AI generated questions and notes, so teachers can check understanding inside any video.
edpuzzle.governance_note: Student data agreement; AI questions should be reviewed for accuracy.
edpuzzle.training_optout: Edpuzzle states student data is not used for training; confirm.

cons: Make output needs engineering to ship
figma-ai.name: Figma AI
figma-ai.value: Figma's AI features generate working prototypes from a prompt with Figma Make, fill designs with realistic content, rename layers, search designs visually and generate or edit images, all inside the tool most product teams already use. Make is the piece that competes with Lovable and v0.
figma-ai.engine: Partner models including OpenAI and Anthropic, plus Figma's own.
figma-ai.tagline: AI inside the design standard: Make for prototypes from prompts, plus search, rename, content fill and image tools.
figma-ai.governance_note: Admins can turn AI features off per team and set whether content trains Figma's models; set both deliberately. Figma states its models are not trained on customer content by default for Organization and Enterprise.
figma-ai.training_optout: Opt out available in admin settings; default varies by plan.

helicone.api: Base-URL swap plus headers. Dashboard covers logs, sessions, user metrics, cost tracking, P95 and P99 latency, alerts, and eval scores.
cons: Maintenance mode since March 2026: security patches and new models only, no roadmap
The proxy is in the critical path, so its availability is your availability, a sharper risk when the product is no longer actively developed
New integrations and analytics will not arrive, so the gap against active competitors widens over time
Not a sound default for a new production system being chosen for the next three years
helicone.name: Helicone
pros: Lowest integration cost in the category: change a base URL and you have observability
Gateway functions (caching, rate limiting, routing) live in the same layer as logging
Apache 2.0 core is self-hostable, which makes a stay-put decision viable
helicone.files: Prompts, datasets, and eval scores in the hosted plane.
helicone.value: A proxy-based observability platform and AI gateway: point your client base URL at Helicone and every request and response is logged with cost, token count, and latency, with no SDK to adopt and no code to instrument. That near-zero integration cost was the product, and it came with caching, rate limiting, and multi-provider routing in the same layer. The Apache 2.0 core can be self-hosted. For new production deployments in 2026 the maintenance-mode status is the deciding fact, not the feature set.
helicone.engine: HTTP proxy in front of provider APIs; self-hostable via Docker.
helicone.status: Maintenance mode. Mintlify acquired Helicone on 3 March 2026 and the founders joined Mintlify; the service stays live with security updates, bug fixes, and new model support, but active feature development has ended and Mintlify has said it will help customers migrate.
helicone.latency: The proxy sits in the request path, which is the architectural trade: an outage or slowdown there affects live traffic rather than only telemetry.

pricing.includes: Unlimited seats, alerts, reports, query language
Multiple organisations, compliance attestations, SSO, on-premises options

helicone.quality: Proven at scale before the acquisition, having served roughly 16,000 organisations. What ships today still works; what will not arrive is new capability.
helicone.tagline: The one-line proxy that made LLM observability trivial to adopt, now in maintenance mode after acquisition.
use_cases: Getting cost and latency visibility in minutes without instrumenting code
Caching and rate limiting at the gateway layer alongside logging
Existing deployments already running it, where the near-term question is migration planning
integrations: Any provider reachable by base-URL swap
OpenAI, Anthropic, and 100-plus models through the gateway
helicone.governance_note: This is the clearest live example of dependency lifecycle as a governance question rather than a procurement one. A proxy carries your API keys and all prompt and completion traffic through a component whose vendor has publicly stopped feature development, which concentrates two risks in one place: critical-path availability and stalled security posture in a fast-moving ecosystem. Existing users are not in danger today, and the Apache 2.0 licence means self-hosting is a real option, but an architecture review should record a migration decision with a date rather than leaving it implicit. The wider pattern belongs in the same review: ClickHouse acquired Langfuse in January 2026 and Mintlify acquired Helicone in March, so standalone LLM observability is consolidating into larger infrastructure platforms, and asking who owns a tool and what their strategic priority is has become part of choosing one.
helicone.training_optout: Proxy architecture means full request and response bodies transit the vendor unless self-hosted. Verify terms, or self-host if prompt content is sensitive.

hour-one.name: Hour One
hour-one.value: Hour One produces presenter videos from text with photoreal avatars, scene templates and brand kits, selling to marketing and learning teams. It positions on avatar realism and on consistent branded output rather than breadth of features.
hour-one.engine: Hour One's own avatar models with partner voices.
hour-one.tagline: Avatar presenter videos with a focus on realistic virtual humans and brand consistency.
hour-one.governance_note: Standard avatar consent and synthetic labelling rules.

ideogram.name: Ideogram
ideogram.value: Ideogram solved the problem of legible text inside generated images before its rivals, and added a canvas with inpainting and extension, style references and character consistency. Designers use it when the image needs words.
ideogram.tagline: Image generation known for rendering text accurately, which makes it the choice for posters, logos and ads.
ideogram.governance_note: Free tier generations are public by default; use a paid tier with private generation for client work. Logo concepts are inspiration, not trademarks, until a designer finishes them.

internlm.name: InternLM
internlm.value: InternLM is produced by a state research lab rather than a company, released openly with a full toolchain for training, evaluation and deployment, and competitive in reasoning and math. It shows how China's public research system contributes to the open model ecosystem.

pricing.limits: Apache licence with registration for commercial use

internlm.tagline: Open model family from Shanghai AI Lab, a government backed research institute, with strong reasoning and tooling.
internlm.governance_note: Commercial use requires a registration step with the lab; note it in the licence record.

cons: Only useful within Khan Academy's curriculum
Pedagogical approach frustrates students who want a direct answer
khanmigo.name: Khanmigo (Khan Academy)
pros: Safety and pedagogy designed in, not bolted on
COPPA and FERPA compliance built from the start
Tutors rather than answers, which serves learning outcomes
khanmigo.files: Khan Academy's curriculum content and student progress data.
khanmigo.value: A Socratic tutor that helps rather than answers, with content moderation and safety guardrails designed for minors from the ground up. Positioned against the risk of a student using a general assistant to skip the thinking rather than do it.
khanmigo.engine: Built on frontier models (primarily OpenAI) with Khan Academy's educational methodology and safety layer.
khanmigo.quality: Pedagogically oriented: better at guiding a student to an answer than at producing one efficiently. That is the intention.
khanmigo.tagline: The AI tutor Khan Academy built with child safety and learning theory at the centre.
use_cases: Guided tutoring on Khan Academy's curriculum without direct answer provision
Safe AI assistance for K-12 students in a moderated environment
Teacher-facing features for lesson planning and student progress context
khanmigo.governance_note: This is the reference case for child-safe AI deployment. The governance requirements for AI tools used by children are substantively different from adult deployment: COPPA (under 13), FERPA (student records), and the content moderation requirements that come with minors as users all apply. The product was designed with those constraints as requirements rather than afterthoughts. Institutions deploying any AI tool to K-12 students should use this as the comparison baseline for what a compliant product looks like.
khanmigo.training_optout: Follows OpenAI's sub-processor terms plus Khan Academy's own student data terms. COPPA and FERPA compliance are explicit product requirements.

krita-ai.name: Krita AI
krita-ai.value: Krita itself is a free digital painting program; the AI comes from community plugins, chiefly the AI Diffusion plugin, that run Stable Diffusion or Flux locally for inpainting, live painting and upscaling without leaving the canvas. It is the artist's local, free alternative to Photoshop generative fill.
krita-ai.engine: Stable Diffusion and Flux via ComfyUI, run locally or on a connected server.
krita-ai.quality: As good as the model you run.
krita-ai.tagline: Open source painting software with community plugins that run Stable Diffusion locally inside the canvas.
krita-ai.governance_note: Local means private; the governance issue is the licence of each model file you download, which varies and sometimes bars commercial use.

langfuse.api: Python and JavaScript SDKs, OpenTelemetry OTLP, public REST API.
cons: Production self-hosting has a real ops footprint: several stateful services, not a single binary
The unit-based billing model is easy to under-forecast, since one multi-step trace consumes many units
No built-in gateway, so caching, routing, and failover need a separate component
Now owned by an infrastructure company, which is a strategic-priority question to revisit rather than a present-day defect
langfuse.name: Langfuse
pros: MIT-licensed core, genuinely self-hostable, no per-seat multiplication
Usage-based pricing means a ten-person team pays the same as a two-person team for the same traffic
OpenTelemetry-native and framework-neutral, so instrumentation stays portable
Largest open-source community in the category, which shows in integration coverage
langfuse.files: Prompt versions, datasets, scores, and annotation queues as first-class objects; dataset-based regression testing runs in CI.
langfuse.value: Tracing, prompt management, evaluation, datasets, human annotation, and cost analytics for LLM applications, with an MIT-licensed core you can run yourself via Docker Compose or take as managed cloud. It is deliberately neutral: built on OpenTelemetry, with native integrations for LangChain, LlamaIndex, AutoGen, Haystack, and Semantic Kernel, plus thin wrappers for raw provider SDKs. For teams that want production observability without adopting a framework or a per-seat contract, it is the most common landing place.
langfuse.engine: Self-hosted or managed cloud. OpenTelemetry-native ingest.
langfuse.status: Active. Acquired by ClickHouse in January 2026; development has continued and the open-source core remains MIT-licensed.
langfuse.latency: Asynchronous SDK export; no proxy in the request path.

pricing.includes: MIT-licensed core: tracing, prompts, evals, datasets

pricing.limits: Billed per tracing unit, where a trace, observation, or score each count as a unit, so one multi-span trace consumes several
pricing.includes: Higher allowances, longer retention, enterprise features

langfuse.quality: Broad and mature feature coverage with the largest open-source community in the category. Self-hosting is real but not trivial: a production deployment expects Postgres, ClickHouse, a Redis-compatible cache, object storage, and worker processes.
langfuse.tagline: The open-source observability default: framework-agnostic, self-hostable, and priced on data rather than seats.
use_cases: Framework-agnostic tracing across a stack that is not standardised on one library
Self-hosted observability where prompts and completions must stay in your infrastructure
Prompt versioning and dataset-based regression tests wired into CI
Cost attribution by model, user, or session
integrations: LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, AutoGen, Haystack, Semantic Kernel
langfuse.governance_note: The self-hosted option makes this the straightforward answer when prompt and completion text cannot leave your environment, which is the usual blocker for observability in regulated settings. Running it yourself transfers rather than removes the obligation: the trace store becomes a system holding sensitive text, and belongs in the data map with its own retention, access control, and encryption decisions. The January 2026 ClickHouse acquisition is worth recording in a dependency review, not as a warning but as a fact with a review date, since a widely used open-source tool acquired by an infrastructure vendor has a different long-run trajectory than an independent one, and the MIT core is the hedge that keeps the exit cheap.
langfuse.training_optout: Self-hosted deployments send nothing outward. Cloud tiers are governed by the vendor agreement; verify current terms.

cons: Generic answers if knowledge base is thin
mainstay.name: Mainstay
mainstay.value: Mainstay, formerly AdmitHub, sends and answers text messages to students at scale with a chatbot that handles common questions and escalates to staff, with research showing gains in enrolment and persistence. It is one of the earliest studied AI chatbots in education.
mainstay.engine: Mainstay's conversational models with partner LLMs.
mainstay.tagline: Conversational texting platform for colleges and K12 that nudges students on enrolment, financial aid and persistence.
mainstay.governance_note: Texting students requires consent under TCPA and FERPA handling of conversation records; disclose that the responder is a bot.

merative.name: Merative
merative.value: Merative carries the Watson Health assets, Micromedex drug information, Truven analytics, clinical development and imaging software, after IBM sold the division in 2022, and applies AI across them more quietly than Watson's original claims. It is a cautionary tale and a continuing business.
merative.engine: Merative's own analytics and partner AI.
merative.tagline: The former IBM Watson Health, now a standalone health data and analytics company under Francisco Partners.
merative.governance_note: Watson for Oncology's overpromising is the standard case study in AI governance for healthcare; it belongs in training material.

monitaur.name: Monitaur
monitaur.value: Monitaur records model development, validation and monitoring in a structured system of record designed for insurance regulators and model risk teams, with templates aligned to NAIC and SR 11-7 expectations. It is a specialist for regulated model governance.
monitaur.tagline: Model governance software for insurance and financial services, built around regulator facing documentation.
use_cases: Insurer model governance under NAIC bulletins
monitaur.governance_note: Maps to the NAIC model bulletin on insurer AI use; useful where state insurance regulators examine.

opusclip.name: OpusClip
opusclip.value: OpusClip reads a podcast, webinar or stream and cuts it into vertical clips with animated captions, a virality score and automatic reframing. It is the market leader in repurposing long form into short form.
opusclip.engine: OpusClip's own clip selection and caption models.
opusclip.tagline: Turns long videos into short clips with captions, picking the moments most likely to perform.
opusclip.governance_note: Clips are published under your brand; keep a human approval before auto posting, since a clip out of context can misrepresent a speaker.

otter-ai.api: API available on higher tiers for transcript retrieval and workflow integration.
cons: Recording consent exposure is serious and jurisdiction-dependent
Speaker attribution errors carry real consequences
otter-ai.name: Otter.ai
pros: Strong searchable archive across many meetings
otter-ai.files: Live meeting audio plus uploaded audio and video files.
otter-ai.value: Joins meetings, transcribes them, and produces searchable notes and summaries automatically. Removes note-taking overhead entirely, which is why adoption tends to spread through an organization without anyone approving it.
otter-ai.engine: Proprietary speech recognition and summarisation models.
otter-ai.latency: Real-time captioning during the meeting; summaries follow shortly after.
otter-ai.quality: Strong on clear audio and standard accents. Degrades with crosstalk, heavy accents, and specialised vocabulary, and summaries occasionally attribute a statement to the wrong speaker, which matters more than a plain transcription error.
otter-ai.tagline: Meeting transcription and notes, and the tool most likely to create a consent problem.
use_cases: Automatic transcripts and summaries of recurring internal meetings
Searchable archive of decisions across many calls
Accessibility, live captioning for participants who need it
otter-ai.governance_note: The highest-risk tool in ordinary daily use, and the risk is legal rather than technical. Recording consent law varies by jurisdiction: several US states require all-party consent, and recording a call without it is a criminal matter in some of them, not a policy breach. Add legal privilege, HR investigations, and regulated client conversations and the exposure compounds. Any deployment needs an explicit consent practice, a retention policy, and a clear list of meeting types where it must never join. This is also the tool most often found in an AI inventory that nobody approved.
otter-ai.training_optout: Business and enterprise tiers offer data controls. Consumer tiers differ. Verify before any privileged or regulated conversation is recorded.

panorama.name: Panorama
panorama.value: Panorama Education collects surveys on climate and social emotional learning, tracks student data for MTSS and intervention, and added Solara, an AI assistant that drafts plans and answers questions over district data. Its AI is a layer on a data platform.
panorama.tagline: Student success and survey platform with an AI assistant, Solara, for teachers and administrators.
panorama.governance_note: An assistant over behavioural and social emotional data is high sensitivity; limit access by role and review the agreement on how Solara uses records.
panorama.training_optout: Panorama states student data is not used to train models; confirm.

pinecone.api: Yes. REST and gRPC with client libraries.
cons: Costs can surprise at scale compared with self hosting
Your vectors live in Pinecone's cloud
Open source alternatives have closed the feature gap
pinecone.name: Pinecone
pinecone.files: Vectors and metadata; documents are embedded before they arrive.
pinecone.value: Pinecone sells one thing, vector search as a service, and does it without operations: serverless indexes, metadata filtering, hybrid search and namespaces, billed by what you store and query. It is the default choice when a team wants RAG to work on Monday and does not want to run a database.
pinecone.engine: Proprietary vector index on Pinecone's cloud; the embeddings come from your model or Pinecone's hosted ones.
pinecone.latency: Low tens of milliseconds for typical queries.

pricing.limits: Pay per storage, read and write unit

pinecone.quality: Reliable at scale; the retrieval quality is mostly about your embeddings and chunking.
pinecone.tagline: The managed vector database that made retrieval augmented generation a product category.
pinecone.governance_note: Embeddings are derived data, and a vector store full of them is still a store of your documents for most privacy purposes. Treat it as you would the source documents: region, access control, retention and deletion all apply.
pinecone.training_optout: Pinecone does not use customer data for training. Confirm in the current terms.

pitch-ai.name: Pitch AI
pitch-ai.value: Pitch is a modern presentation tool with real time collaboration, templates, analytics on who viewed a deck, and AI that drafts a deck from a prompt. It targets startups and sales teams who outgrew Google Slides.
pitch-ai.tagline: Collaborative presentation software with AI generation, built for startup and sales teams.
pitch-ai.governance_note: Viewer analytics on shared decks are personal data; align with your privacy notice.

quillbot.name: QuillBot
quillbot.value: QuillBot paraphrases text in chosen modes, checks grammar, summarises, translates and detects AI text, with a huge student user base. Course Hero, now Learneo, owns it; its paraphraser raises academic integrity questions in education.
quillbot.tagline: Paraphrasing, grammar and summarising tool popular with students and writers, owned by Course Hero.
quillbot.governance_note: In education it sits on the integrity line; policies should say whether paraphrasing tools are permitted. In business, paraphrased legal or contractual text must be checked for meaning drift.

slack-ai.api: Slack API; AI features are in product.
slack-ai.name: Slack AI
pros: Data stays within Slack's trust boundary
slack-ai.value: Slack AI summarises channels and threads, answers questions from workspace history, writes huddle notes and daily recaps, and hosts Salesforce Agentforce agents as teammates. It is included in higher plans rather than sold separately now.
slack-ai.engine: Salesforce hosted LLMs within the Einstein Trust Layer.
slack-ai.tagline: Summaries, search answers and recaps inside Slack, with Agentforce agents joining channels.
slack-ai.governance_note: AI search surfaces anything a user could already see, so channel permissions are the control; audit them before enabling.
slack-ai.training_optout: Salesforce does not train on customer Slack data.

slidesai.name: SlidesAI
slidesai.value: SlidesAI runs inside Google Slides and PowerPoint, taking pasted text or a topic and producing slides with layouts and images. It suits people who want AI inside the tool they already use rather than a new platform.
slidesai.tagline: Google Slides and PowerPoint add on that turns text into slides.
slidesai.governance_note: An add on with document access; review Workspace permissions before deploying org wide.

smartcat.name: Smartcat
pros: AI plus human in one workflow
smartcat.value: Smartcat runs the whole localisation workflow: AI translation with glossaries and memory, human post editing from its marketplace, and management of projects, vendors and payments. It competes with Phrase and Lokalise for enterprise localisation.
smartcat.engine: Multiple MT engines and LLMs with Smartcat's own routing.
smartcat.latency: Seconds for AI; days for human review.
smartcat.tagline: Translation platform combining AI translation, a marketplace of human linguists and localisation project management.
smartcat.governance_note: Marketplace linguists are contractors who see your content; confidentiality terms and NDA options matter for sensitive material.
smartcat.training_optout: Smartcat states customer content is not used to train shared models; confirm.

soundraw.name: Soundraw
