soundraw.value: Soundraw generates background music by mood, genre and length from a library of in house produced material, which lets it offer clean commercial licences. It targets YouTubers and marketers who need safe music fast.
soundraw.engine: Soundraw's own models trained on its own recordings.
soundraw.tagline: Royalty free music generator for creators, with tracks built from the company's own recordings.
soundraw.governance_note: Training on owned recordings is the reason it is low risk; keep the licence record per track.

stack-ai.api: Yes. Every workflow exposes an endpoint.
cons: Smaller template ecosystem than the consumer builders
Visual flows still need an owner who understands them
stack-ai.name: Stack AI
pros: Deployment options that satisfy security review
stack-ai.files: Document upload and connectors to document stores.
stack-ai.value: Stack AI competes for the enterprise end of the no code builder market: SOC 2, HIPAA, on premises and VPC deployment, connectors to internal systems, and a visual builder for agents and document workflows. It is bought by operations and IT teams who want to build internally without a model vendor contract per project.
stack-ai.engine: Multiple model providers, including private and on premises options.
stack-ai.tagline: An enterprise no code builder for AI agents and workflows, with the compliance posture that regulated buyers ask for.
use_cases: Document intake and extraction in regulated firms
Internal knowledge assistants with access control
integrations: Model providers including Azure OpenAI and Bedrock
stack-ai.governance_note: The deployment options are the point: a VPC or on premises install keeps documents inside the boundary, and the audit log answers who ran what. Confirm which model providers are reachable from the install you buy.
stack-ai.training_optout: Stack AI does not train on customer data; private deployments keep data inside the customer boundary.

submagic.name: Submagic
submagic.value: Submagic began as the caption tool whose animated word by word styles became the short form look, and added auto b roll, zooms, sound effects and clipping from long videos. Creators use it to finish clips rather than cut them.
submagic.engine: Submagic's own caption and effects models.
submagic.tagline: Animated captions, b roll and sound effects for short form video, with a clipper added later.
submagic.governance_note: Captions are accessibility records; check accuracy on names and figures before publishing.

typeface.name: Typeface
typeface.value: Typeface, founded by a former Adobe executive, trains on a brand's assets to produce campaign content, images and copy that match, with approval workflows and integrations into Salesforce, Microsoft and Google. It sells to large marketing organisations.
typeface.engine: Partner LLMs and image models with Typeface's brand layer.
typeface.tagline: Enterprise content generation for brands, combining text and image generation with brand training and approvals.
typeface.governance_note: Brand asset training uploads your library; check ownership and deletion terms. Approval workflows are the control for regulated claims.
typeface.training_optout: Typeface states customer content is not used to train shared models; confirm.

voicemod.name: Voicemod
voicemod.value: Voicemod changes your voice live in games, Discord and streams, with AI voices that sound like different people and a soundboard. It is consumer entertainment software with a large user base.
voicemod.engine: Voicemod's own real time voice models.
voicemod.tagline: Real time voice changer for gamers and streamers, with AI voices and a soundboard.
voicemod.governance_note: Consumer tool; the risk is impersonation of real people, which its terms prohibit.

weaviate.api: Yes. REST, GraphQL and gRPC with client libraries.
cons: Operating it yourself takes database skills
Schema design matters more than in Pinecone
Cloud pricing by dimensions needs modelling
weaviate.name: Weaviate
weaviate.files: Objects with vectors and metadata; documents are chunked and embedded on the way in.
weaviate.value: Weaviate stores objects and their vectors together, runs hybrid keyword and vector search, and can call embedding and generative models for you through its module system. It is the open source answer to Pinecone for teams that want to run the database themselves or buy it hosted from the same vendor.
weaviate.engine: Weaviate's own vector index with pluggable embedding modules for OpenAI, Cohere, Hugging Face and local models.
weaviate.latency: Milliseconds for typical queries; depends on index settings and hardware.

pricing.includes: Dedicated or bring your own cloud, support

weaviate.quality: Mature and widely deployed; retrieval quality is mostly your embeddings and schema.
weaviate.tagline: Open source vector database with hybrid search and built in model integrations, self hosted or as a cloud service.
use_cases: RAG where keyword and semantic search both matter
Self hosted vector search for data that cannot leave
Multimodal search over images and text
integrations: Embedding APIs from the major vendors
weaviate.governance_note: Self hosting answers the data residency question and raises the operations one. If a module calls an external embedding model, that call is a data transfer to the model vendor and belongs in the vendor review.
weaviate.training_optout: Self hosted, nothing leaves. Weaviate Cloud does not train on customer data; external model calls follow the model vendor's terms.

windsurf.api: No general API; it is an editor.
cons: Ownership changed twice in one summer
Model routing across vendors widens the data path
windsurf.name: Windsurf
pros: Agentic multi file editing on a par with Cursor
Also available as a plugin for JetBrains and others
Enterprise tier with on premises options from the Codeium days
windsurf.files: Full repository context with its own indexing.
windsurf.value: Windsurf, formerly Codeium, is a VS Code derived editor with an agent, Cascade, that can plan and execute multi file changes. Its 2025 summer is the story: a reported OpenAI acquisition fell through, Google hired the founders in a licensing deal, and Cognition, maker of the Devin agent, bought what was left. The product continued, and that history is why procurement will ask about the roadmap.
windsurf.engine: Model agnostic; routes to frontier models from several vendors plus its own fast models.
windsurf.latency: Fast completions; agent runs take longer by nature.

pricing.includes: Admin controls, SSO, zero data retention options

windsurf.quality: Strong, and still improving under Cognition. Review agent changes as carefully as any contractor's pull request.
windsurf.tagline: An agentic code editor that passed through an OpenAI deal and a Google licence before Cognition bought it.
use_cases: Agent driven feature work across a codebase
Enterprises wanting self hosted code AI
windsurf.governance_note: Ask two questions before buying: who owns the product and its roadmap for the next two years, and which model vendors see your code under the plan you choose. The enterprise tier's zero retention and self hosted options exist because the original company sold to regulated customers.
windsurf.training_optout: Paid tiers exclude training on your code and offer zero data retention. Confirm the current terms under Cognition.

wordtune.name: Wordtune
wordtune.value: Wordtune rewrites sentences in different tones and lengths, summarises documents and drafts emails, running on AI21's own models. It is the writing assistant for people who want suggestions rather than generation.
wordtune.tagline: Rewrite and tone assistant from AI21 Labs that suggests alternatives sentence by sentence.
wordtune.governance_note: Browser extension reads what you type; business tier for admin control.
wordtune.training_optout: AI21 states user content is not used for training by default; confirm.

2short-ai.name: 2short.ai
2short-ai.value: 2short is a lighter clipping tool aimed at YouTubers: paste a link, get candidate shorts with captions and reframing, tweak in a simple editor. It competes on price and simplicity.
2short-ai.tagline: YouTube focused clipper that pulls shorts from long videos with captions and a built in editor.

arthur-ai.name: Arthur AI
arthur-ai.value: Arthur monitors models in production for drift, bias and performance and added LLM guardrails and an open source engine for evaluating generative outputs, serving financial services and other regulated customers. It is one of the independent governance vendors.
arthur-ai.tagline: Model monitoring and guardrails for classic ML and LLMs, with an open source evaluation engine.
use_cases: Fairness monitoring for credit and hiring models
arthur-ai.governance_note: Monitoring output is evidence for SR 11-7 and EU AI Act obligations; define thresholds and who responds to alerts.
arthur-ai.training_optout: Arthur does not train on customer data.

browse-ai.api: Yes. Each robot can be called as an API.
cons: Not suited to very large crawls
Same legal questions as any scraper
browse-ai.name: Browse AI
pros: Change monitoring is a strong use on its own
Clean exports to sheets and APIs
browse-ai.files: Outputs as tables, CSV and JSON.
browse-ai.value: Browse AI lets a non developer build a scraper by clicking the data on a page, then run it on a schedule, turn it into a monitor that alerts on changes, or expose it as an API. It is the quickest route to structured data from a site for analysts and marketers.
browse-ai.engine: Browse AI's own extraction runtime with AI assisted field detection.
browse-ai.latency: Minutes per run; monitors on a schedule.
browse-ai.tagline: No code web scraping and monitoring: point at a page, train a robot, get a table or an alert.
use_cases: Collecting directory data into a spreadsheet
browse-ai.governance_note: Same scraping rule: decide which sites and which data are in scope, and keep personal data out unless you have a lawful basis. Monitoring a competitor's public prices is routine; collecting people's details is not.
browse-ai.training_optout: Browse AI does not train on customer data under its terms; confirm the current position.

cheggmate.name: CheggMate
cheggmate.value: CheggMate combined GPT models with Chegg's decades of expert answered questions to give students step by step help, as Chegg's subscriber base collapsed under free AI competition. It is a case study in a homework help business overtaken by general models.
cheggmate.status: Active. Chegg's business shrank sharply under AI competition and the product's future is uncertain.
cheggmate.quality: Good where its archive is strong.
cheggmate.tagline: Chegg's AI study assistant built on its archive of expert answers, launched as the company's response to ChatGPT.
cheggmate.governance_note: Institutions treat homework help services under academic integrity policies; the AI layer does not change that.

classdojo.name: ClassDojo
classdojo.value: ClassDojo connects teachers, students and families with behaviour points, portfolios and messaging, used in most US elementary schools, and its AI is limited to message translation and a teacher assistant for drafting. The AI is a feature, not the product.
classdojo.status: Active. AI features limited to translation and teacher drafting; flagged for vendor check.
classdojo.tagline: Classroom communication and behaviour app for families, with AI added for message translation and teacher assistance.
classdojo.governance_note: Student data platform; district agreement required. AI use is minimal and should be described accurately on the site.
classdojo.training_optout: ClassDojo states student data is not used for training; confirm.

colossyan.name: Colossyan
colossyan.value: Colossyan competes with Synthesia specifically on learning and development: scenario branching, quizzes, SCORM export and a document to video feature for turning policies into training. It is the choice when the buyer is the L and D team.
colossyan.engine: Colossyan's own avatars with partner voices.
colossyan.tagline: Avatar video built for workplace learning, with branching scenarios and LMS export.
colossyan.governance_note: Training videos are records in a compliance programme; version them and keep the script as the source of truth, since the avatar reads whatever the script says.

consensus.name: Consensus
consensus.value: Consensus searches hundreds of millions of papers, extracts findings relevant to a question and shows a meter of how many studies support, oppose or are mixed, with citations to each. It is the research tool for people who need evidence, not a chatbot's opinion.
consensus.engine: Consensus's own retrieval and extraction models over Semantic Scholar and other indexes, with partner LLMs.
consensus.tagline: AI search over peer reviewed research that summarises what papers say about a question and shows the evidence split.
use_cases: Evidence checks for policy and practice
consensus.governance_note: Citations are real papers, which is the point; still read the paper before relying on a summary in anything that matters.
consensus.training_optout: Not applicable to user content of note.

darktrace.api: Darktrace API for SIEM integration and management.
cons: Autonomous action requires explicit policy governance
False positive management is ongoing work
darktrace.name: Darktrace
pros: Detects novel threats that rules miss
Broad coverage across network, cloud, and identity
darktrace.files: Network traffic, endpoint telemetry, email, cloud, and identity logs.
darktrace.value: Network and endpoint security that builds a model of normal behaviour for every device and user, then detects and responds to deviations autonomously. The autonomous-response capability is both the product's main differentiator and the clearest governance challenge.
darktrace.engine: Proprietary unsupervised machine learning. Not an LLM product; it learns patterns rather than reasoning in language.
darktrace.latency: Continuous real-time monitoring. Autonomous response triggers within seconds.
darktrace.quality: Sensitive detection across subtle behavioural deviation. False positive rate management is the primary implementation challenge.
darktrace.tagline: Autonomous cyber AI that detects and responds to threats by learning normal behaviour.
use_cases: Detecting novel attacks that signature-based tools miss
Autonomous containment of active threats without waiting for analyst action
Continuous monitoring across network, cloud, email, and identity
darktrace.governance_note: Autonomous response is where AI governance and security governance converge. Darktrace can act: it can isolate a device, block a connection, or quarantine a user account without human approval, in seconds. That capability prevents damage, and it also carries risk if a false positive triggers it on a critical system during peak hours. The governance requirement is explicit policy on which autonomous actions are approved, under which conditions, with what notification, and who has the authority to override. Those decisions belong in a human-reviewed policy document, not in the tool's default settings.
darktrace.training_optout: The model learns your environment. Darktrace's terms govern what they retain. Autonomous action is taken on your infrastructure, which is the salient governance point.

decktopus.name: Decktopus
decktopus.value: Decktopus produces decks from a few prompts with templates and adds forms, Q and A and viewer tracking, selling to small businesses and freelancers at low prices. It is a lighter rival to Gamma.
decktopus.tagline: Budget AI deck generator with templates, forms and basic analytics.

edgenuity.name: Edgenuity
edgenuity.value: Edgenuity delivers full online courses used for credit recovery and virtual school, with video instruction and automated scoring, and became Imagine Edgenuity after the merger. Its automated essay grading drew public criticism when students found keyword tricks, which makes it a case study in assessment AI.
edgenuity.engine: Automated scoring with limited AI features.
edgenuity.status: Active. Now Imagine Edgenuity; AI claim limited to automated grading; flagged for vendor check.
edgenuity.tagline: Online course platform for credit recovery and virtual learning, now Imagine Edgenuity, with automated grading of student responses.
edgenuity.governance_note: Flagged on the unverified list: automated grading is the only AI claim and it has known weaknesses. Automated scores for credit decisions should be reviewed by teachers.

cons: Far from general-purpose capability at current scale
Product liability and safety law requirements are significant
figure-ai.name: Figure AI
pros: Commercial production deployment, not purely research
General-purpose physical AI capability is the long-horizon value
BMW and other industrial partnerships validate commercial viability
figure-ai.files: Camera feeds, sensor data, and verbal instruction.
figure-ai.value: Figure's humanoid robots, powered by AI vision and language models, are the furthest-along commercial attempt at general-purpose physical AI in industrial settings. Currently deployed in limited production environments.
figure-ai.engine: Vision-language-action models trained on robot interaction data. OpenAI partnership for language capability.
figure-ai.latency: Real-time physical control with AI-driven decision making.
figure-ai.quality: Operational in limited production environments. Far from general-purpose capability at scale.
figure-ai.tagline: Humanoid robotics powered by AI, the leading commercial deployment attempt.
use_cases: Warehouse and manufacturing tasks currently requiring human dexterity
Physically demanding or repetitive industrial work without dedicated tooling
Long-horizon research into general-purpose physical AI capability
integrations: Industrial plant systems via partnership integration
figure-ai.governance_note: Physical AI is where AI governance, product liability, and workplace safety law converge. A robot that injures a worker is governed by OSHA, product liability, and potentially sector-specific safety regulations, not just AI policy. The EU AI Act specifically classifies AI in safety-critical physical environments as high-risk. The governance requirement before any physical AI deployment is a safety case: what are the failure modes, what is the physical consequence of each, and what are the guards against each mode. That safety case should be documented independently of the vendor's own safety claims.
figure-ai.training_optout: Physical operation data terms are governed by partnership agreements.

formative.name: Formative
formative.value: Formative lets teachers see student responses live, auto grades, and generates questions and feedback with AI from standards or uploaded content, and Newsela acquired it in 2023. It competes with Wayground for in class checks.
formative.tagline: Real time formative assessment platform with AI generated questions and feedback, now part of Newsela.

grammarly.api: Limited. Primarily an end-user product rather than a platform.
cons: Extension sees an extremely broad slice of organizational text
Free-tier installs bypass vendor review entirely
grammarly.name: Grammarly
pros: Genuinely effective on mechanics and clarity
Style guide enforcement at enterprise tier
grammarly.files: Operates on text in place. Document upload in the web editor.
grammarly.value: Real-time correction and rewriting wherever text is typed, across browser, desktop, and mobile. Ubiquity is the product: it works everywhere without changing how anyone works.
grammarly.engine: Proprietary language models, with third-party frontier models behind some generative features.

pricing.includes: Style guide, SSO, admin analytics, data controls

grammarly.quality: Excellent on mechanics and clarity. Style suggestions can flatten distinctive voice if accepted uncritically.
grammarly.tagline: Writing assistance almost everyone already has installed, reading almost everything they type.
use_cases: Correctness and tone consistency across all business writing
Enforcing a house style guide across a large team
Non-native English speakers producing publication-quality writing
grammarly.governance_note: The exposure here is breadth, not depth. A browser extension with permission to read and modify text sees drafts of everything: board material, legal correspondence, HR matters, client data, and anything typed into an internal system. It is frequently installed by individuals on the free tier and so never appears in a vendor review. Two practical controls: manage the extension through browser policy rather than leaving it to individuals, and confirm which tier the organization is actually running, because free and enterprise carry materially different terms.
grammarly.training_optout: Business and enterprise tiers carry stronger data commitments than the free tier. Verify which applies to the seats actually deployed.

cons: Lawyer review remains mandatory before any client-facing use
Privilege policy must be confirmed for the specific data path
harvey-ai.name: Harvey AI
pros: Legal-domain specificity rather than general adaptation
Data terms designed for client matter sensitivity
harvey-ai.files: Legal documents: contracts, filings, case documents, and statutory text.
harvey-ai.value: Legal-domain AI built for law firms rather than adapted from a general assistant. Handles legal research, document drafting, contract review, and due diligence in the contexts a lawyer actually works in, not the contexts a general AI was trained on.
harvey-ai.engine: Built on frontier models (primarily OpenAI and Anthropic) with legal-domain fine-tuning and retrieval.
harvey-ai.latency: Fast enough for interactive research. Document review at scale is batch.

pricing.includes: Data controls, professional liability alignment, admin oversight

harvey-ai.quality: Strongest for legal English and legal reasoning. Outputs still require lawyer review before any client-facing use.
harvey-ai.tagline: AI for legal work, built specifically for law firms and legal departments.
use_cases: Legal research and issue spotting across case law and statutes
Due diligence document review at scale
integrations: Document management systems used in legal practice
harvey-ai.governance_note: The legal professional responsibility question is the same regardless of tool: a lawyer cannot delegate judgment to an AI, and outputs must be reviewed before they touch client work. What changes is which tasks can be accelerated. The professional liability point is that if Harvey produces a flawed contract clause and a lawyer submits it without review, the lawyer's error, not the vendor's. On the data side, privilege must be maintained for client matter inputs, which requires a confirmed data path under the firm's privilege policy, not just the vendor's standard terms.
harvey-ai.training_optout: Legal-grade data terms. Client matter data is not used to train models. Verify the DPA for your jurisdiction.

headliner.name: Headliner
headliner.value: Headliner turns podcast audio into shareable videos with waveforms, captions and artwork, and now picks clips automatically. It is the podcast marketer's tool and integrates with podcast hosts.
headliner.tagline: Audiograms and podcast promotion videos with captions and waveforms, plus an AI podcast clipper.

imovie-ai.name: iMovie AI
imovie-ai.value: iMovie is the editor on every Mac, iPhone and iPad, and its magic movie feature picks clips, adds music and titles from a selection of footage. It is the starting point for Apple users before Final Cut.
imovie-ai.tagline: Apple's free consumer editor with magic movie and storyboard modes that assemble a video automatically.
imovie-ai.governance_note: Local processing; nothing to review beyond device policy.

inshot-ai.name: InShot AI
inshot-ai.value: InShot is one of the most downloaded mobile editors, with AI cutout, auto captions and effects for social clips. It is a CapCut alternative for people who want a simpler, less ByteDance tied app.
inshot-ai.tagline: Popular mobile editor with AI background removal, captions, effects and music matching.

langchain.api: Python and JavaScript libraries. LangSmith for observability.
cons: Can become complex and hard to debug for sophisticated agent patterns
LlamaIndex is often simpler for pure document RAG
Rapid release cadence means documentation can lag code
langchain.name: LangChain
pros: Dominant ecosystem with extensive documentation and community
Broadest integration surface in the category
LangSmith provides production monitoring and evaluation
langchain.files: Loaders for PDF, web, code, and database content. Integrations for all major vector stores.
langchain.value: The dominant Python framework for building LLM-powered applications: chains, agents, RAG pipelines, and tool use. More general-purpose than LlamaIndex, with a broader integration surface. Most LLM application tutorials and patterns assume LangChain.
langchain.engine: Framework. Orchestrates calls to models, vector stores, and tools from any provider.
langchain.latency: Framework overhead is minimal. Latency dominated by model and store calls.

pricing.includes: Tracing, evaluation, and monitoring for LLM applications

langchain.quality: Very broad integration coverage. Can become complex quickly; LlamaIndex is often simpler for pure RAG use cases.
langchain.tagline: The most widely used framework for building LLM applications, and the one most documentation assumes you are using.
use_cases: Building LLM applications that chain multiple model calls, tools, and data sources
Agent orchestration where the model selects which tools to call
RAG pipelines combining retrieval, reranking, and generation
integrations: Tool integrations across search, code execution, and external APIs
langchain.governance_note: LangChain is the plumbing, not the policy. The governance surface of an application built on LangChain is the model it calls, the data it retrieves, and the tools it executes. LangSmith is the monitoring layer that makes those calls visible. The audit question for a LangChain-based application is the same as for any LLM application: what can the agent call, what data can it access, and what is the review process before it takes actions with consequences.
langchain.training_optout: Framework only. Data handling is entirely determined by the model and store providers chosen.

langsmith.api: Python and JavaScript SDKs; OpenTelemetry endpoint; REST API.
cons: Seat-based pricing means the bill scales with team size, not just traffic, and per-trace overage stacks on top at production volume
Closed source; self-hosting requires an Enterprise contract
Teams not on LangChain get a thinner experience than the marketing implies
Long retention is a paid add-on rather than the default
langsmith.name: LangSmith
pros: Unmatched trace depth for LangChain and LangGraph, with near-zero instrumentation effort
Observability, evaluation, prompt management, and human review in one product
OpenTelemetry support means non-LangChain services can still report in
langsmith.files: Datasets for evaluation, prompt versions, and annotation queues are first-class objects.
langsmith.value: Captures every LLM call, tool call, retrieval step, and agent decision as a nested trace you can replay, with latency and token cost at each step. Beyond tracing it carries evaluation against datasets, online LLM-as-judge scoring of live traffic, prompt versioning, and annotation queues for structured human review. It is framework-agnostic on paper and ships OpenTelemetry support, but the product is built LangChain-first: instrument a LangGraph agent and the node graph, per-step state, and deploy path line up with almost no glue code. Instrument something else over OpenTelemetry and it works, with less of what makes the platform distinctive.
langsmith.engine: Managed SaaS. Tracing SDKs plus OpenTelemetry ingest.
langsmith.latency: Tracing is asynchronous and out of the request path; the SDK failure mode is lost telemetry rather than a failed call.

pricing.limits: Single user; trace allowance with short default retention

pricing.model: $39 per seat per month plus usage
pricing.limits: Included trace allowance, then per-trace overage; extended retention costs more
pricing.includes: Team seats, evaluation datasets, prompt versioning, longer retention
Self-hosted and bring-your-own-cloud deployment, SSO, procurement terms

langsmith.quality: The richest trace detail available for LangChain and LangGraph applications, including agent graph visualisation and replay. Monitoring dashboards cover token usage, P50/P99 latency, error rates, and cost, with webhook and PagerDuty alerting.
langsmith.tagline: A flight recorder for multi-step LLM applications, deepest if you build on LangChain and workable if you do not.
use_cases: Debugging why a multi-step agent produced the wrong answer, step by step
Gating releases on evaluation runs against a curated dataset
Watching production latency, token spend, and error rates per model and per step
Routing failed traces to human reviewers and turning them into test cases
integrations: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Vercel AI SDKs
langsmith.governance_note: Traces are the audit trail for an AI application, which makes an observability platform a data-residency decision rather than a developer convenience. Prompts and completions frequently contain the most sensitive text an organisation handles, and by default they leave your environment for the vendor cloud. Confirm what is captured, whether payloads can be redacted at the SDK before egress, how long traces are retained, and whether your retention needs push you to an Enterprise contract. The governance value is real once configured: per-step cost and latency, error rates, and evaluation scores are exactly the evidence an AI audit asks for and most teams cannot produce.
langsmith.training_optout: Trace content is customer data under the vendor agreement. Verify current terms directly; do not assume telemetry is excluded from any downstream use.

cons: Slower than GPU servers at scale
llama-cpp.name: llama.cpp
llama-cpp.value: llama.cpp made local LLMs practical by running quantised models efficiently on consumer hardware, and its GGUF format became the standard for local models, used by Ollama, LM Studio and many others. It is maintained by a large open source community.
llama-cpp.tagline: The C++ inference engine that runs quantised LLMs on laptops, phones and servers without a GPU.
llama-cpp.governance_note: Fully local; the only review is model licences and keeping the engine updated for security fixes.

logseq-ai.name: Logseq AI
logseq-ai.value: Logseq is an open source, local first outliner with bidirectional links, and community plugins add AI assistance using cloud or local models. It appeals to users who want open source rather than Obsidian's closed app.
logseq-ai.engine: Plugins calling cloud APIs or local models.
logseq-ai.tagline: Open source outliner notes with plugins for AI chat and summarisation, privacy first like Obsidian.
logseq-ai.governance_note: Same plugin data path rule as Obsidian.

monday-ai.name: Monday.com AI
pros: CRM and dev products share it
monday-ai.value: monday.com adds AI to boards: categorising, summarising, extracting from documents, drafting and now agents that handle multi step work, priced by credits on top of seats. It suits teams running operations on monday boards.
monday-ai.tagline: AI blocks, agents and automations in monday.com's work OS, with a credit based model.
monday-ai.governance_note: Admins control AI availability; credits need budget ownership.
monday-ai.training_optout: monday.com does not train on customer data.

moveworks.name: Moveworks
moveworks.value: Moveworks resolves employee requests across systems through chat in Slack and Teams, and ServiceNow bought it to become the front end of its own workflows. It was the category leader for employee facing AI service.
moveworks.tagline: Employee AI assistant for IT and HR support, acquired by ServiceNow in 2025.
use_cases: IT and HR requests in chat
moveworks.governance_note: Same permission and audit rule as Aisera.
moveworks.training_optout: Moveworks does not train on customer data.

notion-ai.api: Notion API for workspace content; AI features are primarily in-product.
cons: Only as good as the documentation behind it
Inherits permissive sharing as a disclosure path
Depends on third-party models, so read the sub-processor list
notion-ai.name: Notion AI
pros: Answers from the organization's own documented knowledge
No context switch out of the working document
notion-ai.files: Workspace pages and databases, plus uploaded files and connected sources.
notion-ai.value: Writes, summarises, and answers questions against the organization's own Notion content, respecting existing page permissions. Most useful precisely where a company has already committed its documentation to Notion.
notion-ai.engine: Third-party frontier models operating over Notion workspace content.
notion-ai.latency: Fast for in-page work; retrieval across a large workspace is slower.
notion-ai.quality: Good at summarising and drafting from source pages. Answer quality is bounded by documentation quality, so a messy workspace produces confident answers from stale pages.
notion-ai.tagline: AI inside the workspace, answering from the company's own pages.
use_cases: Answering questions from internal documentation without hunting for the page
Drafting and summarising directly inside working documents
Turning meeting notes into structured, actionable records
integrations: Connectors to common storage and communication tools
notion-ai.governance_note: Two points. First, it inherits Notion page permissions, so it will answer from anything the asking user can already open, which turns permissive workspace sharing into an information-disclosure route. Second, answers are only as current as the pages behind them: a superseded policy page will be quoted back with full confidence. Documentation hygiene becomes a control, not just housekeeping.
notion-ai.training_optout: Notion states customer data is not used to train models. Because generation runs on third-party models, the sub-processor list is the thing to read, not just the headline commitment.

cons: Answer quality depends on doc hygiene
notion-qa.name: Notion Q&A
notion-qa.value: Q and A lets a team ask questions of everything in their Notion workspace and connected tools and get cited answers, and Notion AI grew to include meeting notes, writing and enterprise search over Slack, Drive and more. It is bundled into Notion's business plans.

pricing.includes: Notion AI with Q and A

notion-qa.tagline: Notion AI's question answering over a workspace, now part of a broader Notion AI with meeting notes and search across tools.
notion-qa.governance_note: Q and A respects page permissions; connectors widen what the AI can see, so review them.
notion-qa.training_optout: Notion does not train on customer data.

cons: Generated backgrounds can mislead on product scale
photoroom.name: Photoroom
photoroom.value: Photoroom turns phone photos of products into marketplace ready images, with background removal, generated scenes, retouching and bulk editing, plus an API used by marketplaces themselves. It is the ecommerce seller's tool.
photoroom.engine: Photoroom's own segmentation and generation models.
photoroom.tagline: Product photo editing for sellers: background removal, AI backgrounds, shadows and batch processing.
photoroom.governance_note: Generated scenes must not misrepresent the product; marketplace rules on AI altered images apply.

promptfoo.name: Promptfoo
promptfoo.value: Promptfoo runs prompts against models and test cases from a config file, compares outputs, and includes a red teaming suite that probes applications for jailbreaks, injection and data leakage, with an enterprise version for teams. It is widely used in CI pipelines.
promptfoo.tagline: Open source tool for testing prompts, evaluating LLM outputs and red teaming applications for security.
promptfoo.governance_note: Red team reports are evidence for secure AI development obligations; run them before release and on model changes.

remove-bg.name: Remove.bg
remove-bg.value: Remove.bg does one thing, removes backgrounds from images, and does it through a web page, desktop app, API and plugins for Photoshop and ecommerce platforms. Canva acquired it with Kaleido in 2021 and uses the technology inside Canva.
remove-bg.tagline: The one click background removal service, now owned by Canva, with an API and plugins.
remove-bg.governance_note: Uploads are processed in the cloud; Canva terms apply.

replicate.api: Yes. REST API with client libraries and webhooks.
cons: Community models vary in quality and licence
Cold starts on less popular models
Not a place for closed frontier LLMs
replicate.name: Replicate
pros: Enormous catalogue of ready to run models
Versioned model APIs that do not change under you
Good for media generation that LLM hosts ignore
replicate.files: Model inputs by model: images, audio, video, text.
replicate.value: Replicate is where developers go to run a model someone else published without setting up GPUs: thousands of community models, each with a versioned API, pay by the second. It is strongest for image, video and audio generation, where the open model ecosystem is richest.
replicate.engine: Community and vendor published open models, packaged with Cog and run on Replicate's GPU fleet.
replicate.latency: Warm models respond quickly; cold starts can take tens of seconds.

pricing.limits: Per second of compute by hardware

replicate.quality: Depends entirely on the model; the platform is reliable.
replicate.tagline: Run open source models, especially image, video and audio, from a one line API call.
use_cases: Adding image or video generation to an app
Trying a research model without a GPU
Serving your own model with Cog
integrations: Python, JavaScript and other client libraries
replicate.governance_note: Each model on Replicate carries its own licence, and some are research only or non commercial. The licence check is per model, every time, and the platform does not do it for you.
replicate.training_optout: Replicate does not train on your inputs. Model authors cannot see them either. Confirm in the current terms.

sambanova.name: SambaNova
sambanova.value: SambaNova runs Llama, DeepSeek and other open models on its reconfigurable dataflow chips, sold as a fast inference cloud with an OpenAI compatible API and as on premises systems for sovereign deployments. It competes with Groq and Cerebras.
sambanova.engine: Open models on SambaNova RDU hardware.
sambanova.quality: As good as the model chosen.
sambanova.tagline: AI chip company serving open models at high speed through its cloud and selling racks to enterprises and governments.
sambanova.governance_note: Confirm data retention on the cloud tier; on premises answers residency.
sambanova.training_optout: SambaNova states API data is not used for training; confirm.

sap-joule.name: SAP Joule
sap-joule.value: Joule answers questions, navigates transactions and runs agents inside SAP applications, with the business context those systems hold, and SAP is positioning it as the single assistant across finance, HR, procurement and supply chain. It is included in SAP's premium cloud contracts.
sap-joule.engine: Partner LLMs including OpenAI, Anthropic and Mistral through SAP's generative AI hub.

pricing.tier: Included with RISE and GROW premium

sap-joule.quality: Good where SAP data is clean.
sap-joule.tagline: SAP's AI copilot and agent layer across S/4HANA, SuccessFactors, Ariba and the rest of its cloud suite.
sap-joule.governance_note: Agents acting in the ERP touch financial records; SOX controls, segregation of duties and audit logging apply to agent actions as to users.
sap-joule.training_optout: SAP does not use customer data to train models.

sketch-ai.name: Sketch AI
pros: Lower cost than Figma for small teams
sketch-ai.value: Sketch added AI helpers for layer naming, content and image generation while keeping its position as the Mac native, locally stored design tool. It appeals to teams that want files on their own machines.
sketch-ai.engine: Partner models with local file handling.
sketch-ai.tagline: Mac native design tool with AI assist features, the privacy focused alternative to Figma.
sketch-ai.governance_note: Local files answer residency; AI features still call partner models, so check what leaves the machine.

cons: Not for cinematic or creative work
synthesia.name: Synthesia
pros: Fastest way to localise a presenter video
synthesia.value: Synthesia is the enterprise standard for avatar videos, used for training, onboarding and internal communication where a human presenter would be filmed again every time the script changed. It leads on languages, custom avatars of real employees and enterprise controls.
synthesia.engine: Synthesia's own avatar, voice and translation models.
synthesia.tagline: Avatar video for training and communication: type a script, pick a presenter, get a video in 140 languages.
synthesia.governance_note: Custom avatars require filmed consent from the person, which Synthesia enforces; your policy should also say when an avatar may be used after the person leaves. Label avatar videos as synthetic where the audience could be misled.
synthesia.training_optout: Enterprise terms exclude training on customer content; confirm for lower tiers.

tempus-ai.name: Tempus AI
tempus-ai.value: Tempus sequences tumours, structures clinical records and applies AI to match patients to treatments and trials, selling to hospitals and pharma, and listed on Nasdaq in 2024. It is one of the largest clinical AI data businesses.
tempus-ai.engine: Tempus's own models over its data platform.
tempus-ai.tagline: Precision medicine company using AI over clinical and molecular data for oncology diagnostics and trial matching.
tempus-ai.governance_note: De identified patient data licensing to pharma is lawful under HIPAA but raises consent questions that health systems should address with patients.

trello-ai.name: Trello AI
trello-ai.value: Trello's AI summarises card descriptions and comments, drafts content and, with the inbox feature, turns forwarded emails and notes into cards. It is a light layer on a simple tool.
trello-ai.tagline: Atlassian Intelligence in Trello for card summaries, drafting and turning messy notes into tasks.
use_cases: Personal and small team task capture
trello-ai.training_optout: Atlassian does not train on customer data.

uipath-ai.api: UiPath API for management and integration.
cons: AI exception handling requires accuracy testing before reducing human review
AI decision errors propagate at robot speed
uipath-ai.name: UiPath AI
pros: AI enhances existing robot fleet without rebuilding workflows
Strong document understanding for high-volume processing
Process mining identifies automation ROI before building
uipath-ai.files: Documents, forms, images, and process logs within the UiPath platform.
uipath-ai.value: AI capabilities embedded in UiPath's RPA platform: document understanding, process mining, and AI-powered decision steps within robotic workflows. For organizations already running UiPath for automation, this adds AI to the existing robot fleet without rebuilding the workflow layer.
uipath-ai.engine: UiPath's own document AI models plus frontier model integration for unstructured tasks.
uipath-ai.latency: Async for batch document processing; near-real-time for inline robot decision steps.

pricing.includes: AI features within the UiPath platform licence

uipath-ai.quality: Strong for document understanding at scale. AI exception handling requires careful accuracy testing before removing human review.
uipath-ai.tagline: AI across the enterprise RPA platform, adding judgment to robotic process automation.
use_cases: Adding document understanding and extraction to existing RPA workflows
AI-powered exception handling in robotic processes that used to require human review
Process mining to identify automation opportunities using AI pattern detection
integrations: Full UiPath platform: Studio, Orchestrator, Insights
uipath-ai.governance_note: RPA governance predates AI governance, and for good reason: a robot that executes the wrong process at scale does damage faster than a human making the same mistake. Adding AI decision steps to an RPA workflow amplifies the risk: the robot now acts on an AI judgment, and if the AI is wrong, the robot acts on it thousands of times. The audit requirement is: which AI decision steps in which robots require human review before downstream action, and what is the fallback if the AI is uncertain. Those policies belong in the robot design, not the exception queue.
uipath-ai.training_optout: UiPath's enterprise terms govern. Models are licensed and deployed within the customer's platform tenancy.

v0-vercel.api: Yes. The v0 model is available through Vercel's AI gateway for your own tools.
cons: Tied to the Vercel ecosystem by design
v0-vercel.name: v0 (Vercel)
pros: Output matches the Next.js and shadcn conventions a Vercel team already uses
A model API for building your own generator
v0-vercel.files: Images, screenshots and Figma frames as input; code exports to GitHub.
v0-vercel.value: v0 started as a component generator and became a full app builder, tuned to Vercel's own stack: Next.js, shadcn/ui, Tailwind, deployed on Vercel. For a team already on that stack it produces code that looks like code they would write, which is its advantage over generic builders.
v0-vercel.engine: Vercel's own fine tuned models plus frontier models, behind the AI SDK.
v0-vercel.latency: Fast for components; full app generation takes minutes.
v0-vercel.quality: The best looking front end output of the builders when you want shadcn style; backend code is thinner.
v0-vercel.tagline: Vercel's generative UI tool that writes React and Next.js from a prompt and deploys to Vercel.
use_cases: Front end components and pages for a Next.js app
Design to code from a screenshot or Figma frame
integrations: Supabase and other Vercel marketplace integrations
v0-vercel.governance_note: Lock in is the governance question here, not safety: the output assumes Vercel hosting. That is fine if you are already there and a migration cost if you are not.
v0-vercel.training_optout: Vercel's terms exclude training on customer code for paid and enterprise plans; confirm for the free tier.

videoleap.api: No for the app; LTX models are open.
videoleap.name: Videoleap
videoleap.value: Videoleap is a creative mobile editor from Lightricks, the Facetune company, with AI transformations, text to video and template effects. Lightricks also released the open LTX video model, which gives the app a generation engine of its own.
videoleap.engine: Lightricks LTX video models and licensed effects.
videoleap.tagline: Lightricks' mobile editor with AI effects, text to video and the LTX video model behind it.
use_cases: Text to video experiments on mobile
videoleap.governance_note: Consumer app; standard synthetic labelling for generated content.

vizard-ai.name: Vizard AI
vizard-ai.value: Vizard competes with OpusClip on clip selection and adds automatic subtitles, speaker framing and a simple editor for fixing cuts. It is priced for creators and small marketing teams.
vizard-ai.tagline: Long to short video clipping with captions and speaker tracking, a close OpusClip rival.
vizard-ai.governance_note: Same approval rule as OpusClip for auto posting.

cons: Complex agents get hard to maintain
voiceflow.name: Voiceflow
pros: Mixes guardrailed flows with LLM freedom
Collaboration features for designers and developers
voiceflow.files: Knowledge base upload from documents and URLs.
voiceflow.value: Voiceflow started as a builder for Alexa and Google voice apps and became a platform for customer facing chat and voice agents, mixing deterministic flows with LLM steps and a knowledge base. Support and CX teams use it to build agents that follow policy where it matters and improvise where it is safe.
voiceflow.engine: Model of your choice for LLM steps; Voiceflow's own runtime for flows.
voiceflow.latency: Fast for flows; model bound for LLM steps.
voiceflow.quality: Strong for designed conversations; open ended quality is the model's.
voiceflow.tagline: A design and build platform for conversational AI agents, from scripted flows to LLM powered support bots.
use_cases: Customer support agents with policy bound answers
voiceflow.governance_note: The flow versus LLM split is a governance tool: anything with a legal or financial consequence belongs in a deterministic flow, and the LLM steps handle phrasing. Log transcripts and keep a human escalation path.
voiceflow.training_optout: Voiceflow does not train on customer data; model calls follow each provider's terms. Confirm in the current terms.

wayground.name: Wayground
wayground.value: Wayground is the renamed Quizizz, where teachers create or generate quizzes, lessons and flashcards, run them live or as homework and get analytics. Its AI generates questions from text, PDFs or topics and adapts difficulty.
wayground.status: Active. Quizizz rebranded to Wayground in 2025.
wayground.tagline: Formerly Quizizz, the classroom quiz and lesson platform with AI generated questions and adaptive features.
wayground.governance_note: Student data platform; check the district data agreement and COPPA and FERPA terms before use.
wayground.training_optout: Education accounts are covered by student privacy terms; confirm.

zapier-ai.api: Zapier API for programmatic Zap management.
cons: Automation continues running when context changes
Sub-processor chain for the model step needs tracking
Quality depends on the model behind the AI step
zapier-ai.name: Zapier AI
pros: No-code AI automation accessible to non-developers
Existing Zapier workflows gain AI steps without rebuilding
zapier-ai.files: Handles the data formats and payloads of the connected apps.
zapier-ai.value: Adds text-driven automation and AI actions to the workflows most organizations already run in Zapier. The value is the integration surface, 7,000-plus apps, not any particular model capability.
zapier-ai.engine: Routes to third-party models (primarily OpenAI) through Zapier's action layer.
zapier-ai.latency: Async by nature, suited to background automation rather than interactive use.

pricing.model: Per-task pricing within existing Zapier pricing

zapier-ai.quality: Quality of the AI step depends on the underlying model. Value is in the connectivity, not the model.
zapier-ai.tagline: AI layered on top of Zapier's automation network: 7,000 apps, text inputs, no code.
use_cases: Building AI-powered automations across SaaS tools without code
Routing, classifying, and acting on incoming data through natural language steps
Connecting AI outputs to downstream systems without building custom integrations
zapier-ai.governance_note: Automation tools have a specific failure mode: they keep running when the world changes. An AI automation approved in one context will continue executing months later when the data, the counterparties, or the policy have shifted. Human review checkpoints must be designed in from the start, not added when something goes wrong. The audit question is not whether the automation worked today but whether anyone would know if it stopped working correctly.
zapier-ai.training_optout: Follows OpenAI and any other sub-processor's terms for the model step. Zapier itself operates under its own data terms. Both matter.

alphasense.api: API for data access and search integration.
cons: Limited to documents in its corpus
Content licence terms govern downstream use of outputs
alphasense.name: AlphaSense
pros: Finance-specific document corpus already licensed and curated
Strong synthesis across earnings call and filing types
Faster than manual research across many documents
alphasense.files: AlphaSense's curated document library: filings, call transcripts, broker research.
alphasense.value: Market intelligence platform that searches and summarizes across a curated set of financial documents: earnings calls, SEC filings, broker research, news, and industry reports. AI synthesis across those sources is the primary value.
alphasense.engine: Proprietary search and summarization models, finance-domain tuned.
alphasense.latency: Fast search. Synthesis of larger document sets takes more time.

pricing.includes: Full platform access including premium content

alphasense.quality: Strong on the specific document types it indexes. Limited to its own corpus.
alphasense.tagline: AI search and analysis across earnings calls, filings, broker research, and news.
use_cases: Rapid synthesis of earnings call themes across a sector
SEC filing and broker research search without reading every document
Competitive intelligence from public and premium financial sources
integrations: Corporate research and financial analysis workflows
alphasense.governance_note: The MNPI and information-barrier questions apply here as they do to all finance research AI. The specific AlphaSense risk is the premium content layer: broker research and licensed data sources require that usage stays within the permitted scope of the underlying content licences. Using AlphaSense outputs in ways that effectively redistribute licensed research without the underlying licence is a contractual issue that predates AI but that AI-speed synthesis makes easier to stumble into.
alphasense.training_optout: AlphaSense's terms govern. Queries stay within their platform.

alteryx-ai.name: Alteryx AI
alteryx-ai.value: Alteryx added AI to its workflow designer so analysts can describe transformations in plain language, get documentation and insights generated, and use LLM tools inside workflows. It serves finance and operations analysts who automate reporting.
alteryx-ai.tagline: AI in Alteryx's analytics automation: natural language workflow building, data preparation and insight generation.
alteryx-ai.governance_note: Workflows are auditable artefacts; AI generated steps should be reviewed like any other logic in a financial process.
alteryx-ai.training_optout: Alteryx does not train on customer data.

assemblyai.name: AssemblyAI
assemblyai.files: Audio and video files or streams.
assemblyai.value: AssemblyAI is a developer API for transcription and audio intelligence: speaker diarisation, PII redaction, sentiment, chapters and a LeMUR layer for asking questions of transcripts. It competes with Deepgram and the cloud providers on accuracy and features.
assemblyai.tagline: Speech to text API with speaker labels, PII redaction and LLM features over transcripts.
assemblyai.governance_note: Transcripts of calls are personal data; use the redaction feature and set retention to zero where offered.
assemblyai.training_optout: AssemblyAI does not train on customer data by default; confirm.

be-my-eyes.name: Be My Eyes
be-my-eyes.value: Be My Eyes added Be My AI, built on GPT-4 vision, so users can photograph anything and get a description and conversation about it, alongside the human volunteer network that made the app. It is the reference accessibility use of multimodal AI.
be-my-eyes.tagline: App connecting blind and low vision users to volunteers, with an AI mode that describes images and answers questions about them.
be-my-eyes.governance_note: Images may include other people and private information; the app's terms and OpenAI's data handling apply.
be-my-eyes.training_optout: Be My Eyes states images are not used to train models; confirm.

blue-prism.api: Yes. Control room and process APIs.
cons: AI features arrived later than competitors
blue-prism.name: Blue Prism
pros: Strongest governance model among RPA vendors
SS&C ownership brings financial services domain tooling
blue-prism.files: Documents through document intelligence; application data through processes.
blue-prism.value: Blue Prism coined the term robotic process automation and built the governance heavy, IT owned model of it: a digital workforce managed centrally with audit trails and release controls. SS&C bought it in 2022 and has added document intelligence and generative AI connectors, selling mostly into financial services and healthcare.
blue-prism.engine: Its own RPA runtime; AI through connectors to Microsoft, AWS, Google and SS&C's own services.
blue-prism.quality: Reliable for defined processes; AI connectors are as good as the service behind them.
blue-prism.tagline: The original enterprise RPA platform, now part of SS&C and extended with AI document processing and agents.
use_cases: Regulated back office processes with audit requirements
integrations: Microsoft Azure AI, AWS, Google AI
blue-prism.governance_note: Blue Prism's model is built for audit: every process is versioned, every run is logged, and credentials sit in a vault. The governance work is in deciding which steps may call a model and how the output is validated before the bot acts on it.
blue-prism.training_optout: Enterprise terms exclude training on customer data; AI connector terms belong to the service used.

braintrust.name: Braintrust
braintrust.value: Braintrust lets teams build eval datasets, score outputs with code or model graders, trace production, and iterate prompts in a playground, with a focus on fast loops for product teams. It is a leader among the LLM evaluation platforms.
braintrust.tagline: Evaluation and observability platform for AI products, with datasets, scorers, tracing and prompt playgrounds.
braintrust.governance_note: Eval results are governance evidence; traces contain customer data and need retention rules.
braintrust.training_optout: Braintrust does not train on customer data.

clearscope.name: Clearscope
clearscope.value: Clearscope grades drafts against the terms top ranking pages use and produces briefs and audits, with a cleaner, more conservative approach than Surfer and a reputation among large publishers. It added AI drafting later and lightly.
clearscope.tagline: Content optimisation with term grading and reports, favoured by enterprise content teams.
clearscope.governance_note: Same editorial review rule as Surfer.

clickup-ai.name: ClickUp AI
clickup-ai.value: ClickUp Brain answers questions across the workspace and connected tools, writes and summarises, takes meeting notes with its AI notetaker, and runs agents, bundled with ClickUp's all in one positioning. It is priced as an add on per user.
clickup-ai.tagline: ClickUp Brain: AI across tasks, docs and chat, with agents, meeting notes and enterprise search in one workspace.
clickup-ai.governance_note: Model choice means data may go to different vendors; set the allowed models in admin.
clickup-ai.training_optout: ClickUp does not train on customer data.

cohere-api.name: Cohere API
cohere-api.value: Cohere's API is built for enterprise RAG and agents: Command models for generation with citations, Embed for multilingual search and Rerank to improve retrieval, available on its own cloud, AWS, Azure, Oracle and private deployments. It is the vendor neutral choice for search quality.
cohere-api.tagline: Cohere's Command, Embed and Rerank models by API, with deployment in any cloud or on premises.
cohere-api.governance_note: Private deployment options answer residency; Cohere does not train on customer data.
cohere-api.training_optout: Cohere does not train on customer data.

dropbox-ai.name: Dropbox AI
dropbox-ai.value: Dropbox Dash searches and answers questions across Dropbox, Google, Microsoft, Slack and other connected tools, and Dropbox AI summarises files and answers questions about them. Dash is Dropbox's bet on universal search.
dropbox-ai.tagline: Dropbox Dash: AI search and answers across Dropbox and connected apps, plus file summaries.
dropbox-ai.governance_note: Connectors widen AI visibility; scope them.
dropbox-ai.training_optout: Dropbox does not train on customer content.

elevenlabs.api: REST API with SDKs, including low-latency streaming.
cons: Voice cloning carries real and rising legal exposure
Character-based pricing escalates with long-form use
Free tier prohibits commercial use, which is easy to miss
elevenlabs.name: ElevenLabs
elevenlabs.files: Text in, audio out. Accepts reference audio for cloning and existing media for dubbing.
elevenlabs.value: Produces synthetic speech convincing enough for commercial publication, with multilingual output and voice cloning from short samples. The realism is the product and the risk in equal measure.
elevenlabs.engine: Proprietary speech synthesis and voice cloning models.
elevenlabs.latency: Fast enough for near real-time use in the low-latency modes.
elevenlabs.quality: The realism benchmark for the category. Long-form prosody and unusual proper nouns remain the weak points.
elevenlabs.tagline: The quality leader in synthetic speech, and a live example of why voice needs governance.
use_cases: Narration for training, marketing, and product content at scale
Dubbing existing content into other languages while keeping the speaker's voice
Accessibility, turning written material into audio
elevenlabs.governance_note: This is the tool most likely to create legal exposure through ordinary use. Cloning a voice requires the speaker's consent, several jurisdictions now regulate synthetic likeness directly, and Tennessee's ELVIS Act is one example already covered in the governance library. Consent capture and provenance labelling belong in the workflow from day one, not after the first complaint.
elevenlabs.training_optout: Enterprise agreements address data use. Verify terms before uploading any voice you do not own.

cons: Behind Llama and Qwen on benchmarks
falcon-tii.name: Falcon
falcon-tii.value: Falcon put the UAE on the open model map with a 180 billion parameter release in 2023 and continued with smaller efficient families, including hybrid architectures, under permissive licences. It is a sovereign AI programme with research credibility.
falcon-tii.tagline: Open models from Abu Dhabi's TII, from the early 180B release to the efficient Falcon 3 and Falcon H1 families.
use_cases: Self hosted assistants in the Gulf region
falcon-tii.governance_note: Licence is permissive; sovereignty narrative matters for buyers in the region.

fiddler-ai.name: Fiddler AI
pros: LLM and classic ML in one
fiddler-ai.value: Fiddler explains model predictions, monitors drift and fairness, and added LLM observability and guardrails with its own trust models, selling to banks, insurers and healthcare. It is a leading independent in model monitoring.
fiddler-ai.tagline: AI observability platform for explainability, monitoring and LLM guardrails in regulated industries.
fiddler-ai.governance_note: Explanations support adverse action notices and model validation; keep the configuration under change control.
fiddler-ai.training_optout: Fiddler does not train on customer data.

cons: AI credits on top of licence
filmora-ai.name: Filmora AI
filmora-ai.value: Filmora is Wondershare's mainstream editor, between iMovie and Premiere in complexity, with AI features for cutting, masking, music, captions and an assistant that suggests edits. It sells to hobbyists and small businesses.
filmora-ai.tagline: Consumer video editor with AI copilot, smart cutout, text based editing and generative effects.
filmora-ai.governance_note: Cloud AI features upload media; keep confidential footage to local features.

freepik-ai.name: Freepik AI
freepik-ai.value: Freepik added an AI suite over its stock catalogue: generation from Flux, Mystic, Imagen and others, video from the leading models, upscaling, retouching and a designer. It is the aggregator with a stock licence behind it.
freepik-ai.engine: Aggregated third party models plus Freepik's Mystic model.
freepik-ai.quality: As good as the model chosen.
freepik-ai.tagline: Stock library turned AI suite, with image, video and voice generation from many models in one subscription.
freepik-ai.governance_note: Know which model processed an asset; the licence and training data story differ per model behind the single interface.

gradescope.name: Gradescope
gradescope.value: Gradescope scans paper and digital work, uses AI to group similar handwritten and typed answers for batch grading, autogrades code and bubble sheets, and gives rubric analytics, widely used in universities. Turnitin acquired it in 2018.
gradescope.engine: Gradescope's answer grouping and recognition models.
gradescope.tagline: Grading platform that groups similar answers with AI so instructors grade once and apply everywhere, owned by Turnitin.
gradescope.governance_note: AI grouping suggests, the instructor grades; keep that division visible in policy. Student work is retained under Turnitin's terms.

hyperwrite.name: HyperWrite
hyperwrite.value: HyperWrite started as a writing extension, built one of the first consumer browsing agents, and settled into a personal assistant for research, drafting and document work with a Chrome extension. It is a small player with a loyal base.
hyperwrite.tagline: Writing assistant with an early web browsing agent, now a personal AI for research and drafting.
hyperwrite.governance_note: Extension with browser access; consumer grade controls.

janitor-ai.name: Janitor AI
janitor-ai.value: Janitor AI hosts user created characters for roleplay chat, letting users bring their own model API key or use its hosted models, and grew out of the Character.ai audience wanting fewer content restrictions. It is a consumer entertainment product with adult content.
janitor-ai.engine: User supplied model APIs or Janitor's hosted models.
janitor-ai.tagline: Character chat platform where users create and talk to fictional personas, often with their own API keys.
janitor-ai.governance_note: Blocked on most corporate networks for content reasons; relevant to policy only as a category of consumer AI employees may use.

jasper-art.name: Jasper Art
jasper-art.value: Jasper Art lets marketing teams generate and edit campaign images in the same workspace as their copy, with brand style controls and licensed model backends. It is a convenience for Jasper customers rather than a standalone leader.
jasper-art.tagline: Image generation inside Jasper's marketing platform, tuned to brand kits and campaign workflows.
jasper-art.governance_note: Jasper's enterprise terms and brand controls apply; confirm which backend model generates images for indemnity purposes.
jasper-art.training_optout: Jasper states customer data is not used for training; confirm.

llama-meta.api: No first-party API. Served through whatever stack you choose or a third-party host.
cons: Community licence is not standard open source and has real conditions
Behind the frontier on hardest reasoning
Self-hosting demands infrastructure and ML capability
llama-meta.name: Llama (Meta)
llama-meta.files: Depends entirely on the serving stack chosen, not on the model distribution.
llama-meta.value: Removes the third-party data path entirely: weights can be run on infrastructure the organization controls. For regulated environments that is frequently the deciding factor, irrespective of benchmark position.
llama-meta.engine: Meta's own open-weight model family, released in several sizes.
llama-meta.latency: A function of the hardware it runs on. Smaller variants run acceptably on modest hardware; the largest need serious GPU capacity.

pricing.includes: Full weights, fine-tuning rights subject to licence
Managed inference from cloud and inference providers

llama-meta.quality: Competitive with proprietary models on many tasks, generally behind the frontier ones on the hardest reasoning. The trade is capability for control.
llama-meta.tagline: The most widely adopted open-weight model family, and the usual starting point for self-hosting.
use_cases: Running a capable model entirely inside a controlled environment
Fine-tuning on proprietary data without sending it to a vendor
Avoiding per-token costs at high, predictable volume
llama-meta.governance_note: The licence is a community licence, not a standard open-source licence. It carries conditions, including at very large user scale. Have counsel read it before building a commercial product on it rather than assuming MIT-style terms.
llama-meta.training_optout: Not applicable when self-hosted: the data never leaves your environment. That is the entire argument for this option.

llamaindex.api: Python library, TypeScript available. Extensive integration surface.
cons: Index access control is not automatic
Configuration choices strongly affect retrieval quality
llamaindex.name: LlamaIndex
pros: The right tool for document-centric RAG specifically
llamaindex.files: Loaders for PDFs, Word documents, spreadsheets, databases, and web pages.
llamaindex.value: The standard framework for connecting language models to private document stores. Where LangChain is more general-purpose, LlamaIndex is specifically optimized for the ingest-index-retrieve-generate pattern that makes RAG work well in practice.
llamaindex.engine: Framework, not a model. Orchestrates calls to whatever model and vector store you choose.
llamaindex.latency: Framework overhead is minimal; latency is dominated by the model and vector store.
llamaindex.quality: Retrieval quality depends heavily on chunking strategy and embedding model choice. LlamaIndex provides the plumbing; the quality decisions sit with the implementer.
llamaindex.tagline: The framework for building retrieval-augmented applications on top of your own documents.
use_cases: Building a knowledge assistant that answers questions from internal documents
Creating a retrieval layer that feeds context into a language model accurately
Ingesting heterogeneous sources (PDFs, databases, APIs) into a queryable index
integrations: Every major vector store and embedding provider
llamaindex.governance_note: The governance surface of a RAG system is the index, not the model. Whatever documents go in can come out in model responses, including documents that were accessible to the indexing process but should not be surfaced to end users. Access control on the index is not automatic and must be designed explicitly. The most common failure is indexing a shared drive and discovering that everyone can now query everyone else's sensitive files.
llamaindex.training_optout: Framework only. Data handling depends entirely on the model and store chosen.

lovo-genny.name: Lovo (Genny)
lovo-genny.value: Genny is Lovo's studio for voiceovers with a video timeline, subtitle tools and voice cloning across many languages, aimed at marketers and educators. It competes on language coverage and price.
lovo-genny.tagline: Text to speech and video editing studio, Genny, with a wide language and voice catalogue.

marketmuse.name: MarketMuse
marketmuse.value: MarketMuse analyses a site's content against a topic model to show where authority is thin, prioritises what to write, and generates briefs, operating at site strategy level rather than page level. It suits publishers planning content programmes.
marketmuse.engine: MarketMuse's topic models with partner LLMs.
marketmuse.tagline: Content strategy platform that maps topic authority and gaps across a whole site.
marketmuse.governance_note: Strategy tool; no content leaves except what you upload.

midjourney.api: No official public API. Automation depends on unofficial routes, which carry their own terms-of-service risk.
cons: No commercial indemnity comparable to Adobe's
midjourney.name: Midjourney
pros: Best output aesthetics in the category
midjourney.files: Text prompts plus image references for style and composition control.
midjourney.value: Consistently the strongest output aesthetics in the category. Chosen where the image has to look genuinely good rather than merely correct.
midjourney.engine: Proprietary image models. Not open weight.
midjourney.latency: Seconds per generation, typically several variants at once.

pricing.includes: More fast time, relaxed unlimited generation
Highest quotas, stealth mode on upper tiers

midjourney.quality: Best-in-class aesthetics. Weaker than peers at rendering legible text in images and at precise, literal instruction-following.
midjourney.tagline: The aesthetic leader in image generation, with the least clear commercial-use position.
use_cases: Concept art, mood boards, and campaign visual exploration
Marketing imagery where style consistency matters
Rapid visual iteration before commissioning real production
midjourney.governance_note: Two live issues. First, the public-by-default behaviour: staff experimenting with an unreleased product name or design are publishing it. Second, the training-data provenance question that image generators face collectively, which is the subject of ongoing litigation and which Midjourney has not resolved through licensing the way Adobe has. Where indemnity matters more than aesthetics, Firefly is the safer choice, and the reference library's copyright material is the place to start.
midjourney.training_optout: Generations are public by default on lower tiers. Private generation requires an upper tier. That default alone disqualifies it for confidential product work unless the tier is chosen deliberately.

neptune-ai.name: Neptune.ai
neptune-ai.value: Neptune tracks metrics, parameters and artefacts for training runs and optimised itself for foundation model scale, where runs log millions of points over weeks, with on premises deployment. It competes with Weights and Biases and Comet.
neptune-ai.tagline: Experiment tracker built for large scale model training runs, with fast logging and visualisation of long jobs.
neptune-ai.governance_note: Training logs are model provenance records; retain them for model cards and audits.
neptune-ai.training_optout: Neptune does not train on customer data.

cons: Consumer and Workspace data terms differ significantly
notebooklm.name: NotebookLM
pros: Closed-source reasoning dramatically reduces hallucination beyond the source set
Citations back to exact passages support verification
Audio overviews are a genuinely novel output format
notebooklm.files: PDF, Google Docs, Google Slides, web URLs, YouTube links, and pasted text.
notebooklm.value: Upload documents, paste text, or link sources, and NotebookLM answers questions, summarizes, and generates content grounded only on what you gave it, not on general training data. The closed-source property is the point.
notebooklm.engine: Google's Gemini models, operating over user-provided sources.
notebooklm.latency: Fast for question answering. Audio overview generation takes a few minutes.

pricing.includes: Notebooks up to 50 sources, 25M tokens per notebook

pricing.model: Per-seat monthly (Google One AI Premium or Workspace)
pricing.includes: More notebooks, higher limits, team sharing

notebooklm.quality: Strong citation accuracy back to source passages. Stays within sources rather than hallucinating beyond them.
notebooklm.tagline: Research assistant that reasons over documents you provide, not the web.
use_cases: Analyzing a set of documents without the model reasoning outside them
Research synthesis across multiple sources with citations back to the exact passage
Generating audio overviews (podcast format) from uploaded source material
integrations: Web and YouTube as source types
notebooklm.governance_note: The closed-source behavior is the main governance argument for it: the model's answers are grounded on what you uploaded and cite back to passages, which makes hallucination outside the source set much less likely. The remaining question is the data path: documents uploaded to the consumer product are under Google's consumer terms; the same documents in a Workspace deployment are under enterprise terms. Confidential material should only go into a Workspace-governed instance.
notebooklm.training_optout: Google's data terms apply. Consumer tier data handling differs from Workspace. Confirm before uploading confidential material.

nvidia-nim.name: NVIDIA NIM
nvidia-nim.value: NIM containers wrap models, NVIDIA's own and open ones, with optimised inference engines and standard APIs so enterprises can deploy them on premises or in any cloud with one command. They are the deployment layer of NVIDIA AI Enterprise.
nvidia-nim.engine: Any supported model with TensorRT and vLLM backends.
nvidia-nim.tagline: Prebuilt inference microservices that package optimised models as containers for any NVIDIA GPU deployment.
nvidia-nim.governance_note: Self hosted inference keeps data in house; the licence and model terms still apply per container.

cons: Also available through Azure, which splits the contract decision
openai-api.name: OpenAI API / GPT models
pros: Broadest model line from one vendor
The ecosystem's default; every library supports it
Zero data retention and enterprise terms available
openai-api.files: Files API for documents, images, audio and batch inputs.
openai-api.value: The OpenAI API is the reference interface: its request format is the one every other vendor imitates, and its model line, GPT, o series reasoning models, embeddings, speech and image generation, is the broadest from one vendor. Most production AI features in business software run on it or on something shaped like it.
openai-api.engine: OpenAI's GPT and o series models, plus embedding, audio, image and realtime models.
openai-api.latency: Varies by model; the reasoning models are slower by design.
openai-api.tagline: Programmatic access to OpenAI's models, the default API the rest of the industry copies.
use_cases: Any text, reasoning or multimodal feature in a product
Agents with tool calling and structured outputs
integrations: Azure OpenAI Service for Microsoft shops
openai-api.governance_note: The API terms differ from ChatGPT's consumer terms: API inputs are not used for training by default, and zero data retention is available on request. Write down which models and which data classes are approved, because the model line changes every few months and a deprecation notice is also a governance event.
openai-api.training_optout: API data is not used for training by default; zero data retention is available for eligible endpoints. Confirm the current terms.

cons: Not a text to speech tool
respeecher.name: Respeecher
respeecher.value: Respeecher converts one actor's performance into another voice, used in film and television to de age or recreate voices with estate permission, and its marketplace licenses voices for games and dubbing. Its Ukrainian team is known for an explicit consent and ethics policy.
respeecher.tagline: Speech to speech voice conversion for film, games and media, with a strict ethics process.
use_cases: Recreating a voice with estate permission
respeecher.governance_note: Respeecher's consent requirements are a model for any voice policy: written permission from the voice owner or estate, scope of use, and term.

cons: Optimising to a score can produce stuffed content
surfer-seo.name: Surfer SEO
surfer-seo.value: Surfer analyses the top results for a keyword and tells you the terms, length and structure to match, with an AI writer that drafts to the score and an audit tool for existing pages. It is the standard content optimisation tool for SEO teams.
surfer-seo.engine: Surfer's own ranking analysis plus partner LLMs.
surfer-seo.tagline: Content optimisation that scores pages against top ranking competitors and drafts articles to match.
surfer-seo.governance_note: Search engines penalise content written for scores rather than readers; keep editorial review.

tableau-ai.name: Tableau AI (Einstein)
