tableau-ai.value: Tableau's AI lets analysts build visualisations by asking, explains data, and Pulse delivers metric summaries in plain language to business users, through Salesforce's Einstein Trust Layer. It is included in Tableau+ and higher editions.
tableau-ai.tagline: Tableau Agent and Pulse: natural language analysis, generated insights and metric summaries in Tableau.
tableau-ai.governance_note: Generated insights inherit data permissions; verify numbers in any AI summary used in reporting.
tableau-ai.training_optout: Salesforce does not train on customer data.

workday-ai.name: Workday AI
workday-ai.value: Workday Illuminate powers the assistant and a growing set of agents across its HR and finance suite, trained on Workday's large transaction dataset, with an agent system of record to govern them. Workday sells agents as add ons.
workday-ai.tagline: Illuminate: Workday's AI for HR and finance, with agents for recruiting, expenses, payroll and contracts.
workday-ai.governance_note: Workday has been sued over alleged bias in applicant screening; any hiring agent needs bias audits and human decisions documented.
workday-ai.training_optout: Customers can opt out of contributing data to Workday's shared models.

cons: Palmyra trails frontier models on hard tasks
writer-com.name: Writer.com
pros: Own models with clear data terms
writer-com.value: Writer trains its own Palmyra models and sells a full stack platform, knowledge graph, agents, brand and compliance guardrails, to large companies that want AI without sending data to the big labs. It is the enterprise alternative to Jasper and a credible agent platform.

pricing.includes: Palmyra models, agents, knowledge graph, SSO

writer-com.tagline: Enterprise generative AI platform with its own Palmyra models, built for governed content and agents.
writer-com.governance_note: Writer's guardrails for claims, terminology and compliance are the feature regulated teams buy; configure them against your own policy documents.
writer-com.training_optout: Writer does not train on customer data.

writesonic.name: WriteSonic
pros: SEO and AI search tracking together
writesonic.value: Writesonic started as a copy generator with a chatbot called Chatsonic and repositioned toward SEO: article writing, content audits, and tracking how brands appear in AI search answers. It competes with Surfer and Frase now more than with Jasper.
writesonic.tagline: AI writing and SEO platform that shifted toward search visibility and AI search optimisation.
use_cases: Monitoring brand mentions in AI answers
writesonic.governance_note: Mass produced SEO content risks search penalties and brand harm; publish with editorial review.

zscaler-ai.name: Zscaler AI
zscaler-ai.value: Zscaler uses AI for threat detection and risk scoring and provides visibility and policy over employee use of generative AI apps, blocking or coaching users and preventing sensitive data from being pasted into them. It is a shadow AI control at the network layer.
zscaler-ai.tagline: AI powered security in Zscaler's zero trust platform, including controls for generative AI app use and data loss.
use_cases: Blocking data leakage to AI tools
zscaler-ai.governance_note: Network level AI controls complement device and policy controls; use the reports as the inventory of what employees use.
zscaler-ai.training_optout: Zscaler does not train on customer content.

aleph-alpha.name: Aleph Alpha
aleph-alpha.value: Aleph Alpha built models with explainability features and sells PhariaAI, an operating system for deploying any model on premises with EU data sovereignty, after stepping back from competing head on with the frontier labs. It serves German public sector and regulated industry.
aleph-alpha.engine: Aleph Alpha's Luminous and Pharia models plus hosted open models.
aleph-alpha.tagline: German AI company offering sovereign, explainable models and the PhariaAI platform for European enterprises and governments.
use_cases: Public sector AI in Germany and the EU
aleph-alpha.governance_note: Designed around EU AI Act obligations; useful where data must stay in the EU and decisions must be explainable.
aleph-alpha.training_optout: Customer data is not used for training.

aws-bedrock.api: AWS SDK and REST. Largely compatible with existing SDK patterns.
cons: Policy approval of Bedrock without specifying models is underspecified
Model availability lags direct provider releases
AWS dependency for organizations not already on the platform
aws-bedrock.name: AWS Bedrock
pros: Multi-model access under one enterprise agreement
AWS's enterprise compliance controls and regional deployment
No minimum commitment required to start
aws-bedrock.files: Text, images, and embeddings depending on the model selected.
aws-bedrock.value: Access to models from Anthropic, Meta, Mistral, Stability, and others through a single AWS API, with AWS's enterprise data controls, IAM, and billing. The multi-model access under one contract is the differentiator.
aws-bedrock.engine: Multiple: Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, Mistral, Stability AI, and Amazon Titan.
aws-bedrock.quality: Same models as the direct APIs, under AWS data terms.
aws-bedrock.tagline: Multiple frontier models available through a single AWS API, under enterprise data terms.
use_cases: Running multiple foundation models under a single enterprise agreement and billing model
Building model-agnostic applications that can switch providers without contract changes
Deploying Anthropic's Claude family inside an AWS-governed environment
integrations: Full AWS ecosystem: VPC, IAM, CloudWatch, S3
AWS Agents for Bedrock for agentic workflows
Same tooling as other AWS services
aws-bedrock.governance_note: The multi-model architecture means the governance envelope (data terms, residency, IAM) is AWS's, while model capability and model-specific risks vary by the model selected. Switching models within Bedrock does not change the data terms but does change which model's characteristics and limitations apply. A policy that approves 'AWS Bedrock' without specifying which models is underspecified.
aws-bedrock.training_optout: AWS states that customer inputs and outputs are not used to train foundation models. Verify via the AWS service terms.

captions-ai.name: Captions AI
pros: Eye contact and lip sync fixes
captions-ai.value: Captions started as a caption app and became a full creator studio: AI dubbing into other languages, eye contact and lip sync correction, AI avatars and its Mirage model that generates talking video from a script. It is strongest on phone made talking head content.
captions-ai.tagline: Mobile first video creation app with captions, AI dubbing, eye contact correction and an AI creator called Mirage.
use_cases: UGC style ads with AI creators
captions-ai.governance_note: Eye contact correction and AI creators change what a real person appears to do; disclose synthetic edits in advertising where the rules require it, and label AI generated creators.

claude-code.api: Built on the Anthropic API; usage can be billed through it directly.
cons: Executes commands, so scoping and review discipline are mandatory
Usage costs escalate on large tasks
Confident multi-file errors are hard to catch in review
claude-code.name: Claude Code
pros: Fits existing terminal and Git workflow
claude-code.files: Whole-repository access within the directory it is run in, subject to its permission prompts.
claude-code.value: Operates on a repository the way a developer does: reads files, makes multi-file changes, runs commands, and iterates on the result. Suited to a described task rather than a completed line.
claude-code.latency: Slower than inline completion by design, because it is reading, editing, and verifying rather than predicting the next token.
claude-code.quality: Strong on substantial multi-file changes. As with any agentic tool, a confident wrong change spread across several files is harder to spot in review than a single bad line.
claude-code.tagline: An agentic coding tool that works in the terminal against a whole repository.
use_cases: Multi-file refactors and feature implementation from a written description
Investigating and fixing a bug across an unfamiliar codebase
Automating repetitive engineering work such as migrations and test scaffolding
integrations: Model Context Protocol for external systems
claude-code.governance_note: Agentic coding tools change the control question from what the model reads to what it is allowed to do. It executes commands and edits files, so scope it deliberately: run it in a repository rather than a home directory, keep secrets out of the working tree, and require human review before merge. The corresponding audit evidence is the pull request history, which is where the record of what an agent changed actually lives.
claude-code.training_optout: Follows Anthropic's commercial terms: business and API data is not used for training by default.

doubao-seed.name: Doubao / Seed
doubao-seed.value: Doubao is ByteDance's consumer assistant with the largest user base in China, and Seed is the research team behind the models, including strong video and multimodal work that connects to CapCut and TikTok. Volcano Engine sells the models to enterprises at aggressive prices.
doubao-seed.tagline: ByteDance's Seed research models and Doubao, the most used AI assistant app in China.
doubao-seed.governance_note: ByteDance is restricted on many Western managed devices; the enterprise API is a China hosted service.

holistic-ai.name: Holistic AI
holistic-ai.value: Holistic AI inventories an organisation's AI systems, assesses risk against the EU AI Act, NYC Local Law 144 and other rules, runs bias audits and tracks remediation, selling to enterprises and as an independent auditor. It is one of the governance platform leaders.
holistic-ai.engine: Holistic's assessment frameworks and audit tooling.
holistic-ai.tagline: AI governance platform for inventory, risk assessment, bias audits and regulatory compliance, from a London firm.
holistic-ai.governance_note: An inventory and risk register is the first artefact every AI governance regime asks for; this is a tool that produces one.

ibm-watsonx.name: IBM watsonx
pros: Granite models are open and indemnified
ibm-watsonx.value: watsonx has three parts: watsonx.ai for building with IBM Granite and third party models, watsonx.data for the lakehouse and watsonx.governance for monitoring, risk and compliance of models wherever they run. IBM sells it to regulated enterprises that need on premises and audit trails.
ibm-watsonx.engine: IBM Granite models plus Llama, Mistral and others.
ibm-watsonx.tagline: IBM's AI and data platform with Granite open models, a governance module and on premises deployment.
ibm-watsonx.governance_note: watsonx.governance maps to NIST AI RMF and EU AI Act obligations and monitors models from any vendor, which makes it an audit tool as much as a platform.
ibm-watsonx.training_optout: IBM does not use customer data to train its models.

inaturalist.name: iNaturalist
pros: Model trained on verified community data
inaturalist.value: iNaturalist's app identifies plants and animals from a photo with a model trained on its own community verified observations, and the observations feed research, with the Seek app for younger users. It is a nonprofit and a model of AI trained on consented, attributed data.
inaturalist.vendor: California Academy of Sciences and National Geographic Society
inaturalist.tagline: Citizen science platform whose computer vision suggests species from photos, used in classrooms for biology and ecology.
inaturalist.governance_note: Observations are public by default with location; the Seek app avoids accounts and location sharing for children.
inaturalist.training_optout: Contributed observations train the model under the platform's open data terms.

leonardo-ai.name: Leonardo.ai
leonardo-ai.value: Leonardo offers its own Phoenix models, fine tuned community models, a canvas and video generation, with a strong following among game artists and marketers. Canva bought it and uses its models behind Canva's AI features while keeping the standalone product.
leonardo-ai.engine: Leonardo's Phoenix models plus community fine tunes.
leonardo-ai.tagline: Image and video generation platform for games and marketing, acquired by Canva in 2024.
leonardo-ai.governance_note: Community fine tuned models may carry training data risks; use Leonardo's own models for commercial work and keep the licence record.

cons: Vote gaming and style bias criticisms
Leaderboard is a signal, not a benchmark
lmsys-arena.name: LMSYS Arena Models
lmsys-arena.value: LMSYS, a Berkeley research group, created Vicuna, an early open chat model, and Chatbot Arena, the blind pairwise voting leaderboard that became the most cited public ranking of models before spinning out as LMArena. The arena is the product now; the models are history.
lmsys-arena.engine: Leaderboard over all major models; Vicuna models are historical.
lmsys-arena.status: Active. Chatbot Arena operates as LMArena; Vicuna models are historical.
lmsys-arena.tagline: The Chatbot Arena, where anonymous models are compared by human votes, and the Vicuna lineage of open chat models.
lmsys-arena.governance_note: Use the arena as one input to model selection; procurement decisions need your own evaluation on your tasks.
lmsys-arena.training_optout: Arena prompts may be released in research datasets; do not enter confidential text.

lokalise-ai.name: Lokalise AI
lokalise-ai.value: Lokalise manages software strings and content with AI translation that uses screenshots, glossaries and style guides for context, and integrates with Git, design tools and CMSs. It suits product teams shipping in many languages.
lokalise-ai.engine: Lokalise's AI translation over partner models.
lokalise-ai.tagline: Developer friendly localisation platform with AI translation tuned by context and glossaries.
lokalise-ai.governance_note: Standard: human review for legal and regulated strings.
lokalise-ai.training_optout: Lokalise states customer data is not used for training; confirm.

magicschool.name: MagicSchool
magicschool.value: MagicSchool is the most adopted teacher AI platform, with tools for lesson plans, rubrics, IEP support, report card comments and a student facing version with guardrails, sold to districts with privacy agreements. It is the reference for classroom AI assistants.
magicschool.engine: Partner LLMs with MagicSchool's prompts and guardrails.
magicschool.tagline: AI assistant for teachers with dozens of tools for lesson planning, differentiation, feedback and communication.
magicschool.governance_note: Student facing use requires a signed district agreement under FERPA and COPPA; teacher use should not include identifiable student data on free accounts.
magicschool.training_optout: MagicSchool states data is not used to train models; confirm in the district agreement.

obsidian-ai.name: Obsidian AI
obsidian-ai.value: Obsidian stores notes as plain files on your machine and has no built in AI; plugins such as Copilot and Smart Connections add chat over the vault with cloud or local models. It is the choice for people who want AI on notes they fully control.
obsidian-ai.engine: Plugins calling cloud APIs or local models.
obsidian-ai.tagline: Local first markdown notes with community plugins that add AI chat, local models and semantic search over your vault.
obsidian-ai.governance_note: Plugins may send vault content to cloud APIs; check each plugin's model setting. Local models keep everything on the device.
obsidian-ai.training_optout: Depends on the model provider chosen.

resemble-ai.name: Resemble AI
resemble-ai.value: Resemble sells voice cloning to enterprises and media with on premises deployment, a real time API and, unusually, a detection product that identifies synthetic audio. The pairing of generation and detection is its position.
resemble-ai.engine: Resemble's own speech models and detection classifiers.
resemble-ai.tagline: Enterprise voice cloning and speech synthesis with deepfake detection and watermarking.
use_cases: Detecting synthetic audio in fraud and media
resemble-ai.governance_note: Detection tools belong in fraud controls for call centres and finance; treat their output as a signal, not proof. Cloning consent and watermarking are mandatory process steps.
resemble-ai.training_optout: Enterprise terms exclude training on customer data; confirm.

supernormal.name: Supernormal
supernormal.value: Supernormal records and summarises meetings with customisable templates and shares notes to Slack and Notion, positioned as the simpler, cheaper note taker. It is a small player in a crowded field.
supernormal.tagline: Lightweight meeting notes with templates and a focus on simple summaries.

together-ai.api: Yes. OpenAI compatible REST API, plus fine tuning and embeddings endpoints.
cons: Quality and availability vary across the long tail of models
Enterprise compliance posture is newer than the hyperscalers'
together-ai.name: Together AI
pros: Largest open model menu among the inference hosts
OpenAI compatible, so switching is a URL change
together-ai.files: Datasets for fine tuning; inputs are text and images per model.
together-ai.value: Together serves the open model catalogue, Llama, DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral and hundreds more, through one OpenAI compatible API, with fine tuning and dedicated GPU clusters on top. It is one of the two or three places a team goes when it wants open weights without the operations.
together-ai.engine: Open models on Together's own inference stack and GPU fleet.
together-ai.latency: Fast on popular models; cold starts on rarely used ones.
together-ai.quality: As good as the open model you choose; the serving is solid.
together-ai.tagline: Hosted inference and fine tuning for open models, at prices that undercut running them yourself.
use_cases: Running an open model in production without a GPU team
Fine tuning a model on your own data
A/B testing open models against closed ones
together-ai.governance_note: You are buying hosting, not a model. Keep the model licence, the hosting terms and your data residency needs as three separate checks, because the licence of an open model can restrict commercial use even when the host does not.
together-ai.training_optout: Together states it does not train on customer inputs; dedicated endpoints add isolation. Confirm in the current terms.

cons: False positive rate is real and has disparate impact implications
Cannot be used as standalone evidence in disciplinary proceedings
FERPA data handling requires explicit institutional review
turnitin-ai.name: Turnitin AI Detection
pros: Integrated with existing Turnitin infrastructure most institutions already have
Scale: every submission gets a signal automatically
turnitin-ai.files: Submitted student writing in standard document formats.
turnitin-ai.value: Adds AI-generated content detection to Turnitin's established plagiarism infrastructure, giving institutions a single place for both questions. Used wherever academic integrity policy requires verification of whether writing is human-originated.
turnitin-ai.latency: Asynchronous, with the submission review workflow.

pricing.model: Custom, included with or added to Turnitin

turnitin-ai.quality: Probabilistic, not deterministic. Turnitin explicitly states scores should not be used as standalone evidence of misconduct.
turnitin-ai.tagline: The leading academic integrity tool, now with AI detection, and the governance lessons that come with it.
use_cases: Institutional AI detection at scale alongside existing plagiarism checking
Providing instructors with a signal for academic integrity review
Policy enforcement where institutional rules prohibit AI-generated submission
integrations: LMS platforms: Canvas, Blackboard, Moodle, D2L
turnitin-ai.governance_note: The hardest governance point is the reliability gap. AI detection tools, including Turnitin's, have documented false positive rates: they sometimes flag human writing as AI-generated, at higher rates for non-native English writers in some studies. Using a detection score as standalone evidence in a disciplinary proceeding is both a due-process problem and a potential disparate-impact one. Turnitin says explicitly not to do this. The policy question institutions must answer is how the score enters the misconduct process and what other evidence is required before a finding. That policy must exist before the tool is deployed, not be constructed case by case.
turnitin-ai.training_optout: Institutional terms govern student submission data. FERPA classification of submission data requires careful review.

azure-openai.api: OpenAI-compatible REST API plus Azure SDK. Same client libraries work with a base-URL change.
cons: Regional availability lags OpenAI's model releases
Quota allocation requires a separate approval process
Adds Azure dependency for teams not already on the platform
azure-openai.name: Azure OpenAI Service
pros: Enterprise data terms, not consumer terms
Azure compliance controls (residency, VNET, private endpoints)
Same models as OpenAI API, unified billing
azure-openai.files: Same as the OpenAI API; the difference is where it runs.
azure-openai.value: The OpenAI model family (GPT, Embeddings, Whisper, DALL-E) deployed inside Azure's infrastructure, under Azure's enterprise data terms, IAM, networking, and compliance controls. For organizations already on Azure, this is the path to OpenAI capabilities without the consumer data-handling question.
azure-openai.engine: OpenAI models: GPT series, embeddings, Whisper, DALL-E, deployed on Azure infrastructure.

pricing.includes: Same models as OpenAI API under Azure billing

azure-openai.quality: Identical to OpenAI's models. The differentiation is the deployment environment.
azure-openai.tagline: OpenAI's models running in Azure, under Microsoft's enterprise data terms.
use_cases: Enterprise AI applications where data must stay inside an existing Azure tenancy
Standardizing the organization on one model API with consistent billing and controls
Regulated industries requiring regional data residency and VNET integration
integrations: Full Azure service ecosystem: Cognitive Search, Azure AI Foundry, VNET, Log Analytics
Enterprise identity and access via Azure AD
Same SDK surface as the OpenAI API
azure-openai.governance_note: The governance case is simple: it is the same capability as the OpenAI API under Microsoft's enterprise compliance envelope. For organizations that have already approved Azure for sensitive data, this is usually the faster path to deployment than a separate OpenAI vendor review. The specific controls to confirm are VNET integration, private endpoints, and whether the region chosen satisfies any data residency requirements. One common mistake is deploying to a convenient region without checking residency.
azure-openai.training_optout: Microsoft's commercial data terms apply: Azure OpenAI does not use customer data to train models. This is the point. Verify via the Microsoft Product Terms, not the OpenAI terms, which do not govern here.

beautiful-ai.name: Beautiful.ai
beautiful-ai.value: Beautiful.ai's smart slides reflow automatically so a deck stays on grid, and its AI writes and generates decks from prompts and documents. Teams use it for consistent sales and marketing decks with brand control.
beautiful-ai.engine: Partner LLMs plus its own layout engine.
beautiful-ai.tagline: Presentation software with smart templates that keep slides well designed as you add content, plus AI generation.
beautiful-ai.governance_note: Standard: verify facts, use enterprise tier for confidential content.

cons: Minors have been a large share of users, with the safety record to match
Not designed for factual or work use
Litigation over harm to young users is ongoing
character-ai.name: Character.ai
pros: Deep persona consistency over long conversations
Huge library of characters and scenarios
character-ai.files: Images in some character chats; not a document tool.
character-ai.value: Character.ai is persona chat at scale: millions of user made characters, long running conversations and a young audience. It matters to the AI map less as a work tool than as the product that defined the companion category and drew the first wrongful death suits over chatbot conduct.
character-ai.engine: Character.AI's own models, with a licensing and talent agreement with Google since 2024.
character-ai.latency: Fast on the paid tier; queues on free during peaks.
character-ai.quality: Excellent at staying in character; weak on facts, which is not the point.
character-ai.tagline: Conversational characters built by users, the largest consumer companion chat product.
integrations: None of note for business use
character-ai.governance_note: For a school or an employer the question is not whether to buy it but whether to block it. The product's own tracker entries on this site cover the lawsuits that followed teen use; parental controls and age checks have been added since, and their adequacy is the live issue.
character-ai.training_optout: Conversations are used to improve the service under the consumer terms; there is no enterprise tier with a contractual opt out.

cohere-coral.name: Cohere Coral
cohere-coral.value: Coral was Cohere's chat assistant for enterprises, grounded in company documents with citations and deployable in a customer's own cloud, and has been folded into North, Cohere's secure agent workspace. Cohere's pitch is data sovereignty for regulated and government buyers.
cohere-coral.status: Active. Coral has been absorbed into Cohere North.
cohere-coral.tagline: Cohere's enterprise chat interface over its Command models, now sold as part of its North platform.
use_cases: Grounded Q and A over documents
cohere-coral.governance_note: Private deployment is the control; confirm whether the deployment is in your tenancy or Cohere's.
cohere-coral.training_optout: Cohere does not train on enterprise customer data.

eightfold-ai.name: Eightfold AI
eightfold-ai.value: Eightfold builds a skills graph of candidates and employees to match them to jobs, suggest career paths and plan workforce needs, used by large employers and governments. It is a leading AI hiring platform and a frequent subject of bias audit requirements.
eightfold-ai.tagline: Talent intelligence platform that matches people to roles and skills across hiring, mobility and workforce planning.
eightfold-ai.governance_note: Automated employment decision tools fall under NYC Local Law 144, Colorado, Illinois and EU AI Act high risk rules; require bias audits and candidate notices.
eightfold-ai.training_optout: Enterprise terms; confirm use of your data in shared models.

fireflies-ai.name: Fireflies.ai
fireflies-ai.value: Fireflies joins meetings as a participant, produces transcripts, summaries and action items, and makes every past meeting searchable, with integrations into CRMs and project tools. It is one of the three big independent note takers with Otter and Fathom.
fireflies-ai.tagline: Meeting bot that records, transcribes and summarises calls across Zoom, Meet and Teams, with search and CRM sync.
fireflies-ai.governance_note: A bot joining external calls needs consent under two party recording laws and client contracts; set retention and admin controls before rollout.
fireflies-ai.training_optout: Fireflies states customer data is not used to train models; confirm.

fireworks-ai.api: Yes. OpenAI compatible, with fine tuning and batch endpoints.
fireworks-ai.name: Fireworks AI
pros: Among the fastest serving of open models
Reliable function calling and structured output
SOC 2 and HIPAA options for the enterprise tier
fireworks-ai.files: Fine tuning datasets; model inputs per model.
fireworks-ai.value: Fireworks competes on speed and reliability for open models, with its own inference engine, function calling that works, and compound AI features that chain models. Teams that have outgrown a prototype and need predictable latency are its market.
fireworks-ai.engine: Open models on Fireworks' proprietary inference engine.
fireworks-ai.latency: A selling point; consistently among the fastest hosts.
fireworks-ai.quality: Serving is excellent; model quality is whatever open model you pick.
fireworks-ai.tagline: Fast open model inference built for production, with a compiler level focus on speed.
use_cases: Latency sensitive production apps on open models
Agents that need reliable tool calling
Fine tuned models served at scale
fireworks-ai.governance_note: Same three check rule as any inference host: model licence, host terms, data residency. Fireworks' compliance tier is the answer for regulated workloads that still want open models.
fireworks-ai.training_optout: Fireworks states customer data is not used for training. Confirm in the current terms.

cons: Sends text to a model provider
goblin-tools.name: Goblin Tools
goblin-tools.value: Goblin Tools was built by one developer for people with ADHD and autism, with a magic to do list that breaks tasks into subtasks, a tone judge for messages, a formaliser and a time estimator, free on the web with cheap mobile apps. It is a well regarded accessibility use of LLMs.
goblin-tools.tagline: Free set of small AI helpers for neurodivergent users: break tasks into steps, judge tone, estimate time, simplify text.
goblin-tools.governance_note: Text goes to a third party model; do not enter confidential content. For schools, use as a teacher demonstrated tool rather than a student account.
goblin-tools.training_optout: Depends on the model provider; the site states it does not store inputs.

google-medlm.name: Google Med-PaLM / MedLM
google-medlm.files: Clinical text, images for some models.
google-medlm.value: Med-PaLM was the research model that first passed medical licensing exam questions at expert level; MedLM packaged it for healthcare customers on Vertex AI, and Google has since released MedGemma open models for developers. The line shows how a lab moves medical AI from paper to product.
google-medlm.status: Active. Med-PaLM is research lineage; MedLM and MedGemma are the current offerings.
google-medlm.quality: Research leading; clinical validation per use.
google-medlm.tagline: Google's medical language model line, from the Med-PaLM research to MedLM on Vertex AI and the MedGemma open models.
google-medlm.governance_note: A medical model is not a medical device until a product makes it one; FDA and HIPAA obligations attach to the application, not the model. Google's BAA covers Vertex AI.
google-medlm.training_optout: Vertex AI does not train on customer data.

huawei-pangu.name: Huawei PanGu
huawei-pangu.value: PanGu is Huawei's model family built for vertical industries rather than consumer chat, with a weather model published in Nature and deployments in Chinese state and industrial customers, all on Ascend hardware that avoids US chips. It matters as the backbone of China's sovereign AI stack.
huawei-pangu.tagline: Huawei's industry focused models for weather, mining, finance and government, running on its Ascend chips.
huawei-pangu.governance_note: Huawei is subject to US sanctions; most Western organisations cannot procure it. Track it for market understanding.

hugging-face.api: REST inference API plus the Python libraries that are the de facto standard for working with open models.
cons: Quality and licensing vary wildly by publisher
Self-hosting shifts the entire operational burden in-house
hugging-face.name: Hugging Face
pros: The definitive source for open-weight models
Self-hosting removes third-party data exposure entirely
Model cards support genuine due diligence
hugging-face.files: Hosts model weights, datasets, and demo applications.
hugging-face.value: Where open-weight models and their datasets actually live. Less a product than the distribution layer the entire open-model ecosystem depends on, including the tooling most teams use to run models themselves.
hugging-face.engine: Not a model itself. A hub and a set of libraries hosting models from many publishers.
hugging-face.latency: Not applicable to the hub. Hosted inference performance depends on the model and tier.

pricing.includes: Public model and dataset access, community features
SSO, audit logs, access controls, region selection

hugging-face.quality: Quality varies enormously by publisher, which is the nature of an open hub. Model cards and licences must be read individually.
hugging-face.tagline: The public infrastructure of open-weight AI: models, datasets, and the libraries around them.
use_cases: Finding, comparing, and downloading open-weight models for self-hosting
Building on the Transformers library rather than a vendor API
Sourcing and publishing datasets, and reading model cards before adopting a model
hugging-face.governance_note: The critical governance step here is licence review. Open weight does not mean open licence, and several widely used models carry commercial restrictions or acceptable-use terms that survive fine-tuning. Read the licence, not the headline.
hugging-face.training_optout: Self-hosted use means data never leaves the organization, which is the main governance argument for open weights in the first place.

khan-academy.name: Khan Academy
khan-academy.value: Khanmigo, built with OpenAI, tutors students by asking questions rather than giving answers and helps teachers plan, grade and differentiate, free for US teachers and offered to districts for students. It is the most studied AI tutor in K12.
khan-academy.engine: OpenAI models with Khan Academy's tutoring design.
khan-academy.tagline: Nonprofit learning platform whose Khanmigo tutor gives students guided help and teachers planning tools.
khan-academy.governance_note: Khan Academy publishes its student privacy and safety approach; districts still sign the data agreement.
khan-academy.training_optout: Student data is not used to train OpenAI models under Khan Academy's agreement.

kira-systems.name: Kira Systems
kira-systems.value: Kira pioneered machine learning contract review for due diligence, extracting provisions from thousands of agreements with trained models, and Litera acquired it in 2021 and folded it into its legal workflow suite. It remains in use at law firms for M and A review.
kira-systems.engine: Kira's trained extraction models with generative additions.
kira-systems.tagline: Contract review software that extracts clauses and data from documents, now part of Litera.
kira-systems.governance_note: Extraction output supports lawyer review; it does not replace it, and privilege handling applies to uploaded documents.
kira-systems.training_optout: Litera does not train shared models on customer documents; confirm.

palantir-aip.api: Palantir's own API surfaces within the platform.
cons: Significant platform investment required before AI adds value
Premium pricing, primarily accessible at enterprise and government scale
palantir-aip.name: Palantir AIP
pros: AI grounded on a governed, structured data ontology rather than unstructured documents
On-premises deployment available for the highest-sensitivity environments
Human oversight documented in the platform
palantir-aip.files: Structured operational data via Palantir's ontology. Not a document chat product.
palantir-aip.value: AI-enabled decision support built on top of Palantir's data integration and ontology layer. The proposition is that AI acting on structured, governed operational data is more defensible and controllable than AI acting on unstructured documents. Primarily used in defense, intelligence, and critical infrastructure.
palantir-aip.engine: Frontier models (primarily OpenAI and Anthropic) operating over Palantir's data ontology and access-control layer.
palantir-aip.latency: Interactive for decision support. Complex analysis is longer.
palantir-aip.quality: High for well-structured operational data with a maintained ontology. The underlying models are the same frontier models available elsewhere; the differentiation is the data layer.
palantir-aip.tagline: AI layered on top of Palantir's operational data platform, targeting defense and critical infrastructure.
use_cases: AI-assisted decision support in defense and national security operations
Operational intelligence over complex multi-source data in critical infrastructure
Rapid scenario analysis over a governed enterprise data ontology
integrations: Palantir Foundry and the broader Palantir data platform
Government and enterprise data sources via Palantir connectors
palantir-aip.governance_note: The most consequential AI governance question in the Palantir context is human oversight of AI-assisted decisions in high-stakes settings. The EU AI Act's highest-risk category and the US Executive Order on AI both specifically address AI in national security and critical infrastructure. The documentation requirement is not just 'what did the AI recommend' but 'what did the human decision-maker do, based on what information, and why.' The platform supports this documentation; the policy requirement is to actually use it.
palantir-aip.training_optout: On-premises deployment options mean data can remain fully within the customer's environment. Palantir's government contracts require FedRAMP or equivalent clearance in relevant contexts.

parentsquare.name: ParentSquare
parentsquare.value: ParentSquare unifies district, school and classroom communication to families with translation into many languages and an AI assistant that drafts messages for staff, adopted widely by districts as the official channel. Its AI is translation and drafting.
parentsquare.status: Active. AI limited to translation and drafting; flagged for vendor check.
parentsquare.tagline: School to home communication platform with automatic message translation and AI writing help for staff.
parentsquare.governance_note: Flagged on the unverified list: AI is translation and drafting only. Family data under FERPA and the district agreement.
parentsquare.training_optout: ParentSquare states data is not used for training; confirm.

relevance-ai.api: Yes. Agents and tools can be triggered by API and webhook.
cons: Credit consumption is hard to forecast
Agents that email prospects need tight review
Less control than a code framework
relevance-ai.name: Relevance AI
pros: Usable by a business team without engineering
Strong integrations with CRMs and email
Agent templates that work on day one
relevance-ai.files: Spreadsheets and documents as inputs; CRM data through integrations.
relevance-ai.value: Relevance AI sells agents to business teams rather than developers: templates for research, outbound, support and data enrichment, a visual tool builder, and a workforce view where agents are managed like staff. It is a reference product for the agentic workforce pitch that enterprise vendors adopted later.
relevance-ai.engine: Multiple model providers chosen per agent.
relevance-ai.latency: Seconds to minutes per agent run.
relevance-ai.quality: Good for structured, repeatable tasks; open ended tasks need a human check.
relevance-ai.tagline: A no code platform for building and running AI agents as a digital workforce, popular with sales and operations teams.
relevance-ai.governance_note: An agent that sends email on your domain is a brand and compliance risk; keep a human approval step on outbound and log every message. The platform holds CRM credentials, so it belongs in the vendor register with that access documented.
relevance-ai.training_optout: Relevance AI states customer data is not used to train models; model calls follow each provider's terms. Confirm in the current terms.

replit-agent.api: No agent API; the IDE has an API for workspace automation.
cons: The agent has taken destructive actions on live data
Usage based billing surprises are common complaints
replit-agent.name: Replit Agent
pros: Full stack with database, auth and hosting in one place
Mobile app that can build from a phone
Checkpoints and rollbacks after the 2025 incident
replit-agent.files: Anything in the workspace; the agent can read and write all of it, which is the point and the risk.
replit-agent.value: Replit already had the hosted environment, database, secrets and deployment, so its agent builds on real infrastructure from the first prompt rather than a sandbox. It is popular with non developers and schools, and it produced the most quoted vibe coding incident of 2025, when the agent deleted a production database during a code freeze and then misreported it.
replit-agent.engine: Frontier models from several vendors driving Replit's own agent harness.
replit-agent.quality: Good at getting something running; the July 2025 database deletion is the reminder that an agent with write access to production needs guardrails the product did not have at the time.
replit-agent.tagline: An agent inside Replit's cloud IDE that builds, runs and deploys an app end to end.
use_cases: Building and hosting an app with no setup
replit-agent.governance_note: Separate development and production environments before an agent touches anything, and never give an agent credentials to live data you cannot restore. Replit added rollbacks and environment separation after its incident; your policy should not depend on the vendor's defaults.
replit-agent.training_optout: Replit's terms distinguish free and paid tiers on training use; confirm the current terms for the plan you buy.

repurpose-io.name: Repurpose.io
repurpose-io.value: Repurpose.io is a distribution automation: publish once and it reformats and posts to every other platform, with AI clipping of long videos and captions. It is used by creators who want the publishing chore removed.
repurpose-io.engine: Repurpose's licensed models for clipping and captions.
repurpose-io.tagline: Automation that republishes video and audio across platforms, with AI clipping and captions added.
integrations: YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, X
repurpose-io.governance_note: Automatic posting across platforms is the risk: one bad clip goes everywhere. Keep a review step or a delay for anything from a live source.

speechmatics.name: Speechmatics
speechmatics.value: Speechmatics, from Cambridge in the UK, trained its models to handle accents and dialects that trip up rivals, and sells batch and real time transcription plus translation and summarisation, including on premises. It is favoured in broadcast, contact centres and government.
speechmatics.tagline: Speech recognition API known for accent coverage and accuracy, with on premises deployment.
speechmatics.governance_note: UK vendor with on premises deployment suits public sector and regulated buyers; confirm data location for the cloud API.
speechmatics.training_optout: Enterprise terms exclude training on customer data; confirm.

adobe-firefly.api: Firefly Services API for enterprise automation.
cons: Credit-based pricing is easy to exhaust
Best value assumes you already pay for Creative Cloud
adobe-firefly.name: Adobe Firefly
pros: Licensed training data and commercial indemnity
adobe-firefly.files: Text prompts and image inputs, with deep integration into Adobe file formats.
adobe-firefly.value: Trained on licensed and public-domain material rather than an undisclosed web scrape, and sold with enterprise indemnity. For organizations where legal review gates creative tooling, that provenance position matters more than output quality.
adobe-firefly.engine: Adobe's own Firefly models, positioned on licensed training data.
adobe-firefly.latency: Fast enough for interactive editing inside the Creative Cloud applications.
adobe-firefly.quality: Good, and improving, though generally behind Midjourney on pure aesthetics. Its advantage is integration and legal posture rather than raw output.
adobe-firefly.tagline: Image generation built for commercial use, with indemnity, which is the point.
use_cases: Commercial marketing imagery where provenance must survive legal review
Generative editing inside Photoshop and Illustrator workflows already in place
Brand-controlled generation using an organization's own approved assets
integrations: Photoshop, Illustrator, Express, and the wider Creative Cloud
adobe-firefly.governance_note: This is the reference case for training-data provenance as a procurement criterion. Where a generator cannot say what it was trained on, the organization inherits that uncertainty on every asset it publishes. Firefly's commercial indemnity converts that uncertainty into a contractual allocation, which is exactly the sort of control an auditor can test. Content Credentials support also helps with the provenance-labelling obligations now appearing in AI law.
adobe-firefly.training_optout: Enterprise agreements cover customer content use. Adobe's position on training data provenance is the product's central claim and should be read directly rather than taken second-hand.

arize-phoenix.api: Python SDK (arize-phoenix, arize-phoenix-evals), OpenInference instrumentors, OpenTelemetry OTLP ingest.
cons: Elastic License 2.0 is source-available, not OSI open source; read it before building a product on top
Self-hosting means you own upgrades, storage, and backups
Span-based pricing on the commercial tiers scales badly for agents that emit thousands of spans per run
Team collaboration and persistence features push you toward the paid platform
arize-phoenix.name: Arize Phoenix
pros: Self-hosting is genuinely free, with no per-trace bill at scale
OpenTelemetry and OpenInference native, so instrumentation is portable rather than vendor-specific
Retrieval and embedding analysis are deeper than most general-purpose tracers
Runs locally in a notebook for development, which shortens the loop
arize-phoenix.files: Datasets and experiments as first-class objects; embeddings analysis for retrieval pipelines.
arize-phoenix.value: The source-available observability platform from Arize, built on OpenTelemetry with OpenInference semantic conventions for LLM spans. It runs in a notebook, on a laptop, or as a container in your own cloud, and covers tracing, datasets, LLM-as-judge evaluation, RAG-specific retrieval metrics, and embedding drift visualisation. Its distinguishing property is that instrumentation is standard: the same OpenTelemetry spans can be routed to Phoenix today and a different backend tomorrow without re-instrumenting the application.
arize-phoenix.engine: Self-hosted or Phoenix Cloud. OpenTelemetry collector ingesting OpenInference-shaped spans.
arize-phoenix.latency: Asynchronous span export; no proxy in the request path.

pricing.includes: Full tracing, evals, datasets, embeddings analysis under Elastic License 2.0

pricing.limits: Commercial tiers meter on spans per month, which climbs quickly for agents that emit thousands of spans per run

arize-phoenix.quality: Strongest of the open options for retrieval-heavy work, with embedding drift and RAG metrics that generic tracers lack. Prompt-and-notebook centric heritage means very long agent runs can be laborious to read as a raw span tree.
arize-phoenix.tagline: Self-hostable LLM tracing and evaluation built on open standards, so your trace data stays yours and stays portable.
use_cases: Debugging RAG pipelines where the failure is in retrieval rather than generation
Keeping prompts and completions inside your own infrastructure for data-residency reasons
Instrumenting once with OpenTelemetry and staying free to change backends
Comparing evaluation runs across prompt or model changes
arize-phoenix.governance_note: Self-hosting resolves the question that dominates observability procurement: prompts and completions never leave your environment, so trace capture does not become a new data-transfer decision to justify. The remaining obligations move to you rather than disappearing, since retention, access control, and encryption of the trace store are now your responsibility, and a trace store holds exactly the sensitive text a data map has to account for. The OpenTelemetry foundation is itself a governance asset: instrumentation that is not vendor-specific means an observability vendor changing hands, raising prices, or entering maintenance mode does not force a re-instrumentation project.
arize-phoenix.training_optout: Self-hosted deployments send nothing to the vendor. Hosted tiers are governed by the Arize agreement; verify current terms.

bloomberg-gpt.api: Bloomberg API for programmatic access within Terminal licences.
cons: Not benchmarked publicly against current frontier models
bloomberg-gpt.name: Bloomberg GPT
pros: Finance-domain training on proprietary data produces better financial NLP
Information barrier controls designed into the platform
No data export or additional API contract required for Terminal users
bloomberg-gpt.files: Bloomberg Terminal data: news, filings, market data, and financial documents.
bloomberg-gpt.value: A large language model trained on Bloomberg's proprietary financial data, deployed within the Bloomberg Terminal and Bloomberg Intelligence. Provides finance-native NLP that outperforms general models on financial NLP tasks because it was trained on the actual data.
bloomberg-gpt.engine: BloombergGPT, a 50B parameter model trained on Bloomberg's financial corpus, plus updates since that paper.

pricing.includes: AI features as part of the Terminal

bloomberg-gpt.quality: Stronger than general models on finance-specific NLP. Not publicly benchmarked against the current frontier on general tasks.
bloomberg-gpt.tagline: The finance-domain LLM, trained on Bloomberg's proprietary data, not publicly accessible.
use_cases: Financial NLP tasks: sentiment analysis, earnings call analysis, and regulatory filing review
Finance-domain question answering within Bloomberg's research ecosystem
Structured extraction from financial documents at scale
integrations: Bloomberg Data License for enterprise data users
bloomberg-gpt.governance_note: The material non-public information (MNPI) question is the first governance point for finance AI: a model that helps analyze earnings calls or regulatory filings must be operated under the firm's information barrier controls. Bloomberg's infrastructure is already designed around those controls for terminal users, which is an advantage over running a general AI against the same documents. The AI layer adds speed; the compliance layer requires that speed be bounded by the same information barriers that govern all Bloomberg data use.
bloomberg-gpt.training_optout: Bloomberg's data terms govern. Customer queries stay within Bloomberg's infrastructure.

confluence-ai.name: Confluence AI
confluence-ai.value: Confluence's AI summarises pages and comments, drafts content, answers questions across Atlassian and connected tools through Rovo and runs agents for routine knowledge tasks. It is included in premium plans and ties to Jira.
confluence-ai.engine: Partner LLMs with Atlassian's Teamwork Graph.
confluence-ai.tagline: Atlassian Intelligence and Rovo in Confluence: summaries, writing help, search and agents over team knowledge.
use_cases: Finding answers across Jira and Confluence
confluence-ai.governance_note: Admins choose which AI features are on and which connectors Rovo reads; data residency options exist.
confluence-ai.training_optout: Atlassian does not train on customer data.

cons: Best value assumes significant existing Databricks investment
DBU pricing can be opaque for AI workloads specifically
DBRX trails frontier models on the hardest tasks
databricks-ai.name: Databricks AI / DBRX
pros: AI and data governance unified in one platform
Unity Catalog lineage applies to AI workloads
DBRX as an open-weight option for Databricks customers
databricks-ai.files: Databricks data formats: Delta tables, Unity Catalog governed assets.
databricks-ai.value: AI capabilities, including DBRX (Databricks' own model) and LLM access, embedded in the platform used for data engineering and ML. For organizations running Databricks, this means AI work stays in the same governed environment as the data it needs.
databricks-ai.engine: DBRX (Databricks' open-weight model) plus access to frontier models, all operating on the Databricks Lakehouse.
databricks-ai.latency: Batch and interactive depending on the workload type.
databricks-ai.quality: DBRX is competitive for its size. The platform advantage is governance of the data pipeline and model together, not the raw model quality.
databricks-ai.tagline: AI and LLM capabilities inside the data platform where ML teams already live.
use_cases: Fine-tuning and deploying models on your own data inside Databricks
Building RAG and AI applications on top of existing data pipelines
DBRX as an open-weight model option for organizations with Databricks investment
integrations: Unity Catalog for governed data access
MLflow for model tracking and deployment
Delta Lake and the Databricks Lakehouse
databricks-ai.governance_note: The governance case here is data lineage: AI models trained or operating on Databricks data inherit the Unity Catalog access controls and lineage tracking. That is significantly easier to audit than AI models operating on data exfiltrated to an external API. For organizations with a Databricks investment, the governance case for keeping AI work inside the platform is often stronger than the pure model-quality case for moving outside it.
databricks-ai.training_optout: Databricks' enterprise terms apply. Unity Catalog governs data access for AI workloads within the platform.

dreambox-math.name: DreamBox Math
dreambox-math.value: DreamBox pioneered intelligent adaptive learning in math, analysing each student's strategy within a lesson rather than only the answer, with research on gains at scale, and Discovery Education acquired it in 2023. It is a long standing adaptive learning engine rather than a generative AI product.
dreambox-math.tagline: Adaptive K8 math program that adjusts every lesson to how a student solves problems, now part of Discovery Education.
dreambox-math.governance_note: Adaptive engines make instructional decisions about children; districts should review the evidence and the data agreement.
dreambox-math.training_optout: Student data is not used to train shared models under the district agreement; confirm.

cons: AI claim is predictive, not generative
everyday-labs.name: EveryDay Labs
everyday-labs.value: EveryDay Labs, formerly InClass Today, reduces chronic absenteeism with research based family messaging, using predictive models to identify at risk students and personalise outreach, with randomised trial evidence. Its AI is predictive analytics and message personalisation.
everyday-labs.status: Active. AI is predictive analytics and personalised messaging; flagged for vendor check.
everyday-labs.tagline: Attendance intervention service that sends personalised family messages, with predictive analytics on absenteeism.
everyday-labs.governance_note: Flagged on the unverified list: predictive risk scoring of students is a legitimate AI use but should be reviewed for fairness and explained to families.

ibm-openpages.name: IBM OpenPages with Watson
ibm-openpages.value: OpenPages is a long standing GRC system for operational risk, compliance and audit, and IBM connected it to watsonx.governance so model inventories, risk assessments and monitoring evidence flow into the same register banks already use. It suits organisations with existing OpenPages deployments.
ibm-openpages.engine: IBM GRC platform with watsonx AI features.
ibm-openpages.tagline: IBM's governance, risk and compliance platform with AI model risk management connected to watsonx.governance.
ibm-openpages.governance_note: The right home for model risk if OpenPages already holds the firm's risk register.

ibm-openscale.api: REST APIs for monitoring and metadata. SDK for integration.
cons: Best value inside an existing IBM stack
Complexity may exceed needs of smaller model estates
ibm-openscale.name: IBM watsonx.governance
pros: Deepest governance feature set in the category
On-premises option removes cloud data exposure
ibm-openscale.files: Integrates with model stores, feature stores, and data warehouses.
ibm-openscale.value: The most established enterprise governance platform from a traditional software vendor. Covers model monitoring, drift detection, fairness testing, and audit-trail generation across both IBM and third-party models. Sold to regulated industries on the strength of its on-premises deployment option and IBM's compliance track record.
ibm-openscale.engine: Monitors models from any provider. Runs its own explainability and fairness algorithms.
ibm-openscale.latency: Background monitoring, not interactive. Dashboards update periodically.

pricing.includes: Managed deployment, monitoring, and explainability features

ibm-openscale.quality: Deep and auditable. Configuration complexity is real, and the investment in setup is proportional to the environment it is managing.
ibm-openscale.tagline: IBM's enterprise AI governance platform: model monitoring, explainability, and audit.
use_cases: Monitoring production ML models for drift, bias, and performance degradation
Generating explainability artifacts for regulator inquiries
Building a governed model lifecycle from training through retirement
integrations: IBM Watson Studio and the wider IBM data and AI stack
Enterprise data warehouses and feature stores
ibm-openscale.governance_note: This is what an AI audit of a regulated organization's model estate looks like in practice: continuous monitoring, explainability, and documented evidence rather than a point-in-time review. The EU AI Act's high-risk system requirements (Article 9 risk management, Article 17 quality management) describe exactly this kind of ongoing oversight. The product is expensive and complex, and the right question is whether your model estate is large enough to justify it, or whether lighter tooling covers the actual scope.
ibm-openscale.training_optout: On-premises deployment means model and data stay on your infrastructure. Cloud deployment follows IBM's standard data terms.

iflytek-spark.name: iFlytek Spark
iflytek-spark.value: iFlytek built Spark on its decades of speech recognition work and deploys it in education devices, medical assistants and office tools across China, on Huawei Ascend chips. It is a top tier Chinese model outside the big internet companies.
iflytek-spark.tagline: Chinese voice technology leader's LLM, strong in speech, education and healthcare applications.
iflytek-spark.governance_note: iFlytek is on the US entity list; not procurable for most Western organisations.

lexia-english.name: Lexia English
lexia-english.value: Lexia English teaches academic English to emergent bilingual students through adaptive lessons with speech recognition for speaking practice, from the maker of Lexia Core5, part of Cambium Learning. It is a structured program rather than a general AI tool.
lexia-english.engine: Lexia's adaptive engine with speech recognition.
lexia-english.tagline: Adaptive English language development program for multilingual learners, from Lexia, with speech recognition for speaking practice.
lexia-english.governance_note: Voice recordings of children; retention terms in the agreement.

cons: Not self-hostable, unlike the open-weight models
Smaller ecosystem than the US majors
mistral-large.name: Mistral Large 2
pros: Frontier quality under EU data terms
Simpler GDPR transfer analysis than US providers for EU organizations
Competitive pricing at the API tier
mistral-large.files: Document and image handling via the API.
mistral-large.value: Mistral's strongest model, aimed at the tasks where the smaller open-weight models fall short: complex reasoning, long-document analysis, and demanding coding work. Retains the EU-residency argument of the Mistral family.
mistral-large.engine: Mistral's proprietary frontier model. Not open weight.
mistral-large.quality: Frontier-class. Competitive on reasoning and coding benchmarks with the US majors.
mistral-large.tagline: Mistral's frontier model, the one in the proprietary tier, not the open-weight releases.
use_cases: Demanding reasoning and analysis requiring frontier capability under EU data terms
Enterprise API deployment where EU residency is required and quality cannot be compromised
Tasks where Mistral's lighter models show limits
mistral-large.governance_note: The EU-residency distinction that makes Mistral / Le Chat interesting applies equally here. The difference from the open-weight models is that this one cannot be self-hosted, so the data path runs through Mistral's infrastructure. That is still a significantly simpler transfer analysis than a US provider for a European organization, but it is not the same as self-hosting an Apache-licensed weight.
mistral-large.training_optout: API and enterprise terms address training data use. Verify for your tier.

perplexity-ai.api: REST API returning answers with source citations.
cons: A citation does not always support the claim attached to it
Weaker than dedicated assistants at writing and reasoning
Source quality varies with what ranks well
perplexity-ai.name: Perplexity AI
pros: Genuinely current, unlike static model knowledge
perplexity-ai.files: Accepts document uploads on paid tiers, with web retrieval as the primary input.
perplexity-ai.value: Answers questions with inline citations to the sources used, which makes it materially more checkable than a general assistant. The right tool when the answer needs to be traced back rather than merely produced.
perplexity-ai.engine: Model-agnostic, routing to frontier models from several vendors, layered over its own retrieval and ranking.

pricing.includes: Advanced model choice, file upload, higher limits
SSO, admin controls, data retention controls

perplexity-ai.quality: Citations are the differentiator and the caveat. They make verification possible, but a citation is not a guarantee: the tool sometimes cites a source that does not fully support the sentence. Read the source, do not trust the footnote.
perplexity-ai.tagline: Search rebuilt as a citing answer engine rather than a list of links.
use_cases: Fast market and competitor research with sources attached
Checking a current fact where a general model's knowledge would be stale
First-pass literature and regulatory scanning before deeper verification
perplexity-ai.governance_note: For an audit or compliance workflow, treat its citations exactly as this site treats news: a lead to the primary source, never the evidence itself.
perplexity-ai.training_optout: Enterprise tiers offer data controls and an AI training opt-out. Consumer tiers differ. Verify before regulated research goes through it.

samsung-gauss.name: Samsung Gauss
samsung-gauss.value: Gauss is Samsung's family of language, code and image models, used internally and in Galaxy AI alongside Google's Gemini, with on device variants for translation and summarisation. It is Samsung's hedge against dependence on outside models.
samsung-gauss.tagline: Samsung's in house generative models for internal use and Galaxy AI features on its devices.
samsung-gauss.governance_note: Relevant for device policy; on device features keep data local, cloud features follow Samsung and Google terms.

sharepoint-ai.name: SharePoint AI
pros: Agents from any site in minutes
sharepoint-ai.value: SharePoint agents let any site become a Copilot agent grounded in its documents, and Copilot in SharePoint drafts pages and summarises content, under Microsoft 365 terms. It is the easiest enterprise RAG for Microsoft shops.
sharepoint-ai.tagline: Copilot in SharePoint and SharePoint agents that answer questions from a site's documents.
sharepoint-ai.governance_note: Copilot surfaces oversharing that was always there; run SharePoint Advanced Management and restricted search before rollout.
sharepoint-ai.training_optout: Microsoft 365 data is not used for training.

talkingpoints.name: TalkingPoints
talkingpoints.value: TalkingPoints lets teachers message families who read in over 150 languages, with machine translation refined by human reviewers for sensitive education vocabulary, free for teachers and sold to districts. It is the equity focused alternative to general messaging apps.
talkingpoints.tagline: Nonprofit family engagement platform that translates teacher messages into families' languages with human reviewed AI.
talkingpoints.governance_note: Family contact data is student data under FERPA; district agreement required.
talkingpoints.training_optout: TalkingPoints states data is not used for training; confirm.

tesla-optimus.name: Tesla Optimus
tesla-optimus.value: Optimus is Tesla's humanoid, demonstrated doing factory and household tasks and planned for sale, with Tesla claiming it will be its largest product. Public demonstrations have mixed autonomy with teleoperation, so capability claims need care.
tesla-optimus.engine: Tesla's in house vision and control models.
tesla-optimus.status: Development. Not generally available; dates are announced targets only.
tesla-optimus.tagline: Tesla's humanoid robot programme, trained with the same AI stack as its driving software.
use_cases: Future general purpose labour, as claimed
tesla-optimus.governance_note: Treat capability claims as marketing until independent evidence; track for workforce and safety policy planning.

tutor-copilot.name: Tutor CoPilot
tutor-copilot.value: Tutor CoPilot is a research prototype that coaches tutors during live sessions with expert style prompts, and a 2024 randomised trial with hundreds of tutors found it raised student mastery, especially for less experienced tutors. It is cited as evidence that AI assisting humans can outperform AI replacing them.
tutor-copilot.engine: GPT models prompted with expert tutoring practices.
tutor-copilot.tagline: Stanford research system that gives human tutors real time AI suggestions, shown in a randomised trial to improve student math outcomes.
tutor-copilot.governance_note: A model for how to deploy AI in education: assist the adult, measure outcomes, publish results.

cons: Speech recognition with accents and young voices
amira-learning.name: Amira Learning
pros: Scales one to one reading practice
amira-learning.value: Amira uses speech recognition tuned to young readers to assess oral reading, screen for dyslexia risk and tutor with interventions, and merged with Istation and partnered with HMH to reach districts at scale. It is the most deployed AI reading assistant in US schools.
amira-learning.engine: Amira's own speech and assessment models.
amira-learning.tagline: AI reading tutor that listens to children read aloud, assesses fluency and coaches in the moment.
amira-learning.governance_note: Voice recordings of children are biometric adjacent data in some state laws; the data agreement should specify retention.

brisk-teaching.name: Brisk Teaching
brisk-teaching.value: Brisk works where teachers already are, adding feedback on student writing in Docs, changing reading levels of any web page, generating quizzes and inspecting writing history for AI use. Its extension design made it one of the fastest growing teacher tools.
brisk-teaching.tagline: Chrome extension that brings AI into Google Docs, Classroom and the web for feedback, levelling and lesson creation.
brisk-teaching.governance_note: The extension reads student documents; districts should approve it and sign the data agreement before teachers install it.
brisk-teaching.training_optout: Brisk states student data is not used for training; confirm.

cisco-webex-ai.name: Cisco Webex AI
cisco-webex-ai.value: Webex AI Assistant summarises meetings and messages, transcribes and translates, and extends into Cisco's contact centre with agent assist, with Cisco's enterprise security posture. It serves organisations standardised on Webex.
cisco-webex-ai.tagline: AI Assistant for Webex meetings, calling and contact centre, built on Cisco's own and partner models.
cisco-webex-ai.governance_note: Cisco publishes data handling for AI features; admins control each one.
cisco-webex-ai.training_optout: Cisco does not use customer data to train models.

github-copilot.api: Not a general-purpose API product. Extensibility is through editor extensions and GitHub.
cons: Behind dedicated agentic editors on large refactors
Premium request caps can surprise heavy users
Quality varies by language and by editor
github-copilot.name: GitHub Copilot
github-copilot.files: Works against the open repository and editor context. Repository-wide awareness varies by tier and editor.
github-copilot.value: The safest institutional choice for AI-assisted coding: broad IDE support, mature enterprise administration, and an established procurement path. Rarely the most capable option, usually the easiest to approve.
github-copilot.engine: Multiple underlying models, primarily OpenAI, with other model options in some tiers.
github-copilot.latency: Low latency for completion, which is the property that matters most for inline use.

pricing.includes: Policy controls, audit logs, IP indemnity

github-copilot.quality: Strong at idiomatic completion and boilerplate. Weaker at large multi-file refactors, where dedicated agentic tools have moved ahead.
github-copilot.tagline: The most widely deployed AI coding assistant, and the default in most enterprises.
use_cases: Inline code completion across the editors teams already use
Explaining unfamiliar code and assisting review
integrations: VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains IDEs, Neovim
github-copilot.governance_note: The enterprise tiers carry IP indemnity for suggestions, which is usually the deciding factor for legal review rather than any capability difference.
github-copilot.training_optout: Business and enterprise tiers exclude customer code from model training. A public-code filter is available. Confirm current terms for your tier.

google-meet-ai.api: Meet API; AI features in product.
google-meet-ai.name: Google Meet AI
google-meet-ai.value: Meet's Gemini features take notes without a bot, summarise, translate captions live, improve audio and lighting and generate backgrounds, covered by Workspace terms and included in business plans since 2025. It replaces third party note takers for Google shops.
google-meet-ai.tagline: Gemini in Meet: notes, summaries, translated captions and studio audio and video, included in Workspace plans.
google-meet-ai.governance_note: Workspace admins control availability and retention; participants are notified when notes are on.
google-meet-ai.training_optout: Workspace data is not used to train Gemini.

paradox-olivia.name: Paradox (Olivia)
paradox-olivia.value: Olivia handles high volume hiring conversations, answering candidate questions, screening against requirements, scheduling interviews and sending onboarding paperwork, used by retailers and restaurants hiring thousands. It automates the funnel rather than the decision.
paradox-olivia.engine: Paradox's conversational models with partner LLMs.
paradox-olivia.tagline: Conversational recruiting assistant that screens, schedules and onboards candidates by text and chat.
paradox-olivia.governance_note: Knockout screening questions are automated decisions; document criteria and offer a human path.

researchrabbit.name: ResearchRabbit
researchrabbit.value: ResearchRabbit lets you seed a collection with papers and then recommends related work, maps author networks and sends alerts as new papers appear, free for researchers. It is a discovery and tracking tool rather than a synthesis tool.
researchrabbit.engine: Recommendation algorithms over open citation data.
researchrabbit.tagline: Free literature discovery with collections, author networks and alerts, described as Spotify for papers.

vocabulary-com.name: Vocabulary.com
vocabulary-com.value: Vocabulary.com teaches words through adaptive questions that track which words a learner knows and returns to the ones they do not, alongside a human written dictionary, and is sold to schools and individuals by IXL. Its AI is the adaptive scheduling of practice.
vocabulary-com.status: Active. AI limited to adaptive practice; flagged for vendor check.
vocabulary-com.tagline: Adaptive vocabulary practice with a dictionary written in plain language, owned by IXL Learning.
vocabulary-com.governance_note: Flagged on the unverified list: the AI is adaptive practice scheduling, which is a legitimate but modest claim. Describe it as such.

weights-biases.api: Python and TypeScript libraries. Automatic instrumentation for major provider SDKs; the decorator traces arbitrary functions.
cons: Centre of gravity is still ML experiment tracking; for an LLM-only team Weave can feel like an add-on to a platform they do not otherwise use
Per-seat pricing bundled with the broader subscription pays for ML surfaces an application team may never touch
Trace model is W&B-native, so OpenTelemetry portability is weaker than Phoenix or Langfuse
No gateway layer for caching, routing, or failover
weights-biases.name: Weights & Biases
pros: Unified view from training experiment through to production trace, which no pure LLM tracer offers
Mature compliance and self-hosting story for regulated industries
Versioning and artifact lineage carry over from the ML platform, so reproducibility is genuinely first-class
Built-in guardrail and quality scorers rather than assembling them yourself
weights-biases.files: Artifacts, datasets, model registry, and evaluation runs with versioned lineage.
weights-biases.value: Two products under one account. The original platform is the widely adopted standard for training-run tracking: experiments, hyperparameter sweeps, artifacts, model registry, and reproducibility lineage. Weave layers LLM application observability on top, adding a decorator to any Python function to capture prompts, completions, token counts, cost, and latency, plus evaluation with custom and LLM-judge scorers, and pre-built guardrail scorers for toxicity, bias, PII, and hallucination. Its real advantage is continuity: for a team whose model development already lives in W&B, production traces sit beside the experiments that produced the model.
weights-biases.engine: Managed SaaS with enterprise self-hosting via Kubernetes. Weave SDK is the primary path, with OpenTelemetry-compatible ingest available.
weights-biases.status: Active. Acquired by CoreWeave; W&B Weave is the LLM and agent observability product alongside the original experiment-tracking platform.
weights-biases.latency: Asynchronous logging. Users have reported modest overhead on complex multi-step agent traces.

pricing.includes: Experiment tracking and Weave tracing for personal and small projects

pricing.limits: Storage and usage metered above included allowances
pricing.includes: Team collaboration, longer retention, registry features
Self-hosting in your own VPC, SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, HIPAA, and ISO 27001 coverage

weights-biases.quality: Best-in-class for experiment tracking and reproducibility. Weave is strong on agent tracing and evaluation, though the trace data model is W&B-native with OpenTelemetry as a secondary path, so instrumentation is less portable than the OpenTelemetry-first tools.
weights-biases.tagline: The ML experiment-tracking standard, extended to LLM tracing and evaluation through Weave.
use_cases: Teams already tracking training runs in W&B who want production LLM traces in the same place
Evaluating prompt and model changes against versioned datasets with reproducible lineage
Applying guardrail scorers for toxicity, bias, PII, and hallucination to live traffic
Regulated environments needing self-hosting with recognised compliance attestations
integrations: OpenAI, Anthropic, and other provider SDKs automatically
LangGraph, CrewAI, PydanticAI, OpenAI Agents SDK
Hugging Face and PEFT training workflows
weights-biases.governance_note: The strongest audit story here is lineage rather than tracing: linking a production behaviour back to the training run, dataset version, and hyperparameters that produced the model is precisely the evidence chain an AI audit asks for and most stacks cannot assemble. Enterprise self-hosting with SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, HIPAA, and ISO 27001 coverage answers the residency question that blocks observability adoption in regulated settings. Weigh against that the vendor-native trace format, which raises exit cost relative to OpenTelemetry-first tools, and record the CoreWeave ownership as a dependency fact with a review date, since the parent company's strategic priorities are now part of the platform's trajectory.
weights-biases.training_optout: Trace and experiment content is customer data under the vendor agreement, with enterprise self-hosting available to keep prompt data inside your own VPC. Verify current terms.

whisper-openai.api: REST API on OpenAI's platform. Open weights available for direct use.
cons: Not real-time in the standard form
API cost accumulates at high audio volume
Transcripts inherit the sensitivity of the underlying conversation
whisper-openai.name: Whisper API (OpenAI)
pros: Self-hosted path removes external data exposure
whisper-openai.files: Audio and video files in common formats.
whisper-openai.value: The strongest freely available speech-to-text model, and the reference benchmark for the category. Available both as an OpenAI API and as open weights you can run yourself, which is an unusual combination at this quality level.
whisper-openai.engine: OpenAI's Whisper model family, released as open weights. The API runs a hosted version.
whisper-openai.latency: Not real-time in the base form. The OpenAI API is fast for file transcription; real-time streaming requires the Realtime API endpoint.

pricing.includes: Open weights, full control, no data sent to OpenAI

whisper-openai.quality: Best-in-class across languages and accents for an open-weight model. Still degrades on heavy background noise and very domain-specific vocabulary.
whisper-openai.tagline: Open-weight speech recognition, accurate enough that every other vendor benchmarks against it.
use_cases: Transcribing audio and video files at scale through the API
Self-hosting accurate speech recognition inside a controlled environment
Building voice interfaces or meeting-note pipelines on a reliable accuracy floor
integrations: Self-hosting via Hugging Face and common ML tooling
whisper-openai.governance_note: The self-hosted path is the right answer wherever the audio is privileged, regulated, or involves recording consent issues. An HR investigation interview, a legal call, or a clinical encounter should not be sent through an external API. Open weights mean you get the same model quality on your own infrastructure. Pair with an explicit retention policy for the resulting transcripts, which are often more sensitive than the audio.
whisper-openai.training_optout: Self-hosted: nothing leaves your infrastructure. API: follows OpenAI's commercial data terms for the tier in use.

zapier-central.api: In development; primarily a UI-driven product.
cons: Autonomous action at scale requires deliberate scoping
Edge-case handling requires human escalation design
zapier-central.name: Zapier Central
pros: Standing agents over a vast integration network
zapier-central.value: Persistent AI agents that watch for conditions in connected apps and take actions when those conditions are met. Where Zapier AI is a step in a Zap, Central is a standing agent with memory and multi-step reasoning.
zapier-central.engine: Routes to frontier models via Zapier's infrastructure over the same app network.
zapier-central.latency: Async. Agents run on a schedule or on trigger.
