zapier-central.quality: As an agentic product, output quality depends on prompt quality and how well edge cases are handled in the agent's instructions.
zapier-central.tagline: Zapier's agent layer: bots that observe and act across your connected apps.
use_cases: Monitoring inboxes, CRMs, and ticketing systems and acting when conditions are met
Cross-app workflows that require conditional logic beyond simple if-this-then-that
Delegating recurring multi-step operational tasks to a managed agent
zapier-central.governance_note: An agent that runs autonomously across your business data is a materially different risk profile from a one-shot automation. Two controls are essential: a minimum-permission posture (the agent should connect to only the apps and data it genuinely needs), and a clear escalation path for edge cases the agent encounters. The most common failure pattern is an agent handling an edge case by making a plausible-but-wrong decision, and no one noticing until the downstream consequence has propagated.
zapier-central.training_optout: Same sub-processor chain as Zapier AI. Review both Zapier's terms and the underlying model provider's.

databricks-dbrx.name: Databricks DBRX
pros: Proof that custom training is feasible
databricks-dbrx.value: DBRX was Databricks' 2024 open model, a mixture of experts trained to show that its Mosaic tools could produce competitive models for customers, and it sits inside Databricks' Mosaic AI platform alongside hosted frontier models. It is more platform statement than product.
databricks-dbrx.status: Active. Dated; Databricks now hosts newer frontier and open models alongside it.
databricks-dbrx.tagline: Databricks' open mixture of experts model, released to show enterprises they can train their own.
use_cases: Models over data already in Databricks
databricks-dbrx.governance_note: Serving within Databricks keeps data in the lakehouse governance model, Unity Catalog, which is the reason to use it.
databricks-dbrx.training_optout: Databricks does not train on customer data.

cons: Requires branch protection and mandatory review to be safe
Less reliable on ambiguous or design-heavy tasks
Data terms require careful review before repository access
devin-cognition.name: Devin (Cognition)
pros: Full development environment under the agent's control
Clear PR-based output for human review
devin-cognition.files: Full repository access within its sandboxed environment.
devin-cognition.value: An agent that operates like a developer: it has its own browser, terminal, and code editor, receives a task description, and works through it with minimal handholding. Positioned at longer-horizon autonomous engineering rather than inline assistance.
devin-cognition.engine: Cognition's own model trained specifically for software engineering.
devin-cognition.latency: Hours for substantial tasks. Not an interactive tool.

pricing.includes: Task completion, PR generation, repository access

devin-cognition.quality: Capable on well-defined tasks with clear success criteria. Less reliable on ambiguous requirements or highly context-dependent design decisions.
devin-cognition.tagline: The first commercially available AI software engineer, with its own computer.
use_cases: Autonomous feature development from a brief to a pull request
Bug investigation and fix across an unfamiliar codebase
Repetitive engineering tasks such as migrations and test generation at scale
integrations: Standard developer tooling via its sandboxed environment
devin-cognition.governance_note: This tool makes the agentic governance question concrete: an AI that can commit code, open PRs, and execute commands at the repository level is performing actions with consequences that outlast the session. Three controls are not optional: branch and PR policies that prevent direct commits to main, mandatory human code review before merge, and secrets management that ensures credentials are never in the repository Devin can access. The audit evidence is the git history. If you cannot reconstruct what an agent changed and why, you do not have a defensible record.
devin-cognition.training_optout: Verify data terms before giving repository access containing sensitive code.

google-drive-ai.name: Google Drive AI
google-drive-ai.value: Gemini in Drive summarises documents and folders, answers questions across files and improves search, under Workspace terms, and is included in business plans. It turns Drive into a knowledge assistant without exporting data.
google-drive-ai.tagline: Gemini in Drive: summarise files, ask questions across documents and find things in plain language.
google-drive-ai.governance_note: Gemini sees what the user can see; sharing hygiene is the control.
google-drive-ai.training_optout: Workspace data is not used to train Gemini.

mistral-le-chat.api: REST API with SDKs, plus open weights for the models released that way.
cons: Behind the frontier on hardest reasoning
Smaller ecosystem than the US majors
Open and proprietary model split is easy to confuse
mistral-le-chat.name: Mistral / Le Chat
pros: Genuine EU alternative with real data residency options
Excellent cost and speed at the smaller sizes
mistral-le-chat.files: Document and image handling on the hosted product. Self-hosted capability depends on the serving stack.
mistral-le-chat.value: A capable frontier model family from a European company, with several models released under open weights. For organizations whose constraint is where the data goes rather than which model scores highest, that combination is often decisive.
mistral-le-chat.engine: Mistral's own model family. Several models are released under Apache 2.0; the largest are proprietary.
mistral-le-chat.latency: The smaller models are notably fast and cheap to run, which is a large part of their appeal for high-volume work.
mistral-le-chat.quality: Competitive, particularly for the size and cost. Generally behind the largest US frontier models on the hardest reasoning tasks.
mistral-le-chat.tagline: The European frontier lab, and the usual answer when data must stay in the EU.
use_cases: Deploying a capable assistant where EU data residency is a hard requirement
Self-hosting an open-weight model with a genuinely permissive licence
Reducing dependence on a single US model vendor
integrations: Hugging Face, Ollama, and standard self-hosting stacks
mistral-le-chat.governance_note: This is the clearest available answer to a GDPR transfer problem. Where a US vendor's data path forces a Chapter V transfer analysis, an EU-hosted or self-hosted European model avoids the question rather than mitigating it. Note the distinction between the Apache-licensed models and the proprietary ones, because only the former can actually be run on your own infrastructure.
mistral-le-chat.training_optout: Business and API terms address training use. Self-hosting removes the question entirely. Confirm the terms attached to your specific tier.

nvidia-nemotron.name: NVIDIA Nemotron
nvidia-nemotron.value: Nemotron models are open weights that NVIDIA releases to seed agent development on its platform, including reasoning models built on Llama and its own architectures, plus safety and retrieval models. They ship through NIM microservices and Hugging Face.
nvidia-nemotron.tagline: NVIDIA's family of open models for reasoning, agents and synthetic data, tuned to run on NVIDIA hardware.
nvidia-nemotron.governance_note: Read the NVIDIA Open Model Licence; it is permissive but not identical to Apache. Self hosting keeps data in house.

operator-openai.api: OpenAI Responses API for embedding web browsing in applications.
cons: Consumer data terms differ from enterprise
Real-world commitments require explicit authorization scope
Credential access creates phishing attack surface
operator-openai.name: Operator (OpenAI)
pros: Web task completion without user interaction for each step
operator-openai.files: Web content encountered during task execution.
operator-openai.value: A web-browsing agent that completes tasks on the open web on behalf of the user: booking, ordering, form completion, and web-based research without the user typing each step. The first OpenAI product to take actions with real-world consequences by default.
operator-openai.engine: GPT models with computer use capabilities for browser control.
operator-openai.latency: Task completion takes minutes to hours depending on complexity.

pricing.includes: Web browsing tool integration in API applications

operator-openai.quality: Capable for well-defined web tasks. Less reliable on complex multi-step transactions or sites with unusual flows.
operator-openai.tagline: OpenAI's consumer computer-use agent, currently the widest-deployed agentic AI product.
use_cases: Completing multi-step web tasks such as booking, ordering, and form submission
Web research that requires clicking through multiple sources rather than a single search
Automating repetitive web workflows on behalf of an individual user
integrations: OpenAI Responses API for developer embedding
operator-openai.governance_note: The first mainstream product to make 'AI can do things on the web on your behalf' a consumer experience rather than a developer build. The governance questions are: what is it authorized to commit, what credentials does it access, and what happens if it completes the wrong transaction. For enterprise use, those are policy decisions. For consumer use, they are the user's problem, which is part of why the enterprise and consumer versions need different evaluations. Phishing attacks that impersonate Operator to capture credentials are an emerging threat model that comes with this capability.
operator-openai.training_optout: OpenAI's commercial and consumer terms differ. Consumer ChatGPT data terms apply unless the enterprise API is used. Operator actions are taken under the user's session on third-party sites.

premiere-pro-ai.api: Through Adobe APIs and the Firefly Services API for enterprise.
premiere-pro-ai.name: Premiere Pro AI
pros: Firefly content is trained on licensed material
Generative extend solves a real editing problem
premiere-pro-ai.files: All professional video and audio formats.
premiere-pro-ai.value: Premiere Pro added generative extend, which lengthens a shot by a couple of seconds, text based editing from transcripts, enhance speech and automatic colour and audio matching, all under Adobe's commercially safe Firefly terms. It remains the professional editor for teams that need the full timeline.
premiere-pro-ai.engine: Adobe Sensei and Firefly video models.
premiere-pro-ai.latency: Generative features take seconds to minutes.
premiere-pro-ai.tagline: Adobe's professional editor with Firefly powered generative extend, text based editing and AI audio tools.
premiere-pro-ai.governance_note: Firefly's licensed training data and enterprise indemnity are the reasons regulated brands use Adobe generative features over alternatives; Content Credentials should stay attached to exports.
premiere-pro-ai.training_optout: Adobe does not train Firefly on customer content; confirm the analytics settings in the admin console.

semantic-kernel.api: SDKs for .NET, Python, and Java. Plugins can be native functions, prompt templates, OpenAPI specifications, or Model Context Protocol servers.
cons: In maintenance mode since April 2026: new feature investment goes to Agent Framework, so new projects should start there
Smaller ecosystem and fewer third-party tutorials than LangChain
Enterprise abstraction layers add indirection that a direct SDK call would avoid for simple applications
semantic-kernel.name: Semantic Kernel
pros: First-class .NET and Java support, which most competing frameworks do not offer
Model-agnostic and deployable anywhere, with no Azure lock-in despite the Microsoft origin
Plugins can wrap OpenAPI specs and MCP servers, so existing services become tools without rewriting them
Existing plugins and connectors carry forward to Agent Framework rather than requiring a rewrite
semantic-kernel.files: Vector store integrations including Azure AI Search, Elasticsearch, and Chroma. Multimodal support for text, vision, and audio.
semantic-kernel.value: An open-source, MIT-licensed SDK that sits between application code and the model, handling plugins, connectors, memory, and agent orchestration. Its distinguishing feature has always been reach into languages and stacks the Python-first frameworks do not serve: C# and .NET first, then Python and Java, running on any cloud or on-premises with no Azure requirement. For enterprise teams whose systems are already .NET, it answered the question of how to add agents without abandoning the platform the team knows.
semantic-kernel.engine: Framework. Model-agnostic, with connectors for OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Hugging Face, Amazon Bedrock, Ollama, and others.
semantic-kernel.status: Maintenance mode. Microsoft shipped Agent Framework 1.0 on 3 April 2026 as the successor; Semantic Kernel continues to receive critical fixes and security patches but no new feature work.
semantic-kernel.latency: Framework overhead is minimal. Latency is dominated by model and vector store calls.

pricing.includes: Full SDK under MIT licence. Model and vector store costs are separate.

semantic-kernel.quality: Mature and widely deployed in enterprise .NET environments, with multi-agent orchestration patterns (sequential, concurrent, group chat, handoff) shipped in the SDK. The forward-looking caveat is the maintenance-mode status: new capability now lands in Agent Framework.
semantic-kernel.tagline: Microsoft's orchestration SDK for teams building AI into existing .NET, Python, or Java applications, now succeeded by Agent Framework.
use_cases: Adding agents and LLM calls to existing .NET, C#, or Java enterprise applications
Multi-agent orchestration where specialised agents coordinate on a task
Exposing existing business logic to a model as callable plugins
semantic-kernel.governance_note: Semantic Kernel is orchestration, not policy: the governance surface of an application built on it is the model it calls, the data its connectors reach, and the plugins it is permitted to execute. Because plugins can wrap arbitrary native functions, OpenAPI endpoints, and MCP servers, the load-bearing control is which plugins are registered and what they are allowed to do. The maintenance-mode status is itself a governance fact worth recording: a dependency receiving only security patches has a different lifecycle risk than one under active development, and that belongs in the architecture review rather than being discovered at the next upgrade.
semantic-kernel.training_optout: Framework only. Data handling is determined entirely by the model and store providers configured.

adobe-express-ai.name: Adobe Express AI
adobe-express-ai.value: Express is the fast design tool for social posts, flyers and videos, with Firefly text to image and template generation, background removal, animation and brand controls, under Adobe's commercially safe content terms. It is included in many Creative Cloud and enterprise plans.
adobe-express-ai.tagline: Adobe's Canva competitor with Firefly generation, templates and brand kits for quick marketing content.
adobe-express-ai.governance_note: Firefly indemnity on enterprise plans makes it the safe generator for brand work; Content Credentials should stay attached.
adobe-express-ai.training_optout: Adobe does not train Firefly on customer content.

adobe-podcast-ai.name: Adobe Podcast AI
adobe-podcast-ai.value: Adobe Podcast's Enhance Speech turns laptop and phone recordings into studio sounding audio with one upload, and the web editor cuts by transcript. It is free for a few hours a month, which made it the default cleanup step for many podcasters.
adobe-podcast-ai.tagline: Enhance Speech and transcript editing for podcasts, free from Adobe with Creative Cloud upgrades.
adobe-podcast-ai.governance_note: Adobe terms apply; uploads are processed in Adobe's cloud.
adobe-podcast-ai.training_optout: Adobe does not train on customer content; check the content analysis setting.

amazon-sagemaker.name: Amazon SageMaker
amazon-sagemaker.value: SageMaker covers the classic ML lifecycle, notebooks, training jobs, model registry, endpoints and monitoring, and AWS merged it with its lakehouse and analytics services into a single studio, with Bedrock handling foundation model access alongside. It is where AWS customers run custom models.
amazon-sagemaker.engine: Not a model; the platform for your models and hosted open models via JumpStart.
amazon-sagemaker.tagline: AWS's platform for building, training and deploying machine learning models, now unified with its data and analytics tools.
amazon-sagemaker.governance_note: Model cards, lineage and monitoring are built in; the review question is whether teams use them. Endpoints need the same access control as any API.
amazon-sagemaker.training_optout: AWS does not use customer data to train its services.

bark-for-schools.name: Bark for Schools
bark-for-schools.value: Bark for Schools monitors Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 school accounts with AI that flags concerning content and alerts administrators, free to US schools, with a paid parent product. It sits in the student monitoring category alongside Gaggle and GoGuardian.
bark-for-schools.tagline: Free student safety monitoring that scans school accounts for signs of self harm, bullying and violence.
bark-for-schools.governance_note: Student monitoring is a policy decision with privacy, equity and legal dimensions; disclose it to families and define who responds to alerts and how.
bark-for-schools.training_optout: Bark states student data is not used for training; confirm.

connected-papers.name: Connected Papers
connected-papers.value: Connected Papers takes one paper and draws a graph of related work by co citation and bibliographic coupling, with prior and derivative works, which is the fastest way to map a field you do not know. It is a small tool with a loyal following.
connected-papers.engine: Similarity algorithms over Semantic Scholar data.
connected-papers.tagline: Visual graphs of related papers built from citation similarity, for exploring a field from one paper.

cons: Clone quality varies with training audio
descript-overdub.name: Descript Overdub
descript-overdub.value: Overdub creates a clone of your voice from a consent recording so that edits to the transcript can be spoken in your voice, which removes retakes from podcast and video editing. It ships inside Descript rather than as a standalone product.

pricing.limits: Overdub vocabulary and minutes by plan

descript-overdub.tagline: Descript's voice cloning feature that lets you fix a recording by typing the corrected words.
descript-overdub.governance_note: The consent recording is the control; your policy should say who may create an Overdub of an employee and when it is deleted.
descript-overdub.training_optout: Descript states customer content is not used to train shared models; confirm.

final-cut-pro-ai.name: Final Cut Pro AI
final-cut-pro-ai.value: Final Cut Pro runs its AI features on Apple silicon: transcribe to captions, enhance light and colour, voice isolation and a magnetic mask that cuts subjects without a green screen. It is the choice for Mac based teams who want speed and a one time purchase.
final-cut-pro-ai.tagline: Apple's professional editor on Mac and iPad with on device AI for transcription, enhance light and sound, and magnetic mask.
final-cut-pro-ai.governance_note: On device processing keeps footage local; the governance work is device management, not vendor review.

google-ai-studio.api: Yes. The Gemini API, with keys issued here.
cons: Free tier data may be used to improve Google products
Not the production path; Vertex is
google-ai-studio.name: Google AI Studio
pros: Free access to frontier models for prototyping
First place new Gemini features appear
google-ai-studio.files: Images, audio, video and documents in the workbench and API.
google-ai-studio.value: AI Studio is the fastest way to try Gemini: a browser workbench, a free API key with generous limits, and the latest models before they reach the enterprise console. It is a prototyping tool, and Google's own docs point production work to Vertex AI.

pricing.includes: All public Gemini models, API keys

google-ai-studio.tagline: Google's free developer workbench for Gemini: prompts, keys and prototypes before you touch Vertex.
use_cases: Trying a new Gemini model the day it ships
Prompt development before moving to Vertex
google-ai-studio.governance_note: The free tier's terms allow Google to use inputs to improve its products, which is the reason not to paste work data into it. Paid use and Vertex AI carry the enterprise terms; make that the rule for anything confidential.
google-ai-studio.training_optout: Free tier content may be used to improve Google services; paid API and Vertex AI do not use customer data for training. Confirm the current terms.

google-translate.name: Google Translate
google-translate.value: Google Translate added over a hundred languages in 2024 using its PaLM 2 model and continues to improve with Gemini, with camera translation, conversation mode and offline packs, free to everyone. It is the default for breadth of languages.
google-translate.engine: Google neural translation and Gemini models.
google-translate.tagline: The most used translation service, covering over 240 languages with text, speech, camera and conversation modes.
google-translate.governance_note: Consumer use runs under Google account terms; use the Cloud API for business documents.
google-translate.training_optout: Cloud API data is not used for training; consumer settings govern the app.

google-vertex-ai.api: REST API and Google Cloud SDK.
cons: Third-party model licences need independent review
google-vertex-ai.name: Google Vertex AI
pros: Gemini family under enterprise GCP controls
End-to-end ML platform in one place
GCP residency and IAM controls for regulated industries
google-vertex-ai.files: Training data, models, and inference payloads in GCP storage formats.
google-vertex-ai.value: Google's unified ML platform for training, deployment, and management, with Gemini and third-party models available under GCP's enterprise controls. The enterprise answer when the organization is already on GCP and needs both the Gemini family and ML platform capabilities in one place.
google-vertex-ai.engine: Gemini model family plus third-party and open-source models available through Model Garden.
google-vertex-ai.latency: Comparable to other cloud model endpoints.
google-vertex-ai.quality: Gemini models under GCP controls. Same quality characteristics, different data terms.
google-vertex-ai.tagline: Google's enterprise AI platform: model deployment, MLOps, and Gemini under GCP controls.
use_cases: Deploying and managing ML and generative AI at enterprise scale under GCP
Accessing Gemini models with GCP's IAM, VNET, and residency controls
Building end-to-end ML pipelines with managed training, evaluation, and serving
integrations: Full GCP ecosystem: BigQuery, Cloud Storage, IAM, VNET
Vertex AI Workbench, Pipelines, and Feature Store
Same Gemini API surface as the developer product
google-vertex-ai.governance_note: Same data-path logic as Azure OpenAI: enterprise controls convert a consumer data-handling question into an enterprise compliance question. Residency and VNET are the controls to confirm. Model Garden also surfaces third-party and open-source models with their own licences, so licence review applies to those selections even though they are accessed through a managed platform.
google-vertex-ai.training_optout: GCP enterprise terms: customer data is not used to train Google's models. Verify via the GCP Data Processing Amendment.

imagine-learning.name: Imagine Learning
imagine-learning.value: Imagine Learning sells adaptive programs for English learners, reading and math plus core curriculum, and added an AI assistant for teachers to plan from its content. Its AI is a mix of long standing adaptivity and newer generative help.
imagine-learning.engine: Imagine Learning's adaptive engines with partner LLMs.
imagine-learning.tagline: Digital curriculum company with adaptive language, literacy and math programs and an AI assistant for teachers.
imagine-learning.governance_note: Standard district data agreement; generative assistant output should be reviewed by teachers.

jasper-campaigns.name: Jasper Campaigns
jasper-campaigns.value: Campaigns takes a brief and produces the connected set of assets, emails, landing copy, ads, social posts, in the brand voice, so a launch is drafted in one pass. It is a feature of Jasper rather than a separate product.

pricing.tier: Included with Jasper Pro and Business

jasper-campaigns.tagline: Jasper's campaign feature that generates every asset for a launch from one brief.
jasper-campaigns.governance_note: Same as Jasper; regulated claims need review.

oracle-fusion-ai.name: Oracle Fusion AI
oracle-fusion-ai.value: Oracle built dozens of AI agents into Fusion applications, for ledger reconciliation, payables, HR questions, supply chain exceptions and sales, and includes them in the subscription rather than charging separately, which has pressured SAP and Workday. The agents run on OCI with Oracle's data terms.
oracle-fusion-ai.engine: Partner and Oracle models on OCI.
oracle-fusion-ai.tagline: Embedded AI agents and generative features across Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, HCM, SCM and CX, included at no extra charge.
oracle-fusion-ai.governance_note: Same financial control rule as SAP Joule; Oracle's agent studio lets admins scope what each agent may do.
oracle-fusion-ai.training_optout: Oracle does not use customer data to train models.

presentations-ai.name: Presentations.AI
presentations-ai.value: Presentations.AI generates decks from prompts and documents with a focus on brand matching and clean PowerPoint export, competing with Gamma for business teams who need .pptx output. It is a smaller player.
presentations-ai.tagline: Deck generator with brand sync and PowerPoint compatibility for business users.

semantic-scholar.name: Semantic Scholar
semantic-scholar.value: Semantic Scholar indexes over two hundred million papers with AI summaries, influential citation counts and research feeds, and its open API underpins many other research tools including Consensus and Elicit. It is free and run by a nonprofit.
semantic-scholar.tagline: Free academic search engine from AI2 with AI generated summaries, citation graphs and an open API.
use_cases: Building research tools on the API
semantic-scholar.governance_note: Nonprofit, open data; nothing to review beyond rate limits.

snowflake-arctic.name: Snowflake Arctic
snowflake-arctic.value: Arctic is Snowflake's open model family, an LLM tuned for SQL and enterprise tasks and strong embedding models, built so customers can run AI where their data lives without exporting it. The embedding models are the lasting piece; Cortex also hosts frontier models.
snowflake-arctic.tagline: Snowflake's open enterprise LLM and embedding models, served inside Cortex AI.
use_cases: Embeddings for search over Snowflake data
snowflake-arctic.governance_note: Keeping inference inside Snowflake means warehouse access controls apply to AI use, which simplifies the review.
snowflake-arctic.training_optout: Snowflake does not train on customer data.

snowflake-cortex.name: Snowflake Cortex
snowflake-cortex.value: Cortex exposes LLM functions in SQL, document search, an analyst agent that answers questions over tables and a studio for building agents, all inside Snowflake's governance so data never leaves. Models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Mistral are available in region.
snowflake-cortex.tagline: AI functions, search and agents inside Snowflake, running frontier and open models next to the data.
snowflake-cortex.governance_note: Warehouse role based access governs AI access automatically; the review is cost control and model selection.
snowflake-cortex.training_optout: Snowflake and model partners do not train on customer data.

stable-diffusion.api: REST API for the hosted service; locally, whatever pipeline you build.
cons: Licence terms vary by release and need reading each time
stable-diffusion.name: Stable Diffusion
pros: Fully self-hostable, nothing leaves your infrastructure
stable-diffusion.files: Text prompts, image inputs, masks, and control inputs depending on the pipeline.
stable-diffusion.value: Open-weight image generation that can run entirely on your own hardware. The only mainstream option where confidential visual work never leaves the building, and the base for most of the fine-tuning ecosystem.
stable-diffusion.engine: Stability AI's open-weight diffusion models, in several generations and sizes.
stable-diffusion.latency: Hardware dependent. Fast on a capable GPU, slow on CPU.
stable-diffusion.quality: Very good, and highly controllable through the surrounding tooling. Base output aesthetics generally trail Midjourney; controllability is far ahead.
stable-diffusion.tagline: The open-weight image model that made local, private image generation possible.
use_cases: Generating imagery on confidential product or brand material locally
Fine-tuning a model on an organization's own visual style
integrations: The broad open ecosystem of interfaces and fine-tuning tools
stable-diffusion.governance_note: Licensing is the thing to check, not capability. Stability's model licences have changed across releases and some carry revenue-linked commercial conditions, so the licence attached to the specific checkpoint matters more than the family name. Separately, the training-data provenance litigation affecting the category applies here too: self-hosting removes the data-exposure risk but not the copyright question about outputs.
stable-diffusion.training_optout: Self-hosted use means nothing leaves your infrastructure. Hosted use follows Stability's terms.

tensorflow-keras.name: TensorFlow / Keras
tensorflow-keras.value: TensorFlow remains widely deployed in production, on mobile through LiteRT and in Google's own systems, and Keras 3 runs on TensorFlow, JAX and PyTorch, which keeps it relevant as a high level API. Research moved to PyTorch; production and edge did not entirely.
tensorflow-keras.tagline: Google's deep learning framework and the Keras high level API, now multi backend and strongest in production and mobile deployment.
tensorflow-keras.governance_note: Same supply chain rule as PyTorch.

anthropic-console.api: Yes. The console issues keys for the Claude API and the Admin API.
cons: Administrative, not a product end users touch
Rate limits step up with spend, which slows new accounts
Separate billing from the Claude consumer plans
anthropic-console.name: Anthropic Console
pros: Workbench for iterating prompts with real model output
Organisation level keys, roles and spend limits
Prompt caching and batch controls reduce cost
anthropic-console.files: Files API for documents and images used in prompts.
anthropic-console.value: The console is where a team manages Claude API access, tests prompts in the Workbench, sets spend limits and reads usage, and it is the entry point for the Claude Developer Platform's batch, files and agent features. It is an administration surface rather than a product in its own right.
anthropic-console.tagline: Anthropic's developer console: API keys, usage, billing and a workbench for Claude prompts.
use_cases: Managing API access for a team
Monitoring spend by key and workspace
integrations: Amazon Bedrock and Google Vertex AI as alternative routes to the same models
anthropic-console.governance_note: Workspaces and per key limits are the controls to use: one workspace per application, a spend cap on every key, and the Admin API to pull usage into your own reporting. API inputs are not used for training under the commercial terms.
anthropic-console.training_optout: Commercial API terms exclude training on customer data by default; zero data retention is available by agreement.

cons: Some add ons call cloud services silently
blender-ai-addons.name: Blender AI Add-ons
blender-ai-addons.value: Blender has no built in generative AI; the ecosystem supplies it through add ons that generate textures with Stable Diffusion, create 3D meshes from prompts via external services, and assist animation. Blender's free licence and Python API make it the natural host for these experiments.
blender-ai-addons.engine: Varies by add on; local diffusion models or external APIs.

pricing.limits: Blender is free; add ons vary

blender-ai-addons.tagline: The open source 3D suite extended with community add ons for AI texturing, generation and animation assistance.
blender-ai-addons.governance_note: Check whether an add on sends scene data to a cloud service; several do. Model licences for commercial use vary.

goguardian-beacon.name: GoGuardian Beacon
goguardian-beacon.value: Beacon analyses student web activity and documents for self harm indicators and routes alerts to designated staff with response workflows, built into GoGuardian's device management and filtering platform. It is widely deployed on Chromebooks.
goguardian-beacon.tagline: Suicide and self harm risk detection across school devices and accounts, part of GoGuardian's classroom management suite.
goguardian-beacon.governance_note: Same policy and disclosure rule as the category; define response protocols before enabling.

google-meet-notes.name: Google Meet notes (Take notes for me)
google-meet-notes.value: Take notes for me produces a Google Doc of notes and actions as the meeting runs, shares it with attendees and summarises what a late joiner missed, included in Workspace business and education tiers. It is the botless Google counterpart to Fireflies.
google-meet-notes.tagline: Gemini feature in Meet that writes notes and action items into a Doc during the meeting.
google-meet-notes.catalog_name: Google Meet notes (Take notes for me)
google-meet-notes.governance_note: Participants are notified when notes are on; policy should say when it may be used with students or parents.
google-meet-notes.training_optout: Workspace data is not used for training.

google-notebooklm.name: Google NotebookLM
google-notebooklm.files: PDFs, Docs, slides, web pages, audio, video.
google-notebooklm.value: NotebookLM answers questions with citations to the sources you upload, generates podcast style audio overviews, study guides, quizzes and video explainers, and is available free and in Workspace with enterprise terms. It is the tool for learning from a specific set of documents.
google-notebooklm.tagline: Source grounded research assistant that answers only from documents you add, with audio overviews, mind maps and video explainers.
google-notebooklm.governance_note: Consumer NotebookLM follows personal account terms; use the Workspace version for company documents so data terms apply.
google-notebooklm.training_optout: Workspace data is not used for training; consumer terms differ.

cons: Limited story library in some languages
google-read-along.name: Google Read Along
google-read-along.value: Read Along uses on device speech recognition so children can read stories aloud and get help with words they stumble on, free, without ads and without sending audio to Google, with a classroom version for teachers. It is Google's counterpart to Microsoft Reading Coach.
google-read-along.tagline: Free reading practice app and web tool where a character, Diya, listens to children read and helps with words.
integrations: Google Classroom for the classroom version
google-read-along.governance_note: On device processing means no voice data leaves; the classroom version adds Google Workspace for Education terms.
google-read-along.training_optout: Audio is not sent to Google.

insilico-medicine.name: Insilico Medicine
insilico-medicine.value: Insilico uses generative models to identify targets and design molecules, and its lung fibrosis drug reached Phase 2 as the first drug with both target and molecule discovered by AI, with the company listing in Hong Kong. Its Pharma.AI platform is licensed to pharmaceutical companies.
insilico-medicine.engine: Insilico's generative chemistry and target discovery models.
insilico-medicine.tagline: AI drug discovery company whose generative chemistry platform produced the first AI discovered drug to reach late stage trials.
insilico-medicine.governance_note: Relevant to life sciences AI governance: model outputs enter regulated development, so FDA guidance on AI in drug development applies.

microsoft-copilot.api: Available through Azure OpenAI for direct model access, and extensible via Copilot Studio.
cons: Expensive per seat, and value varies widely by role
microsoft-copilot.name: Microsoft Copilot
pros: Governance and identity continuity with existing Microsoft tenancy
Grounded in the organization's own content
Easiest enterprise procurement path for Microsoft shops
microsoft-copilot.files: Works against the organization's existing Microsoft 365 content, which is the point. Standard document and spreadsheet handling.
microsoft-copilot.value: Reaches into Outlook, Word, Excel, Teams, and SharePoint with the organization's own content, under existing Microsoft tenancy, identity, and compliance controls. For most large enterprises that governance continuity matters more than raw model quality.
microsoft-copilot.engine: Primarily OpenAI models running under Microsoft's enterprise infrastructure, with Microsoft's own models in some surfaces.
microsoft-copilot.latency: Adequate. Perceived speed varies considerably by host application.

pricing.includes: In-app AI across Microsoft 365, tenant grounding, admin controls
Direct model access under Azure controls

microsoft-copilot.quality: Model quality is competitive. The differentiator is grounding in the tenant's own data with permissions respected, not standalone reasoning.
microsoft-copilot.tagline: AI embedded in Microsoft 365, where most enterprise work already happens.
use_cases: Summarising Teams meetings and long Outlook threads
Drafting and analysing directly inside Word and Excel against internal documents
Surfacing answers from SharePoint and internal knowledge under existing permissions
microsoft-copilot.governance_note: Because it inherits existing Microsoft 365 permissions, it will surface anything a user already had access to. Organizations with permissive legacy SharePoint permissions frequently discover the problem only after deployment. Fix permissions before rollout, not after.
microsoft-copilot.training_optout: Commercial data protection applies to licensed enterprise use: prompts and responses are not used to train foundation models. The free consumer tier operates under different terms.

openai-playground.api: Yes. Keys from here serve the OpenAI API and the Administration API.
cons: Projects and organisations confuse new teams
Playground costs real money if left open
Features move between dashboard sections often
openai-playground.name: OpenAI Playground / Dashboard
pros: Projects separate keys, limits and spend by application
Playground covers chat, realtime, assistants and image models
Usage dashboards by project and key
openai-playground.files: Files API for documents, batch inputs and fine tuning data.
openai-playground.value: The dashboard is the administration side of the OpenAI API: project and key management, usage and cost reporting, rate limits, fine tuning jobs, evals and the Playground for trying models and tools before writing code. Most developers see it before they see the API itself.

pricing.includes: Playground use is billed at API rates

openai-playground.tagline: OpenAI's developer dashboard: keys, usage, limits and a playground for every model in the API.
use_cases: Testing a prompt against several models
Managing API keys and budgets for a team
Running fine tuning and eval jobs
integrations: Azure OpenAI as the Microsoft route
openai-playground.governance_note: Use one project per application and set a monthly budget on each; the organisation level spend limit is the backstop. API and Playground use is not used for training under the API terms, unlike the consumer ChatGPT default.
openai-playground.training_optout: API data is not used for training by default; zero data retention available for eligible endpoints.

cons: Chinese parent company for data questions
wondershare-virbo.name: Wondershare Virbo
wondershare-virbo.value: Virbo brings avatar presenters, video translation and photo talking into the Wondershare family alongside Filmora, at consumer prices. It serves small businesses and creators who already use Wondershare software.
wondershare-virbo.engine: Wondershare's licensed avatar and voice models.
wondershare-virbo.tagline: Wondershare's avatar video and video translation tool, bundled into its consumer creative suite.
wondershare-virbo.governance_note: Consumer tool; keep business use to non sensitive content and check where uploads are processed.

zoom-ai-companion.api: Zoom API; AI features in product.
zoom-ai-companion.name: Zoom AI Companion
zoom-ai-companion.value: AI Companion summarises meetings, lets late joiners ask what they missed, drafts chat and email, and extends into docs and tasks, included with paid Zoom plans at no extra cost, which pressured rivals. Zoom's 2023 terms controversy over training data shaped its current no training promise.
zoom-ai-companion.engine: Zoom's federated approach using its own and partner models.
zoom-ai-companion.tagline: Meeting summaries, in meeting questions, chat drafting and tasks across Zoom, included with paid plans.
zoom-ai-companion.governance_note: Meeting summaries are records and participants must be told; admins control which features are on and whether summaries are retained.
zoom-ai-companion.training_optout: Zoom does not use customer content to train its AI models.

apple-intelligence.api: Foundation Models framework for app developers.
apple-intelligence.name: Apple Intelligence
apple-intelligence.value: Apple Intelligence runs small models on the device for writing tools, summaries, notifications and image features, and routes harder requests to Private Cloud Compute, Apple silicon servers that keep data unreadable to Apple. Siri's deeper overhaul arrived in stages, and third party models including ChatGPT can be invoked with consent.
apple-intelligence.engine: Apple's foundation models on device and in Private Cloud Compute; partner models by consent.
apple-intelligence.tagline: Apple's on device and Private Cloud Compute AI across iPhone, iPad and Mac, with ChatGPT and other models as optional extensions.
apple-intelligence.governance_note: Private Cloud Compute is the strongest privacy design among consumer assistants and is independently inspectable; the enterprise question is whether MDM policies allow the ChatGPT extension.
apple-intelligence.training_optout: Apple does not use personal data from Apple Intelligence requests for training.

cons: US caselaw focus limits international utility
Less generalist than Harvey for corporate transactional work
casetext-cocounsel.name: CoCounsel (Casetext)
pros: Deep Westlaw integration for US law
Established trust record in law firms
casetext-cocounsel.files: Legal documents, contracts, deposition transcripts, and production sets.
casetext-cocounsel.value: AI legal research and document analysis from Casetext, now part of Thomson Reuters. Deep integration with Westlaw and a long track record in US legal research distinguish it from newer entrants.
casetext-cocounsel.engine: Built on GPT-4 with legal-domain fine-tuning and Westlaw retrieval.
casetext-cocounsel.quality: Strongest on US common law. The Thomson Reuters integration gives it a sourcing depth other tools lack. Still requires lawyer review.
casetext-cocounsel.tagline: Legal AI from Thomson Reuters, strongest on US caselaw and legal research.
use_cases: US caselaw research and citation checking
Deposition preparation and key issue extraction from document productions
Contract analysis and quick-turn research memos
casetext-cocounsel.governance_note: Same professional responsibility framing as Harvey: the tool accelerates, the lawyer is still accountable. The Westlaw integration is specifically valuable for the sourcing chain, because a hallucinated citation is immediately checkable rather than requiring a separate lookup. Attorney-client privilege analysis for the data path applies as with any legal AI.
casetext-cocounsel.training_optout: Thomson Reuters / Casetext terms govern customer data use. Verify under the current agreement.

davinci-resolve-ai.name: DaVinci Resolve AI
pros: Local AI processing keeps footage on the machine
Best colour tools in the market
davinci-resolve-ai.value: DaVinci Resolve is the professional alternative to Premiere with a free version that covers most needs and a Studio licence that unlocks the neural engine: magic mask, voice isolation, smart reframe, transcript editing and speed warp. The one time licence rather than a subscription is a draw.
davinci-resolve-ai.engine: Blackmagic's neural engine running locally on the GPU.
davinci-resolve-ai.tagline: Blackmagic's free professional editor and colour suite, with neural engine features in the paid Studio version.
use_cases: Professional editing and colour on a budget
davinci-resolve-ai.governance_note: Local processing means nothing leaves the workstation, which is the governance argument for it over cloud editors. Collaboration features add a database server to secure.

jamf-ai-governance.name: Jamf AI Governance
jamf-ai-governance.value: Jamf lets IT control which AI features and apps are allowed on managed Apple devices, including Apple Intelligence settings, the ChatGPT extension and third party AI apps, as part of its device management. It is governance at the endpoint rather than the model.
jamf-ai-governance.tagline: Device level controls for AI features on Apple devices, managing Apple Intelligence and AI app access through Jamf.
use_cases: Restricting AI features on corporate Macs and iPhones
jamf-ai-governance.governance_note: Shadow AI control starts at the device; this is one of the few tools that enforces it on Apple hardware.

microsoft-designer.name: Microsoft Designer
microsoft-designer.value: Designer generates images and layouts from a prompt, edits photos, removes backgrounds and turns ideas into social posts, and its generator is the one behind Copilot's image creation. It is free with a Microsoft account.
microsoft-designer.tagline: Microsoft's free design app with image generation, templates and editing, tied to Copilot and Microsoft 365.
microsoft-designer.governance_note: Consumer and work accounts differ in data terms; use the work account for business content.
microsoft-designer.training_optout: Microsoft 365 commercial terms exclude training on customer content.

microsoft-teams-ai.name: Microsoft Teams AI
microsoft-teams-ai.value: Teams delivers Copilot during and after meetings, answering questions about what was said, producing recaps with actions and speaker timelines, and summarising channels and chats, under Microsoft 365 commercial terms. It is the default for Microsoft organisations.
microsoft-teams-ai.engine: Microsoft Copilot over OpenAI and Microsoft models.
microsoft-teams-ai.tagline: Copilot in Teams: meeting recap, live questions, chat summaries and intelligent recap, with Copilot licensing.
microsoft-teams-ai.governance_note: Purview retention and sensitivity labels apply to recaps; configure them.
microsoft-teams-ai.training_optout: Microsoft 365 data is not used for training.

you-com-enterprise.name: You.com Enterprise
you-com-enterprise.value: You.com Enterprise gives companies the multi model AI search and research agents of You.com with connections to internal documents, SSO and no training on company data, plus APIs that supply web search grounding to other builders. It competes with Perplexity Enterprise and Glean.
you-com-enterprise.engine: Multiple frontier models with You.com's search index.
you-com-enterprise.tagline: Enterprise version of You.com's AI search and agents, with private data connections and admin controls.
use_cases: Grounding internal agents with web search
you-com-enterprise.governance_note: Connecting internal document stores to an AI search product is a data access decision; scope the connectors to what the whole company may see.
you-com-enterprise.training_optout: Enterprise data is not used for training.

automation-anywhere.api: Yes. Control room APIs for bot deployment and monitoring.
cons: Agent features are newer than the marketing suggests
automation-anywhere.name: Automation Anywhere
pros: Reaches systems that have no API
Mature governance, audit and credential vaults
automation-anywhere.files: Documents through its document AI; any application data through bots.
automation-anywhere.value: Automation Anywhere is one of the three large RPA vendors, selling bots that drive legacy applications through their screens, now extended with document AI, an agent builder and process intelligence. For enterprises with years of RPA investment it is the path to agents that can reach systems without APIs.
automation-anywhere.engine: Its own RPA runtime plus AI agents built on third party and partner models.

pricing.includes: Agents, document AI, process intelligence, support

automation-anywhere.quality: Dependable for well defined processes; agent judgement needs the same review as any model.
automation-anywhere.tagline: Enterprise RPA that has rebuilt itself around AI agents and a process orchestration layer.
use_cases: Finance and HR back office processes on legacy systems
Agents that combine RPA steps with model judgement
integrations: Microsoft, Google and AWS AI services
automation-anywhere.governance_note: RPA bots run with user credentials, often privileged ones, which is why the credential vault, bot level audit trail and segregation of duties matter more here than in a chat tool. Adding model judgement to a bot means the bot can now act on an inference, so define where a human signs off.
automation-anywhere.training_optout: Enterprise terms exclude training on customer data; model partner terms apply to AI steps. Confirm in your contract.

canva-for-education.name: Canva for Education
canva-for-education.value: Canva for Education provides the full design platform free to verified K12 schools with AI features for text, image and presentation generation, plus student safe settings and LMS integration. It is one of the most used creative tools in schools.
canva-for-education.engine: Canva's Magic Studio with partner models.
canva-for-education.tagline: Free Canva for K12 teachers and students with Magic Studio AI tools and classroom safeguards.
canva-for-education.governance_note: Student accounts have AI features filtered; districts sign Canva's education data agreement.
canva-for-education.training_optout: Canva for Education data is not used for training.

cons: Generative features blur the academic integrity line without an explicit policy
Admin analytics carry FERPA handling requirements
Free consumer installs can coexist with the campus licence and bypass controls
grammarly-education.name: Grammarly for Education
pros: Meaningful help at scale for non-native English writers
Admin oversight not available on consumer tier
grammarly-education.files: Text in place, in browsers and editors.
grammarly-education.value: Writing assistance deployed at institutional scale across students and staff, with campus admin controls and reporting. The product itself is the same as the business edition; the conversation around it is not.
grammarly-education.engine: Same as Grammarly. Proprietary models, some generative features on third-party models.
grammarly-education.tagline: The campus licence of Grammarly, and the centre of the academic integrity debate.
use_cases: Improving student writing clarity and mechanics at scale
Identifying writing patterns across the student body through admin analytics
Non-native English speakers developing academic writing competence
integrations: Learning management system connectors on some tiers
grammarly-education.governance_note: The governance question in education is not the product, it is the policy. Grammarly corrects grammar; the moment its generative features write sentences, the academic integrity question is live. Institutions need a clear published policy on which features are within-bounds and which are not, before deploying a campus licence rather than after the first academic misconduct case. The admin analytics also surface usage patterns that have FERPA implications if the data is not handled as an education record.
grammarly-education.training_optout: Institutional terms address data use. Confirm which terms apply to the specific agreement, not the product marketing.

microsoft-clipchamp.name: Microsoft Clipchamp AI
microsoft-clipchamp.value: Clipchamp is the editor most Microsoft 365 users already have, with automatic captions, AI voiceover, silence removal and an auto compose feature that cuts a video from clips and a brief. It is the safe choice for organisations that cannot use CapCut.
microsoft-clipchamp.tagline: Microsoft's browser based video editor with AI captions, voiceover and auto compose, included with Microsoft 365.
microsoft-clipchamp.governance_note: Microsoft 365 data terms apply, which is the reason to choose it over consumer editors for anything internal.
microsoft-clipchamp.training_optout: Microsoft 365 commercial terms exclude training on customer content.

cons: Face recognition is local and limited
microsoft-seeing-ai.name: Microsoft Seeing AI
microsoft-seeing-ai.value: Seeing AI reads short text instantly, scans documents, recognises people, describes scenes with generative AI and identifies products and currency, free on iOS and Android. It is a flagship accessibility application.
microsoft-seeing-ai.engine: Microsoft Azure AI vision and GPT models.
microsoft-seeing-ai.tagline: Free Microsoft app that narrates the world for blind and low vision users: text, people, scenes, currency and products.
microsoft-seeing-ai.governance_note: Microsoft's privacy statement applies; face recognition data stays on device.
microsoft-seeing-ai.training_optout: Microsoft does not use Seeing AI images for training.

cons: Feature overlap with free built ins
read-write-texthelp.name: Read&Write by Texthelp
read-write-texthelp.value: Read&Write is the established literacy support tool in schools, offering read aloud, word prediction, dictation, dictionary and highlighting across browsers and Office, and its maker, now Everway, added AI features for summarising and rewording text. It is often funded through accommodation plans.
read-write-texthelp.engine: Texthelp's own tools with partner LLMs for AI features.
read-write-texthelp.tagline: Literacy support toolbar for reading and writing, with text to speech, prediction, dictation and now AI summaries and simplification.
read-write-texthelp.governance_note: Student data agreements through the district; AI features process text with partner models.
read-write-texthelp.training_optout: Texthelp states student data is not used for training; confirm.

salesforce-einstein.api: Salesforce REST and Bulk API; Agentforce configurable via Salesforce Flow.
cons: Autonomous agents require explicit scope, disclosure, and escalation policy
Value highly dependent on CRM data quality
Pricing complexity is high across Salesforce's product portfolio
salesforce-einstein.name: Salesforce Einstein / Agentforce
pros: AI operating on existing CRM data without export or migration
Agentforce is capable at high-repetition customer service at scale
Zero Data Retention option for sensitive use cases
salesforce-einstein.files: Salesforce CRM data: contacts, opportunities, cases, and activity history.
salesforce-einstein.value: AI features across Salesforce: Einstein for predictions and recommendations within CRM data, and Agentforce for autonomous AI agents that can handle customer service, sales development, and support without human escalation. The integration with existing CRM data is the differentiation.
salesforce-einstein.engine: Salesforce's own Einstein models plus frontier model access via Salesforce infrastructure.

pricing.model: Einstein features bundled in some clouds; Agentforce per conversation

salesforce-einstein.quality: Strong when the underlying CRM data is clean and well-structured. Autonomous agents are capable within well-scoped, high-repetition service workflows.
salesforce-einstein.tagline: AI across the Salesforce platform, and the first major enterprise AI agent product at the CRM layer.
use_cases: AI-powered sales forecasting and opportunity scoring within Salesforce
Autonomous customer service agents handling tier-one cases without escalation
AI summarisation and next-step recommendations within Sales Cloud workflows
integrations: All Salesforce clouds: Sales, Service, Marketing, Commerce
Data Cloud for unified customer data
salesforce-einstein.governance_note: Agentforce is the clearest example of an autonomous customer-facing AI agent deployed at scale by a mainstream enterprise platform. The governance questions are: what can the agent commit to on behalf of the company, what happens when it gets it wrong, and how is that escalation path tested. Consumer-protection and financial-product regulations in several sectors require disclosures when a customer is interacting with AI rather than a human, and Agentforce interactions qualify. The disclosure requirement must be built into the agent's opening interaction, not treated as optional.
salesforce-einstein.training_optout: Salesforce Zero Data Retention policy available for Einstein features. Agentforce interactions are stored in Salesforce under its data terms. Verify for your specific clouds and contracts.

sensetime-sensechat.name: SenseTime SenseChat
sensetime-sensechat.value: SenseTime moved from facial recognition into foundation models with SenseNova and the SenseChat assistant, selling to Chinese enterprises and government with multimodal strength from its vision heritage. It is one of the six Chinese labs that released frontier scale models.
sensetime-sensechat.tagline: SenseTime's SenseNova model line and SenseChat assistant, from the computer vision company turned foundation model lab.
sensetime-sensechat.governance_note: SenseTime is sanctioned by the US over surveillance uses; not procurable for most Western organisations.

cons: Free period has an end date
chatgpt-for-teachers.name: ChatGPT for Teachers
chatgpt-for-teachers.value: ChatGPT for Teachers gives verified US K12 educators a free workspace with no training on their data, FERPA aligned terms, collaboration features and education templates, launched in late 2025 and free through mid 2027. It is OpenAI's answer to Gemini for Education.
chatgpt-for-teachers.tagline: OpenAI's free ChatGPT workspace for verified K12 educators in the US, with education data protections and shared prompts.
chatgpt-for-teachers.governance_note: Teacher workspace only; student data should still be minimised, and districts should approve use.
chatgpt-for-teachers.training_optout: Data in the educator workspace is not used for training.

duolingo-for-schools.name: Duolingo for Schools
duolingo-for-schools.value: Duolingo for Schools lets teachers assign and track Duolingo practice, and the app itself uses AI to generate content, personalise sessions and power conversation practice in its Max tier, after Duolingo declared itself AI first in 2025. It is widely used as supplementary language practice.
duolingo-for-schools.engine: Duolingo's models with partner LLMs for Max features.
duolingo-for-schools.tagline: Classroom dashboard for Duolingo's language app, whose lessons and AI features are generated and personalised with models.
duolingo-for-schools.governance_note: Under 13 accounts have restricted features; districts should check the student privacy terms.

cons: Student access policy decisions fall on districts
gemini-for-education.name: Gemini for Education
gemini-for-education.value: Google provides Gemini to education accounts free with enterprise grade data protections, letting admins turn it on for staff and students over 13, with teacher Gems, Classroom AI tools and NotebookLM. It is the default AI for Google schools.
gemini-for-education.tagline: Gemini in Google Workspace for Education with data protections, Gems for teachers and student access controls.
gemini-for-education.governance_note: Education data protections mean no training and no human review of prompts; districts still own the decision on student access by age.
gemini-for-education.training_optout: Education accounts are not used for training.

cons: Quality below DeepL for some pairs
microsoft-translator.name: Microsoft Translator
microsoft-translator.value: Microsoft Translator translates text, speech and images and runs live multilingual conversations where each person reads in their own language, used in classrooms and parent meetings. The same service powers translation across Microsoft 365.
microsoft-translator.tagline: Free translation app and service for text, speech and live multi device conversations, built on Azure AI Translator.
microsoft-translator.governance_note: Azure terms for the API; app use follows the Microsoft privacy statement.
microsoft-translator.training_optout: Azure does not train on customer data; app text may be used to improve services unless settings say otherwise.

cohere-command-r-plus.name: Cohere Command R+
cohere-command-r-plus.value: Command R+ was built for enterprise retrieval, citations and multi step tool use, released with weights under a non commercial licence and served commercially by API, and was followed by the Command A generation. It remains in use and in the cloud marketplaces.
cohere-command-r-plus.status: Active. Superseded by the Command A generation but still served.
cohere-command-r-plus.tagline: Cohere's 2024 flagship for RAG and tool use, with open weights for research and a successor line in Command A.
cohere-command-r-plus.governance_note: Weights are non commercial; production use goes through the API or a licence.
cohere-command-r-plus.training_optout: Cohere does not train on customer data.

crowdstrike-charlotte.api: Falcon API with Charlotte AI capabilities.
cons: Only useful if already running Falcon
Answer quality is limited by telemetry coverage
AI-assisted decisions still require human review for significant events
crowdstrike-charlotte.name: CrowdStrike Charlotte AI
pros: Grounded on your organization's own security data
Natural language dramatically lowers analyst query friction
No data leaves the Falcon platform boundary
crowdstrike-charlotte.files: Falcon platform telemetry: endpoint, identity, cloud, and network data.
crowdstrike-charlotte.value: Natural language access to the CrowdStrike Falcon telemetry: ask in English, get an answer grounded in your organization's own security data. Reduces the query burden on analysts and surfaces context that would otherwise require a specialist to retrieve.
crowdstrike-charlotte.engine: Frontier models grounded on CrowdStrike Falcon telemetry and threat intelligence.
crowdstrike-charlotte.latency: Interactive for queries. Continuous monitoring is background.

pricing.includes: Charlotte AI features across licensed Falcon modules

crowdstrike-charlotte.quality: Bounded by the quality and coverage of your Falcon deployment. Better data coverage produces better answers.
crowdstrike-charlotte.tagline: AI across the CrowdStrike Falcon platform, answering security questions in natural language.
use_cases: Asking natural language questions against the organization's security telemetry
Summarising incidents and threat context for analysts under pressure
Accelerating triage by surfacing relevant context without manual hunting
integrations: Deeply embedded in the Falcon platform
crowdstrike-charlotte.governance_note: Security AI tools create an audit question that general AI tools do not: if the AI missed something, was it because the telemetry was incomplete, the model missed it, or the analyst did not ask the right question? Documenting which AI-assisted decisions were made and what they were grounded on matters for incident response and for regulator inquiries in sectors with notification obligations. The AI layer is not a substitute for human judgment on significant incidents; it is a retrieval accelerator.
crowdstrike-charlotte.training_optout: CrowdStrike's terms govern customer data use. Grounding on your own telemetry is the architectural pattern; verify the data retention and training terms in the customer agreement.

linkedin-recruiter-ai.name: LinkedIn Recruiter AI
linkedin-recruiter-ai.value: Recruiter's AI turns plain language into searches, drafts outreach and, with Hiring Assistant, sources and screens candidates as an agent, over LinkedIn's member data. It is the largest candidate pool with AI on top.
linkedin-recruiter-ai.tagline: AI assisted search, messaging and the Hiring Assistant agent in LinkedIn Recruiter.
linkedin-recruiter-ai.governance_note: AI screening is an automated employment decision tool in several jurisdictions; keep humans on decisions and document it.
linkedin-recruiter-ai.training_optout: LinkedIn member settings govern training; recruiter data under enterprise terms.

microsoft-teams-recap.name: Microsoft Teams recap
microsoft-teams-recap.value: Intelligent recap produces notes, follow up tasks and a navigable timeline for recorded meetings, available with Teams Premium or Copilot, and in Teams for Education it gives absent students a summary of a recorded lesson. It overlaps with the Teams AI profile and is listed here for its education use.
microsoft-teams-recap.tagline: Intelligent recap in Teams: AI notes, tasks, speaker timeline and chapters after a meeting, used for class recordings too.
alternatives: Google Meet notes (Take notes for me)
microsoft-teams-recap.governance_note: Recording students requires notice under school policy and, in some states, consent.
microsoft-teams-recap.training_optout: Education data is not used for training.

cons: Per-seat annual pricing can be hard to size ahead of adoption
perplexity-enterprise.name: Perplexity Enterprise Pro
pros: Consumer product quality with enterprise data controls
Admin dashboard for inventory and governance
perplexity-enterprise.files: Web retrieval plus document uploads where supported.
perplexity-enterprise.value: Extends the Perplexity citing-answer model to enterprise requirements: SSO, admin controls, data retention controls, and prompts not used for training. The underlying product is the same, with the security envelope that regulated organizations need.
perplexity-enterprise.engine: Same as Perplexity AI: multi-model retrieval-augmented generation with citations.

pricing.includes: SSO, admin controls, data retention controls, no training opt-in

perplexity-enterprise.quality: Same quality characteristics as the consumer product. Citations require the same read-the-source discipline.
perplexity-enterprise.tagline: The enterprise tier of the citing answer engine, with data controls and SSO.
use_cases: Organization-wide research capability with audit and admin oversight
Replacing ad-hoc web research with a citable, policy-compliant tool
Embedding sourced answers in internal workflows via the API
perplexity-enterprise.governance_note: Same evidentiary point as the consumer product, now under admin control. The admin dashboard tells you which seats are active and what the usage looks like, which matters for the AI inventory. Citations are still leads, not evidence, and that rule does not change with the tier.
perplexity-enterprise.training_optout: Enterprise Pro explicitly excludes customer data from model training. Verify the current contract terms.

physical-intelligence.name: Physical Intelligence
physical-intelligence.value: Physical Intelligence trains general purpose robot policies, pi0 and successors, that take camera images and language instructions and output actions across different robot arms and mobile platforms, and has released weights and code openly. It is the leading independent lab for the GPT moment in robotics.
physical-intelligence.tagline: Robotics foundation model lab whose pi models control many robot types from one vision language action model.
physical-intelligence.governance_note: Physical AI raises safety questions no chatbot does; any deployment needs physical safeguards and testing outside the model.

cons: Only useful if already running SentinelOne
Autonomous response policy still requires explicit human design
Answer quality bounded by telemetry coverage
sentinelone-purple-ai.name: SentinelOne Purple AI
pros: Natural language over SentinelOne's own telemetry
Reduces investigation barrier for less expert analysts
Single platform, no data leaves the Singularity boundary
sentinelone-purple-ai.files: Endpoint, cloud, and identity telemetry within the Singularity platform.
sentinelone-purple-ai.value: AI threat hunting and incident response assistance across SentinelOne's endpoint, cloud, and identity data. Natural language queries return threat context grounded in your organization's telemetry, similar to CrowdStrike's Charlotte AI but on the SentinelOne platform.
sentinelone-purple-ai.engine: Frontier models grounded on SentinelOne Singularity telemetry.

pricing.includes: Purple AI features across licensed Singularity modules

sentinelone-purple-ai.quality: Bounded by Singularity platform coverage in the environment.
sentinelone-purple-ai.tagline: Natural language threat hunting and investigation across the SentinelOne Singularity platform.
use_cases: Natural language threat hunting across SentinelOne telemetry
Incident summary and investigation path suggestions for SOC analysts
Reducing the expertise barrier for threat investigation on the Singularity platform
integrations: Singularity endpoint, cloud, and identity modules
sentinelone-purple-ai.governance_note: Same AI-assisted SOC governance points as CrowdStrike Charlotte AI: document AI-assisted decisions and the evidence behind them. The specific SentinelOne governance question is autonomous response, which Singularity supports; ensure that policy is explicit about which autonomous actions are enabled and under what conditions, independent of the AI layer.
sentinelone-purple-ai.training_optout: SentinelOne's terms govern. Queries and telemetry stay within the platform.

servicenow-now-assist.name: ServiceNow Now Assist
servicenow-now-assist.value: Now Assist summarises incidents, drafts resolutions, generates code and runs AI agents that work tickets across ITSM, HR, customer service and security operations, priced as a Pro Plus tier. With Moveworks acquired, it is the front end for employee service too.
servicenow-now-assist.tagline: Generative AI and agents across ServiceNow's IT, HR, customer and security workflows.
servicenow-now-assist.governance_note: Agents with change and access rights need scoping; the platform's own AI governance module should register them.
servicenow-now-assist.training_optout: ServiceNow does not train on customer data.

azure-machine-learning.name: Azure Machine Learning
azure-machine-learning.value: Azure ML provides workspaces, compute, pipelines, model registry and responsible AI tooling for custom models, and Azure AI Foundry sits beside it for foundation models and agents. Enterprises on Microsoft use it for governed model development.
azure-machine-learning.engine: Not a model; platform for custom and catalogue models.
azure-machine-learning.tagline: Microsoft's ML platform for custom models, now sharing a foundation with Azure AI Foundry for generative work.
azure-machine-learning.governance_note: The responsible AI dashboard and model registry support audit evidence; make them required steps in the deployment process.
azure-machine-learning.training_optout: Microsoft does not use customer data to train its services.

computer-use-anthropic.api: Claude API with computer use beta tool.
cons: Irreversible actions require explicit human approval policy
Higher token cost due to vision
Less reliable on novel or visually complex interfaces
computer-use-anthropic.name: Computer Use (Anthropic)
pros: Enables automation of any GUI-based workflow
Same model quality as Claude across all tasks
No per-workflow programming for novel interfaces
computer-use-anthropic.files: Operates on whatever the screen contains. No direct file access independent of the applications it opens.
computer-use-anthropic.value: Anthropic's computer use capability allows Claude to operate a computer: clicking, typing, reading screens, and navigating interfaces. It is the underlying capability for agentic desktop automation rather than a finished product.
computer-use-anthropic.engine: Claude's models with tool use for mouse, keyboard, and screen-capture actions.
computer-use-anthropic.latency: Slower than API calls because each action requires a screen observation and decision.

pricing.model: Pay per token, higher than standard Claude due to vision tokens
pricing.includes: Computer use tool calls within the Claude API

computer-use-anthropic.quality: Capable for well-defined workflows. Less reliable on novel interfaces or tasks requiring complex visual inference.
computer-use-anthropic.tagline: The capability that lets Claude control a computer, not just answer questions about one.
use_cases: Automating multi-step workflows that require interacting with GUIs rather than APIs
Operating software that has no API or programmatic interface
Building agentic tools that require desktop interaction as a primitive
integrations: Containerized desktop environments for safer deployment
computer-use-anthropic.governance_note: An AI that can operate a computer is an AI that can take irreversible actions: send emails, execute trades, delete files, commit code, submit forms. The standard agentic governance requirements are at their most critical here. Minimum necessary permissions for the session, explicit human approval before any irreversible action, and a clear task scope are not optional design choices. The blast radius of a mistaken action on an unrestricted desktop is the entire desktop.
computer-use-anthropic.training_optout: Anthropic's commercial API terms apply. Screenshots are processed as images within the same terms.

google-live-transcribe.name: Google Live Transcribe
google-live-transcribe.value: Live Transcribe captions conversations on an Android phone in dozens of languages and flags sounds, built with Gallaudet University, free and part of Android accessibility. It is used in classrooms and meetings for live captioning.
google-live-transcribe.tagline: Android accessibility app that captions speech in real time for deaf and hard of hearing users.
alternatives: Microsoft PowerPoint and Teams live captions
google-live-transcribe.governance_note: Transcripts are not saved by default; recording others still needs consent.

google-slides-captions.name: Google Slides captions
google-slides-captions.value: Presenting in Slides with captions on shows the speaker's words on screen in real time, free in Chrome, which supports deaf students and language learners during lessons. It is a single feature rather than a product.
google-slides-captions.tagline: Live automatic captions during Google Slides presentations.
alternatives: Microsoft PowerPoint and Teams live captions

cons: Best value only for existing OneTrust customers
Less standalone capability than purpose-built AI governance tools
Module pricing adds to existing OneTrust cost
onetrust-ai-governance.name: OneTrust AI Governance
pros: Privacy and AI risk in one evidence store
onetrust-ai-governance.files: AI system records, risk assessments, and policy documentation.
onetrust-ai-governance.value: For organizations already running OneTrust for privacy, this adds AI inventory, risk assessments, and regulatory mapping as an extension of the same platform. Avoids a second governance data silo.
onetrust-ai-governance.engine: Governance platform. Not an AI model. Extends OneTrust's existing workflow engine.

pricing.model: Module licence on top of OneTrust
pricing.includes: AI inventory, risk workflows, regulatory mapping

onetrust-ai-governance.quality: Excellent integration with existing OneTrust privacy workflows. Less standalone depth than dedicated AI governance tools.
onetrust-ai-governance.tagline: AI governance as an extension of OneTrust's established privacy and risk platform.
use_cases: AI inventory and risk classification alongside existing privacy asset inventory
EU AI Act readiness assessment inside the platform already used for GDPR
Centralising AI and privacy risk evidence in one tool for audit
onetrust-ai-governance.governance_note: The practical case is consolidation: an organization already maintaining GDPR data asset inventories in OneTrust can attach AI system inventories to the same platform without a second tool, vendor, and evidence silo. The cross-over between AI risk and privacy risk is significant enough that this consolidation is often the right decision for the first year of an AI governance program.
onetrust-ai-governance.training_optout: Governance metadata platform. Not a model host.

palo-alto-precision-ai.api: Per-product APIs; XSIAM has its own integration surface.
cons: Value strictly within Palo Alto portfolio
Cross-product autonomous action policies require explicit governance
palo-alto-precision-ai.name: Palo Alto Networks Precision AI
pros: Deep integration across a commonly deployed enterprise security stack
Large threat intelligence base behind detection models
Broad coverage without additional tool sprawl
palo-alto-precision-ai.files: Network traffic, security events, and policy configuration.
palo-alto-precision-ai.value: AI capabilities integrated across the Palo Alto Networks portfolio: inline threat detection in firewalls, AI-powered analysis in XSIAM (the SOC platform), and AI-driven network security policy management. The value is the depth of integration across a large deployed base.
palo-alto-precision-ai.engine: Proprietary detection models plus frontier LLMs in XSIAM for investigation assistance.
palo-alto-precision-ai.latency: Real-time for detection. Interactive for investigation.

pricing.model: Within existing Palo Alto product licensing

palo-alto-precision-ai.quality: Strong detection across network and cloud, backed by a large threat intelligence feed. SOC assistance quality depends on XSIAM deployment.
palo-alto-precision-ai.tagline: AI woven through the Palo Alto Networks security product suite, not a standalone tool.
use_cases: AI-enhanced threat detection across Palo Alto's network security products
XSIAM AI-powered SOC automation and incident response
AI-assisted firewall rule and policy management
integrations: Palo Alto Networks product suite: NGFW, Prisma, XSIAM, Cortex
Third-party SIEM and SOAR via integrations
palo-alto-precision-ai.governance_note: Security AI governance across a multi-product portfolio like Palo Alto's requires consistency: the autonomous action policies that govern Cortex XDR responses, NGFW inline actions, and XSIAM playbooks need to be reviewed as a set, not managed product by product. The AI overlay across many products means AI decisions may interact across the stack in ways that are not visible from any single product's dashboard.
